phrases.japanese: こんにちは
phrases.notes: Safe all-purpose greeting during the day. Morning: おはようございます (Ohayou gozaimasu). Evening: こんばんは (Konbanwa).

responses.japanese: こんにちは！いらっしゃいませ！
responses.english: Hello! Welcome!
responses.listen_for: いらっしゃいませ (Irasshaimase) is the standard shop/restaurant welcome chant. No response needed — just nod and smile.

responses.japanese: こんにちは、なにかおさがしですか？
responses.english: Hello, are you looking for something?
responses.listen_for: おさがし (お探し, osagashi) = looking for. Follow up with みているだけです (見ているだけです) if you're browsing.
responses.kanji: こんにちは、何かお探しですか？

phrases.japanese: ありがとうございます
phrases.notes: Use this constantly. Casual: ありがとう (Arigatou). You'll hear どういたしまして (Dou itashimashite) = you're welcome.

responses.japanese: どういたしまして
responses.english: You're welcome
responses.listen_for: The formal response. Less common than you'd expect — Japanese often just smile or nod.

responses.japanese: いえ、どうぞ
responses.english: Not at all, please (go ahead)
responses.listen_for: A softer 'you're welcome'. どうぞ on its own means 'please go ahead / here you go'.

phrases.japanese: すみません
phrases.notes: Most useful word in Japan. Gets attention, apologizes lightly, lets you squeeze past someone.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead / Yes, what is it?
responses.listen_for: Staff responding to your attention-grab. They're ready to help — go ahead with your question.

responses.japanese: はい、なんでしょうか？
responses.english: Yes, what can I do for you?
responses.listen_for: Polite 'what do you need?' — follow with your question.
responses.kanji: はい、何でしょうか？

phrases.japanese: はい
phrases.notes: Also used to acknowledge listening. Very frequent.

responses.japanese: はい、はい
responses.english: Yes, yes (I understand)
responses.listen_for: Repeated はい means 'I'm listening / I got it'. Very common in conversation.

phrases.japanese: いえ
phrases.notes: だいじょうぶです (大丈夫です, Daijoubu desu) is a softer way to decline.

responses.japanese: そうですか
responses.english: Is that so / I see
responses.listen_for: Neutral acknowledgment. Not agreement or disagreement — just 'noted'.

phrases.japanese: わかりました
phrases.notes: Use after someone explains something. わかりません (わかりません (分かりません), Wakarimasen) = I don't understand.

responses.japanese: よかったです！
responses.english: Great! / I'm glad!
responses.listen_for: Relief expression — they're happy you understood.
responses.kanji: 良かったです！

phrases.kanji: 分かりました

phrases.japanese: わかりません
phrases.notes: Say this confidently rather than nodding along confused.

responses.japanese: えいごでいいましょうか？
responses.english: Shall I say it in English?
responses.listen_for: They're offering to switch to English. Say はい if you want that.
responses.kanji: 英語で言いましょうか？

responses.japanese: もういちどいいますね
responses.english: I'll say it one more time
responses.listen_for: They're going to repeat. Get ready to listen again.
responses.kanji: もう一度言いますね

phrases.kanji: 分かりません

phrases.japanese: もういちど、ゆっくりおねがいします
phrases.notes: Absolute lifesaver. Most people will happily comply.

responses.japanese: はい、ゆっくりいいますね
responses.english: Yes, I'll say it slowly
responses.listen_for: They'll slow right down. Focus on the key words — nouns and numbers.
responses.kanji: はい、ゆっくり言いますね

phrases.kanji: もう一度、ゆっくりお願いします

phrases.japanese: にほんごがあまりじょうずじゃないです
phrases.romaji: Nihongo ga amari jouzu ja nai desu
phrases.notes: Sets expectations well. People appreciate the honesty and effort.

responses.japanese: いえいえ、じょうずですよ！
responses.english: No no, you're good at it!
responses.listen_for: Japanese people will almost always say this even if your Japanese is minimal. It's encouragement, not assessment. Smile and say ありがとうございます.
responses.kanji: いえいえ、上手ですよ！

phrases.kanji: 日本語があまり上手じゃないです

phrases.japanese: えいごははなせますか？
phrases.notes: Ask before assuming. Common in tourist areas.

responses.japanese: すこしだけはなせます
responses.english: I can speak a little
responses.listen_for: すこし (少し, sukoshi) = a little. They'll try. Meet them halfway.
responses.kanji: 少しだけ話せます

responses.japanese: すみません、えいごはあまり…
responses.english: Sorry, my English is not great…
responses.listen_for: Trailing off with あまり means 'not much'. Switch to simple Japanese and gestures.
responses.kanji: すみません、英語はあまり…

responses.japanese: はい、すこしはなせます。どうぞ！
responses.english: Yes, I can speak a little. Go ahead!
responses.listen_for: Green light — they're willing to try English.
responses.kanji: はい、少し話せます。どうぞ！

phrases.kanji: 英語は話せますか？

phrases.japanese: よろしくおねがいします
phrases.english: Nice to meet you / Please take care of me
phrases.notes: Said when meeting someone, starting a transaction, or asking a favor.

responses.japanese: こちらこそ、よろしくおねがいします
responses.english: Likewise, pleased to meet you too
responses.listen_for: こちらこそ = 'the same to you / likewise'. The standard warm reply.
responses.kanji: こちらこそ、よろしくお願いします

phrases.kanji: よろしくお願いします

phrases.japanese: これはいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Point at the item. Listen for a number.

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.english: [price] yen
responses.listen_for: Just the number + えん (円, en). E.g., 1500えん = 1500 yen. If you don't catch it, ask: もういちどおねがいします (もう一度お願いします).
responses.kanji: 〜円です

responses.japanese: ぜいこみで〜えんになります
responses.english: Including tax, it's [price] yen
responses.listen_for: ぜいこみ (税込, zeikomi) = tax included. The final price.
responses.kanji: 税込で〜円になります

phrases.japanese: みているだけです
phrases.notes: Response to shop staff when browsing.

responses.japanese: ごゆっくりどうぞ
responses.english: Please take your time
responses.listen_for: ゆっくり = slowly/at your pace. They're giving you space — no pressure.

responses.japanese: なにかありましたらおこえがけください
responses.english: Please let us know if you need anything
responses.listen_for: Long phrase, but just means 'call us if you need help'. Nod and browse.
responses.kanji: 何かありましたらお声がけください

phrases.kanji: 見ているだけです

phrases.japanese: これをください
phrases.notes: Point at item + say this. Works anywhere.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます。〜えんになります
responses.english: Thank you. That will be [price] yen.
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before えん (円). They'll often show you on a calculator or the register screen.
responses.kanji: ありがとうございます。〜円になります

responses.japanese: ふくろはごいりようですか？
responses.english: Do you need a bag?
responses.listen_for: ふくろ (袋, fukuro) = bag. Answer はい or いいえ.
responses.kanji: 袋はご入り用ですか？

phrases.japanese: ほかのいろはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hoka no iro wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace いろ (色, iro) / color with サイズ (saizu / size) if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらにございます
responses.english: Yes, they're over here
responses.listen_for: こちら (kochira) = this way / over here. Follow them.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、このいろだけです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kono iro dake desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, we only have this color
responses.listen_for: もうしわけありません (申し訳ありません) = formal apology. だけ = only. They don't have other colors.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、この色だけです

phrases.kanji: 他の色はありますか？

phrases.japanese: おおきいサイズはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a larger size?
phrases.notes: おおきい (大きい, ookii) = larger. ちいさい (小さい, chiisai) = smaller. Japanese sizing runs small.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.english: Please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: しょうしょう (少々) = a brief moment. They're going to check the back. Stay put.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: ざいこをかくにんいたします
responses.english: I'll check our stock
responses.listen_for: ざいこ (在庫, zaiko) = stock/inventory. They're checking for you.
responses.kanji: 在庫を確認いたします

phrases.kanji: 大きいサイズはありますか？

phrases.japanese: しちゃくできますか？
phrases.notes: For clothing stores.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらへどうぞ
responses.english: Yes, right this way
responses.listen_for: They'll lead you to the fitting room. Follow them.

responses.japanese: フィッティングルームがあちらです
responses.english: The fitting room is over there
responses.listen_for: あちら (achira) = over there. They'll gesture the direction.

phrases.kanji: 試着できますか？

phrases.japanese: カードではらえますか？
phrases.notes: Japan is still cash-heavy. Always check.

responses.japanese: はい、クレジットカードはごりよういただけます
responses.romaji: Hai, kurejitto kaado wa go-riyou itadakemasu
responses.english: Yes, credit cards are accepted
responses.listen_for: クレジットカード = credit card. りよう (利用) = use/utilize. Green light.
responses.kanji: はい、クレジットカードはご利用いただけます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、げんきんのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, genkin nomi desu
responses.english: Sorry, cash only
responses.listen_for: げんきん (現金, genkin) = cash. のみ = only. Find an ATM — 7-Eleven ATMs always work with foreign cards.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、現金のみです

responses.japanese: Suicaはごりよういただけます
responses.english: Suica card is accepted
responses.listen_for: Many shops now accept IC cards like Suica as payment.
responses.kanji: Suicaはご利用いただけます

phrases.kanji: カードで払えますか？

phrases.japanese: ふくろはいりません
phrases.notes: You'll be asked at konbini frequently.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Understood (formal)
responses.listen_for: Very formal acknowledgment. Common in service contexts. Same as わかりました (分かりました) but more polished.

phrases.kanji: 袋はいりません

phrases.japanese: めんぜいはできますか？
phrases.notes: Need passport. Purchase over ¥5,000.

responses.japanese: パスポートをおもちですか？
responses.english: Do you have your passport?
responses.listen_for: パスポート = passport. おもち (お持ち) = do you have. Always carry your passport in Japan.
responses.kanji: パスポートをお持ちですか？

responses.japanese: こちらのようしにごきにゅうください
responses.romaji: Kochira no youshi ni go-kinyuu kudasai
responses.english: Please fill out this form
responses.listen_for: ようし (用紙, youshi) = form/paper. きにゅう (記入, kinyuu) = fill in. They'll hand you a tax exemption form.
responses.kanji: こちらの用紙にご記入ください

phrases.kanji: 免税はできますか？

phrases.japanese: これはなんですか？
phrases.notes: Point at unfamiliar items.

responses.japanese: これは〜です
responses.english: This is [name of item]
responses.listen_for: They'll name it. You might not know the word — that's fine. Smile and nod, or show interest with へえ！ (Hee! = Oh really!)

phrases.kanji: これは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: りょうしゅうしょをください
phrases.notes: For expense tracking or returns.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらがレシートです
responses.english: Here is your receipt
responses.listen_for: レシート (reshiito) = receipt (casual). りょうしゅうしょ (領収書, ryoushuusho) = formal receipt. They may ask: あてなはどうしますか？ (宛名はどうしますか？, Atena wa dou shimasu ka?) = What name for the receipt?

phrases.kanji: 領収書をください

phrases.japanese: わりびきはありますか？
phrases.notes: Haggling isn't common in Japan outside flea markets, but asking about an existing sale or discount is completely normal.

responses.japanese: はい、げんざいセールちゅうです
responses.english: Yes, it's currently on sale
responses.listen_for: セールちゅう (セール中, seeru-chuu) = currently on sale.
responses.kanji: はい、現在セール中です

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、わりびきはいたしかねます
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, waribiki wa itashikanemasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, we're unable to offer a discount
responses.listen_for: いたしかねます (itashikanemasu) = a very polite way to say 'we cannot do that'.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、割引はいたしかねます

phrases.kanji: 割引はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ポイントカードはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a point/loyalty card?
phrases.notes: Many shops have a stamp or point card system for repeat customers — ask if you'll be visiting again.

responses.japanese: はい、むりょうでつくれます
responses.english: Yes, you can make one for free
responses.listen_for: むりょう (無料, muryou) = free of charge.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、とうてんにはございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, touten ni wa gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, this store doesn't have one
responses.listen_for: とうてん (当店, touten) = this store (formal, staff self-reference).
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、当店にはございません

phrases.japanese: へんぴんしたいです
phrases.notes: A receipt is almost always required for returns in Japan — keep it until you leave the store.

responses.japanese: レシートはおもちですか？
responses.english: Do you have the receipt?
responses.listen_for: おもち (お持ち, omochi) = do you have. No receipt usually means no return.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、へんぴんはおうけできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, henpin wa o-uke dekimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we cannot accept returns
responses.listen_for: おうけできません (お受けできません, o-uke dekimasen) = cannot accept. Try asking for こうかん (交換, koukan) / exchange instead.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、返品はお受けできません

phrases.kanji: 返品したいです

phrases.japanese: こうかんできますか？
phrases.notes: Useful for the wrong size or color — the item usually needs to be unused with tags attached.

responses.japanese: はい、どのサイズにごこうかんですか？
responses.romaji: Hai, dono saizu ni go-koukan desu ka?
responses.english: Yes, which size would you like to exchange it for?
responses.listen_for: ごこうかん (ご交換, go-koukan) = polite 'exchange'. Name the size you want.
responses.kanji: はい、どのサイズにご交換ですか？

responses.japanese: みしようのものであればこうかんかのうです
responses.romaji: Mishiyou no mono de areba koukan kanou desu
responses.english: If it's unused, exchange is possible
responses.listen_for: みしよう (未使用, mishiyou) = unused. かのう (可能, kanou) = possible.
responses.kanji: 未使用のものであれば交換可能です

phrases.kanji: 交換できますか？

phrases.japanese: ほしょうしょはついていますか？
phrases.english: Does this come with a warranty?
phrases.notes: ほしょうしょ (保証書, hoshousho) = warranty card/certificate, important for electronics purchases.

responses.japanese: はい、いちねんほしょうがついています
responses.romaji: Hai, ichinen hoshou ga tsuite imasu
responses.english: Yes, it comes with a one-year warranty
responses.listen_for: いちねんほしょう (1年保証, ichinen hoshou) = one-year warranty.
responses.kanji: はい、1年保証が付いています

responses.japanese: ほしょうしょはこのなかにはいっています
responses.romaji: Hoshousho wa kono naka ni haitte imasu
responses.english: The warranty card is inside this
responses.listen_for: はいっています (入っています, haitte imasu) = is inside. Keep the box until you've checked.
responses.kanji: 保証書はこの中に入っています

phrases.kanji: 保証書はついていますか？

phrases.japanese: なんじまであいていますか？
phrases.english: What time are you open until?
phrases.notes: Useful for department stores and small shops, since hours vary a lot by location.

responses.japanese: よるのくじまであいています
responses.romaji: Yoru no kuji made aite imasu
responses.english: We're open until 9pm
responses.listen_for: よる (夜, yoru) = evening/night. じ (時, ji) = o'clock — listen for the number before it.
responses.kanji: 夜の9時まで開いています

responses.japanese: ほんじつはもうすぐへいてんです
responses.romaji: Honjitsu wa mou sugu heiten desu
responses.english: We're about to close for today
responses.listen_for: へいてん (閉店, heiten) = closing time. Time to wrap up your shopping.
responses.kanji: 本日はもうすぐ閉店です

phrases.kanji: 何時まで開いていますか？

phrases.japanese: ためしにつかってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Tameshi ni tsukatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: For electronics, cameras, or demo units on display.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞおためしください
responses.english: Yes, please go ahead and try it
responses.listen_for: おためし (お試し, otameshi) = trying out. Green light to test the product.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、こちらはてんじひんのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kochira wa tenjihin nomi desu
responses.english: Sorry, this is display only
responses.listen_for: てんじひん (展示品, tenjihin) = display item. のみ = only — it can't be powered on or tested.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、こちらは展示品のみです

phrases.kanji: 試しに使ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: とりおきしてもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you hold this item for me?
phrases.notes: とりおき (取り置き, torioki) = holding an item, often for same-day pickup after you've finished browsing elsewhere.

responses.japanese: はい、なんじまでおとりおきしましょうか？
responses.romaji: Hai, nanji made otorioki shimashou ka?
responses.english: Sure, until what time shall I hold it?
responses.listen_for: なんじまで (何時まで, nanji made) = until what time. Give a pickup time.
responses.kanji: はい、何時までお取り置きしましょうか？

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、とりおきはおこなっておりません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, torioki wa okonatte orimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we don't offer item holding
responses.listen_for: おこなっておりません (行っておりません, okonatte orimasen) = we don't carry out/offer that.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、取り置きは行っておりません

phrases.kanji: 取り置きしてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: かいがいはっそうはできますか？
phrases.notes: Big department stores often handle this; small shops usually can't.

responses.japanese: はい、ゆうそうりょうはべつとなります
responses.romaji: Hai, yuusouryou wa betsu to narimasu
responses.english: Yes, shipping cost is separate
responses.listen_for: ゆうそうりょう (郵送料, yuusouryou) = postage/shipping fee. べつ (別, betsu) = separate.
responses.kanji: はい、郵送料は別となります

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、かいがいはっそうはおこなっておりません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kaigai hassou wa okonatte orimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we don't ship overseas
responses.listen_for: かいがいはっそう (海外発送, kaigai hassou) = overseas shipping.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、海外発送は行っておりません

phrases.kanji: 海外発送はできますか？

phrases.japanese: プレゼントようにつつんでもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Purezento you ni tsutsunde moraemasu ka?
phrases.notes: Gift-wrapping is common and often free at department stores, though some shops charge a small fee.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、しょうしょうおまちください
responses.english: Certainly, please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: しょうしょう (少々, shoushou) = a brief moment.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: らっぴんはゆうりょうになります
responses.english: Gift-wrapping has a fee
responses.listen_for: らっぴん (ラッピング, rappingu) = gift-wrapping. ゆうりょう (有料, yuuryou) = paid/fee-based.
responses.kanji: ラッピングは有料になります

phrases.kanji: プレゼント用に包んでもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ほかのサイズはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hoka no saizu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Situation: your size is out of stock or sold out on the shelf. 在庫 (zaiko) = stock.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありません、そのサイズは在庫がございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, sono saizu wa zaiko ga gozaimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we don't have that size in stock
responses.listen_for: 在庫 (zaiko) = stock. ございません = polite 'there isn't'.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、そのサイズは在庫がございません

responses.japanese: えむサイズでしたら、ございます
responses.english: If you want M size, we have it
responses.listen_for: でしたら = in that case / if that works. Usually followed by an alternative.
responses.kanji: Mサイズでしたら、ございます

phrases.japanese: とりよせはできますか？
phrases.english: Can you order it in for me?
phrases.notes: Situation: the item you want isn't on the shelf. 取り寄せ (toriyose) = special order from another store or the supplier.

responses.japanese: はい、三日ほどでお届けできますよ
responses.romaji: Hai, mikka hodo de otodoke dekimasu yo
responses.english: Yes, we can deliver it in about three days
responses.listen_for: お届け (otodoke) = delivery. ほど = about.
responses.kanji: はい、三日ほどでお届けできますよ

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありませんが、取り寄せはしておりません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, toriyose wa shite orimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we don't do special orders
responses.listen_for: しておりません = polite 'we don't do'. Ask at another store if this happens.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、取り寄せはしておりません

phrases.japanese: 値札と、レジの金額がちがいます
phrases.romaji: Nefuda to, reji no kingaku ga chigaimasu
phrases.english: The price tag and the register amount are different
phrases.notes: Situation: the price at the register doesn't match the tag on the item. 値札 (nefuda) = price tag.

responses.japanese: 失礼いたしました。確認いたしますので、少々お待ちください
responses.romaji: Shitsurei itashimashita. Kakunin itashimasu node, shoushou omachi kudasai
responses.english: Sorry. I'll check, so please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: 少々 (しょうしょう) = a little / a moment.
responses.kanji: 失礼いたしました。確認いたしますので、少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: 大変申し訳ありません。表示の金額でお会計いたします
responses.romaji: Taihen moushiwake arimasen. Hyouji no kingaku de okaikei itashimasu
responses.english: I'm very sorry. We'll charge the price shown
responses.listen_for: 表示 (hyouji) = what's displayed. お会計 = checkout / payment.
responses.kanji: 大変申し訳ありません。表示の金額でお会計いたします

phrases.japanese: ひとりです
phrases.notes: Hold up fingers too. They'll ask にんずうはおひとりさまですか？ (人数はお一人様ですか？, Ninzuu wa o-hitorisama desu ka?)

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.english: Please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: They're finding you a table. Wait by the entrance.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: こちらへどうぞ
responses.english: Right this way
responses.listen_for: Follow them — they're seating you now.

responses.japanese: ただいままんせきでございます
responses.english: We are currently full
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full/no seats. You may need to wait or come back.
responses.kanji: ただいま満席でございます

phrases.kanji: 1人です

phrases.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
phrases.english: How many people? (what staff will ask you)
phrases.notes: This is the question you'll hear at almost every restaurant entrance. Staff say なんめいさま (何名様, nanmei-sama) — the polite form. Your answers: 1ひとり (人, hitori), 2ふたり (人, futari), 3さんにん (人, san-nin). Always hold up fingers at the same time.

responses.japanese: おひとりさまですか？
responses.english: Just one person?
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for solo diners. Answer はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お一人様ですか？

responses.japanese: おふたりさまですね
responses.english: Two people, right?
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for two. はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お二人様ですね

responses.japanese: おさんにんさまですね
responses.english: Three people, right?
responses.listen_for: Polite confirmation for three. はい to confirm.
responses.kanji: お三人様ですね

phrases.kanji: 何名様ですか？

phrases.japanese: きんえんせきをおねがいします
phrases.notes: きねん (禁煙, kinen) = no smoking. きつえんせき (喫煙席, kitsuen-seki) = smoking section. Many restaurants in Japan still have both. Request this when being seated.

responses.japanese: きんえんせきにごあんないいたします
responses.english: I'll show you to a non-smoking seat
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内) = guide/lead. Follow them.
responses.kanji: 禁煙席にご案内いたします

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、きんえんせきがまんせきです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kinen-seki ga manseki desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, non-smoking is full
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full. You may need to wait or accept a smoking seat.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、禁煙席が満席です

phrases.kanji: 禁煙席をお願いします

phrases.japanese: カウンターせきでもいいですか？
phrases.notes: Staff may offer a counter seat (bar-style, solo or two people facing the kitchen) if tables are full. Solo diners are often seated here. You may hear this as a question — answer はい to accept or テーブルがいいです to request a table.

responses.japanese: カウンターせきでよろしければごあんないできます
responses.english: We can seat you at the counter if that's okay
responses.listen_for: よろしければ = if that's fine. Say はい、おねがいします (お願いします) to accept.
responses.kanji: カウンター席でよろしければご案内できます

phrases.kanji: カウンター席でもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: メニューをください
phrases.notes: Many places have picture menus.

responses.japanese: こちらがメニューになります
responses.english: Here is the menu
responses.listen_for: They'll hand it to you. English menus are common in tourist areas — you can ask: えいごのメニューはありますか？ (英語のメニューはありますか？, Eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka?)

phrases.japanese: これをひとつください
phrases.notes: Point at menu item. ひとつ (一つ, hitotsu) = one. ふたつ (二つ, futatsu) = two.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received. They may follow with questions about spice, toppings, or cooking preference.

responses.japanese: からさはどうしますか？
responses.english: How spicy would you like it?
responses.listen_for: からさ (辛さ, karasa) = level of spice. Common at curry and ramen shops. Options usually: ふつう (普通, futsuu) / normal, からめ (辛め, karame) / spicier, からくなし (辛くなし, karaku nashi) / no spice.
responses.kanji: 辛さはどうしますか？

phrases.kanji: これを一つください

phrases.japanese: おすすめはなんですか？
phrases.notes: Staff love this question.

responses.japanese: 〜がとてもにんきです
responses.english: [dish] is very popular
responses.listen_for: にんき (人気, ninki) = popular. Remember the dish name they say and point at it on the menu.
responses.kanji: 〜がとても人気です

responses.japanese: きょうのおすすめは〜です
responses.english: Today's recommendation is [dish]
responses.listen_for: きょう (今日, kyou) = today. They're giving you their daily special.
responses.kanji: 今日のおすすめは〜です

phrases.kanji: おすすめは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: おかいけいをおねがいします
phrases.notes: In Japan you usually pay at the register, not at the table.

responses.japanese: 〜えんでございます
responses.english: That will be [amount] yen
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number. They'll often show the total on the register facing you.
responses.kanji: 〜円でございます

responses.japanese: レジでおしはらいください
responses.english: Please pay at the register
responses.listen_for: レジ = register/cashier. Head to the front to pay.
responses.kanji: レジでお支払いください

phrases.kanji: お会計をお願いします

phrases.japanese: べつべつにはらえますか？
phrases.notes: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separately. Very useful for groups. Some restaurants may not support split bills — they may ask you to calculate and hand over separate cash instead.

responses.japanese: はい、しょうちしました
responses.english: Yes, understood
responses.listen_for: They'll split it at the register.
responses.kanji: はい、承知しました

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、べつべつにはできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, betsubetsu ni wa dekimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we can't split the bill
responses.listen_for: できません = cannot. You'll need to settle among yourselves and pay together.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、別々にはできません

phrases.kanji: 別々に払えますか？

phrases.japanese: おいしい！
phrases.notes: Say this to any chef or cook.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます！
responses.english: Thank you!
responses.listen_for: Pure joy. This is one of the best things you can say in Japan.

responses.japanese: よかったです！またきてください
responses.english: I'm glad! Please come again
responses.listen_for: またまたきて (来て, mata kite) = come again. High praise — they want you back.
responses.kanji: 良かったです！また来てください

phrases.kanji: 美味しい！

phrases.japanese: たまごアレルギーがあります
phrases.notes: Swap allergen as needed.

responses.japanese: かくにんしてまいります
responses.english: I'll go check
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check. They're checking with the kitchen. Good sign.
responses.kanji: 確認してまいります

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、〜がふくまれています
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, [allergen] ga fukumarete imasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, it contains [allergen]
responses.listen_for: ふくまれています (含まれています, fukumarete imasu) = is contained/included. The dish has the allergen — avoid it.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、〜が含まれています

phrases.kanji: 卵アレルギーがあります

phrases.japanese: からくしないでください
phrases.notes: Useful at ramen and curry shops.

responses.japanese: はい、かしこまりました
responses.english: Yes, understood
responses.listen_for: They got it. Your food will be mild.

phrases.kanji: 辛くしないでください

phrases.japanese: おみずをください
phrases.notes: Free in most restaurants.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにおもちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring it right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ (sugu) = right away/immediately. Water is coming.
responses.kanji: はい、すぐにお持ちします

phrases.kanji: お水をください

phrases.japanese: おみずを〇つおねがいします
phrases.notes: Ordering water for your group all at once. Hold up fingers to match the number.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにおもちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring them right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away. All glasses coming.
responses.kanji: はい、すぐにお持ちします

phrases.kanji: お水を〇つお願いします

phrases.japanese: もちかえりでおねがいします
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask: おあたためますか？ (温めますか？) (O-atatatemasu ka?)

responses.japanese: あたためますか？
responses.english: Shall I heat this up?
responses.listen_for: Very common at konbini for hot food. はい、おねがいします (お願いします, hai, onegaishimasu) = yes please, だいじょうぶです (大丈夫です, daijoubu desu) = no thank you.
responses.kanji: 温めますか？

responses.japanese: おはしはおつけしますか？
responses.english: Would you like chopsticks?
responses.listen_for: おはし (お箸, ohashi) = chopsticks. They may also offer a fork (フォーク/fooku) or spoon (スプーン/supuun).
responses.kanji: お箸はお付けしますか？

phrases.kanji: 持ち帰りでお願いします

phrases.japanese: てんないでたべます
phrases.notes: Konbini staff will ask this.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、イートインコーナーがあちらです
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, iito in koonaa ga achira desu
responses.english: Understood, the eat-in corner is over there
responses.listen_for: イートイン (iito in) = eat-in area. あちら = over there. They'll gesture.

phrases.kanji: 店内で食べます

phrases.japanese: ラーメンはなんじかんまちますか？
phrases.romaji: Raamen wa nan jikan machimasu ka?
phrases.english: How long is the wait for ramen?
phrases.notes: Listen for みぬてs (分, minutes) or ほうrs (時間, hours).

responses.japanese: だいたい〜ふんほどおまちいただきます
responses.english: You'll wait approximately [X] minutes
responses.listen_for: だいたい (大体) = approximately. ふん (分) = minutes. They may hand you a ticket or buzzer.
responses.kanji: 大体〜分ほどお待ちいただきます

responses.japanese: せいりけんをどうぞ
responses.english: Here is your queue ticket
responses.listen_for: せいりいけん (整理券, seiriiken) = numbered ticket. Hold on to it — your number will be called.
responses.kanji: 整理券をどうぞ

phrases.kanji: ラーメンは何時間待ちますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりです
phrases.notes: ふたり (二人, futari) is irregular — not ni-nin. From three people onward the pattern becomes regular: さんにん (三人, san-nin), よにん (四人, yo-nin).

responses.japanese: こちらへどうぞ
responses.english: Right this way
responses.listen_for: Same seating phrase as for one person — follow them to your table.

responses.japanese: きんえんせきときつえんせきどちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kin'en-seki to kitsuen-seki dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Smoking or non-smoking seat?
responses.listen_for: Rare now but some izakaya still ask. きねん (禁煙, kin'en) = non-smoking, きつえん (喫煙, kitsuen) = smoking.
responses.kanji: 禁煙席と喫煙席どちらがよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 二人です

phrases.japanese: さんにんです
phrases.notes: さんにん (三人, san-nin) is the regular counter pattern used from 3 people onward (四人 yo-nin, 五人 go-nin, etc.).

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.english: Please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: Larger tables may take longer to free up.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

responses.japanese: カウンターせきでもよろしいですか？
responses.english: Is a counter seat okay?
responses.listen_for: Some restaurants seat groups of 3 at the counter if tables are full.
responses.kanji: カウンター席でもよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 三人です

phrases.japanese: ふたつください
phrases.notes: ふたつ (二つ, futatsu) = two, the generic item counter. Point at the menu.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received.

phrases.kanji: 二つください

phrases.japanese: みっつください
phrases.notes: みっつ (三つ, mittsu) = three. The generic counter (一つ, 二つ, 三つ, 四つ, 五つ...) is irregular up through とお (十, too) = ten.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received.

phrases.kanji: 三つください

phrases.japanese: べつべつにかいけいできますか？
phrases.notes: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separately. Some smaller shops in Japan don't allow split bills — ask before ordering if it matters.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、べつべつのおかいけいはできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, betsubetsu no okaikei wa dekimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we can't split the bill
responses.listen_for: べつべつ (別々, betsubetsu) = separate. You may need one person to pay and split later.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、別々のお会計はできません

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、ではべつべつにごよういします
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, dewa betsubetsu ni goyoui shimasu
responses.english: Certainly, I'll prepare separate bills
responses.listen_for: Confirms they'll split the check for your group.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、では別々にご用意します

phrases.kanji: 別々に会計できますか？

phrases.japanese: いっしょにおねがいします
phrases.notes: Say this when asked べつべつですか、ごいっしょですか？ (別々ですか、ご一緒ですか？, Betsubetsu desu ka, go-issho desu ka?) — Separate or together?

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: One combined bill coming up.

phrases.kanji: 一緒にお願いします

phrases.japanese: てんないはきんえんですか？
phrases.notes: Since April 2020 most restaurants in Japan are non-smoking indoors by law, but some izakaya/bars are exempt — always worth confirming.

responses.japanese: はい、てんないはぜんせききんえんです
responses.romaji: Hai, tennai wa zenseki kin'en desu
responses.english: Yes, all seats inside are non-smoking
responses.listen_for: ぜんせき (全席, zenseki) = all seats. きんえん (禁煙, kin'en) = no smoking.
responses.kanji: はい、店内は全席禁煙です

responses.japanese: きつえんせきもございます
responses.english: We also have a smoking section
responses.listen_for: きつえんせき (喫煙席, kitsuen-seki) = smoking seat/section.
responses.kanji: 喫煙席もございます

phrases.kanji: 店内は禁煙ですか？

phrases.japanese: そとにきつえんじょはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Soto ni kitsuenjo wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a smoking area outside?
phrases.notes: きつえんじょ (喫煙所, kitsuenjo) = designated smoking area, common outside stations and convenience stores.

responses.japanese: はい、てんのそとにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, ten no soto ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, it's just outside the shop
responses.listen_for: そと (外, soto) = outside.

responses.japanese: ちかくのえきにきつえんじょがあります
responses.romaji: Chikaku no eki ni kitsuenjo ga arimasu
responses.english: There's a smoking area at the nearby station
responses.listen_for: ちかく (近く, chikaku) = nearby. You may need to walk a bit.
responses.kanji: 近くの駅に喫煙所があります

phrases.kanji: 外に喫煙所はありますか？

phrases.japanese: そとでたばこをすってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Soto de tabako wo sutte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: Many areas (e.g. central Tokyo wards) ban street smoking entirely — always use a designated きつえんじょ (喫煙所, kitsuenjo).

responses.japanese: すみません、このあたりはろじょうきつえんきんしです
responses.romaji: Sumimasen, kono atari wa rojou kitsuen kinshi desu
responses.english: Sorry, street smoking is banned around here
responses.listen_for: ろじょうきつえんきんし (路上喫煙禁止, rojou kitsuen kinshi) = street smoking prohibited.
responses.kanji: すみません、この辺りは路上喫煙禁止です

responses.japanese: はい、そちらのはいざらのところでどうぞ
responses.romaji: Hai, sochira no haizara no tokoro de douzo
responses.english: Yes, please go ahead over by that ashtray
responses.listen_for: はいざら (灰皿, haizara) = ashtray, marks a legal smoking spot.
responses.kanji: はい、そちらの灰皿の所でどうぞ

phrases.kanji: 外でタバコを吸ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: きつえんせきをおねがいします
phrases.notes: The counterpart to きんえんせき (禁煙席, kin'en-seki) requested in rs-01c — fewer restaurants offer this now.

responses.japanese: きつえんせきにごあんないいたします
responses.english: I'll show you to a smoking seat
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内, goannai) = guide/lead. Follow them.
responses.kanji: 喫煙席にご案内いたします

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、とうてんはぜんせききんえんです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, touten wa zenseki kin'en desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, our restaurant is entirely non-smoking
responses.listen_for: とうてん (当店, touten) = this restaurant (formal, staff self-reference).
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、当店は全席禁煙です

phrases.kanji: 喫煙席をお願いします

phrases.japanese: コースをおねがいします
phrases.notes: コース (koosu) = multi-dish set course, as opposed to アラカルト (arakaruto) / a la carte ordering of individual dishes.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、おのみものはいかがしますか？
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, onomimono wa ikaga shimasu ka?
responses.english: Certainly, what would you like to drink?
responses.listen_for: おのみもの (お飲み物, onomimono) = drinks.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、お飲み物はいかがしますか？

responses.japanese: コースはぜんぶでななひんです
responses.romaji: Koosu wa zenbu de nanahin desu
responses.english: The course has seven dishes in total
responses.listen_for: ぜんぶで (全部で, zenbu de) = in total.
responses.kanji: コースは全部で7品です

phrases.kanji: コースをお願いします

phrases.japanese: ごはんはおおもりでおねがいします
phrases.notes: おおもり (大盛り, oomori) = large portion, ふつう (普通, futsuu) = regular, すくなめ (少なめ, sukuname) = small — common at teishoku and donburi shops.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、おおもりですね
responses.english: Certainly, large it is
responses.listen_for: Order confirmed as-is.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、大盛りですね

responses.japanese: おおもりはプラス〜えんです
responses.english: Large portion is an extra [X] yen
responses.listen_for: プラス (purasu) = plus/additional. Listen for the number before えん (円).
responses.kanji: 大盛りはプラス〜円です

phrases.kanji: ご飯は大盛りでお願いします

phrases.japanese: ミディアムでおねがいします
phrases.notes: Steak doneness: レア (rare), ミディアム (medium), ウェルダン (well-done). Staff will ask やきかげんはどうなさいますか？ (焼き加減はどうなさいますか？, Yakikagen wa dou nasaimasu ka?) = How would you like it cooked?

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、ミディアムですね
responses.english: Certainly, medium it is
responses.listen_for: Order confirmed.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください
responses.english: Please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: しょうしょう (少々, shoushou) = a brief moment.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください

phrases.kanji: ミディアムでお願いします

phrases.japanese: トッピングはなにがえらべますか？
phrases.romaji: Toppingu wa nani ga erabemasu ka?
phrases.notes: Common at ramen shops with customizable トッピング (toppingu, toppings) like あじたまご (味玉, ajitamago) / seasoned egg, チャーシュー (chaashuu) / braised pork.

responses.japanese: あじたまごやチャーシューがにんきです
responses.romaji: Ajitamago ya chaashuu ga ninki desu
responses.english: Seasoned egg and braised pork are popular
responses.listen_for: にんき (人気, ninki) = popular.
responses.kanji: 味玉やチャーシューが人気です

responses.japanese: むりょうのトッピングはねぎとのりです
responses.romaji: Muryou no toppingu wa negi to nori desu
responses.english: The free toppings are green onion and nori
responses.listen_for: むりょう (無料, muryou) = free of charge.
responses.kanji: 無料のトッピングはねぎとのりです

phrases.kanji: トッピングは何が選べますか？

phrases.japanese: かためでおねがいします
phrases.notes: Ramen noodle firmness: かため (硬め, katame) = firm, ふつう (普通, futsuu) = regular, やわらかめ (柔らかめ, yawarakame) = soft.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、かためですね
responses.english: Certainly, firm it is
responses.listen_for: Order confirmed.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、硬めですね

responses.japanese: あぶらのりょうはどうしますか？
responses.romaji: Abura no ryou wa dou shimasu ka?
responses.english: How much oil would you like?
responses.listen_for: あぶら (油, abura) = oil/fat, another common ramen customization.
responses.kanji: 油の量はどうしますか？

phrases.kanji: 麺の硬さはどうしますか？

phrases.japanese: セットにへんこうできますか？
phrases.english: Can I change this to a set meal?
phrases.notes: セット (setto) = set meal, usually adds rice, miso soup, and a small side for a bit extra.

responses.japanese: はい、プラス〜えんでセットになります
responses.romaji: Hai, purasu [X] en de setto ni narimasu
responses.english: Yes, for an extra [X] yen it becomes a set
responses.listen_for: プラス (purasu) = plus/additional.
responses.kanji: はい、プラス〜円でセットになります

responses.japanese: スープかサラダをおえらびいただけます
responses.romaji: Suupu ka sarada wo oerabi itadakemasu
responses.english: You can choose soup or salad
responses.listen_for: おえらび (お選び, oerabi) = your choice.
responses.kanji: スープかサラダをお選びいただけます

phrases.kanji: セットに変更できますか？

phrases.japanese: このりょうりになにがはいっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono ryouri ni nani ga haitte imasu ka?
phrases.notes: りょうり (料理, ryouri) = dish/cuisine. A direct way to ask about ingredients before ordering.

responses.japanese: おもに〜とやさいがはいっています
responses.romaji: Omoni [X] to yasai ga haitte imasu
responses.english: It mainly contains [X] and vegetables
responses.listen_for: おもに (主に, omoni) = mainly.
responses.kanji: 主に〜と野菜が入っています

responses.japanese: げんざいりょうはキッチンでかくにんします
responses.romaji: Genzairyou wa kicchin de kakunin shimasu
responses.english: I'll check the ingredients with the kitchen
responses.listen_for: げんざいりょう (原材料, genzairyou) = raw ingredients/materials.
responses.kanji: 原材料はキッチンで確認します

phrases.kanji: この料理に何が入っていますか？

phrases.japanese: これはなにのおにくですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nani no oniku desu ka?
phrases.english: What kind of meat is this?
phrases.notes: Useful since some dishes aren't obvious — common answers: ぶたにく (豚肉, butaniku) pork, ぎゅうにく (牛肉, gyuuniku) beef, とりにく (鶏肉, toriniku) chicken.

responses.japanese: これはぶたにくです
responses.english: This is pork
responses.listen_for: ぶたにく (豚肉, butaniku) = pork.
responses.kanji: これは豚肉です

responses.japanese: ぎゅうにくととりにくのミックスです
responses.romaji: Gyuuniku to toriniku no mikkusu desu
responses.english: It's a mix of beef and chicken
responses.listen_for: ミックス (mikkusu) = mix.
responses.kanji: 牛肉と鶏肉のミックスです

phrases.kanji: これは何のお肉ですか？

phrases.japanese: ベジタリアンようのりょうりはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Bejitarian you no ryouri wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: ベジタリアン (bejitarian) = vegetarian. ヴィーガン (viigan) = vegan — note that many 'vegetarian' dishes in Japan still use dashi (fish stock), so ask specifically if that matters.

responses.japanese: はい、やさいだけのメニューがございます
responses.romaji: Hai, yasai dake no menyuu ga gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, we have a vegetables-only menu
responses.listen_for: やさいだけ (野菜だけ, yasai dake) = vegetables only.
responses.kanji: はい、野菜だけのメニューがございます

responses.japanese: だしにさかながつかわれていることがおおいです
responses.romaji: Dashi ni sakana ga tsukawarete iru koto ga ooi desu
responses.english: The soup stock often contains fish
responses.listen_for: だし (dashi) = Japanese soup stock, often fish-based.
responses.kanji: だしに魚が使われていることが多いです

phrases.kanji: ベジタリアン用の料理はありますか？

phrases.japanese: これにこむぎこははいっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kore ni komugiko wa haitte imasu ka?
phrases.notes: こむぎこ (小麦粉, komugiko) = wheat flour — important for gluten-free needs; soy sauce (しょうゆ) often contains wheat too.

responses.japanese: はい、しょうゆにもこむぎがふくまれています
responses.romaji: Hai, shouyu ni mo komugi ga fukumarete imasu
responses.english: Yes, the soy sauce also contains wheat
responses.listen_for: しょうゆ (醤油, shouyu) = soy sauce.
responses.kanji: はい、醤油にも小麦が含まれています

responses.japanese: グルテンフリーのしょうゆもございます
responses.romaji: Guruten furii no shouyu mo gozaimasu
responses.english: We also have gluten-free soy sauce
responses.listen_for: グルテンフリー (guruten furii) = gluten-free.
responses.kanji: グルテンフリーの醤油もございます

phrases.kanji: これに小麦粉は入っていますか？

phrases.japanese: なまでたべられますか？
phrases.notes: なま (生, nama) = raw. Useful for sashimi/egg dishes to confirm freshness/preparation.

responses.japanese: はい、しんせんなのでなまでどうぞ
responses.romaji: Hai, shinsen nanode nama de douzo
responses.english: Yes, it's fresh so please enjoy it raw
responses.listen_for: しんせん (新鮮, shinsen) = fresh.
responses.kanji: はい、新鮮なので生でどうぞ

responses.japanese: かねつしてからたべるりょうりです
responses.romaji: Kanetsu shite kara taberu ryouri desu
responses.english: This is a dish meant to be eaten after being heated
responses.listen_for: かねつ (加熱, kanetsu) = heating.
responses.kanji: 加熱してから食べる料理です

phrases.kanji: 生で食べられますか？

phrases.japanese: このしょくざいはどこさんですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono shokuzai wa doko-san desu ka?
phrases.notes: しょくざい (食材, shokuzai) = ingredient/foodstuff. 〜さん (産, -san) = produced in [place] — e.g. ほっかいどうさん (北海道産, Hokkaidou-san) = produced in Hokkaido.

responses.japanese: じもとさんのやさいをつかっています
responses.romaji: Jimotosan no yasai wo tsukatte imasu
responses.english: We use locally grown vegetables
responses.listen_for: じもと (地元, jimoto) = local area.
responses.kanji: 地元産の野菜を使っています

responses.japanese: きょうのさかなはほっかいどうさんです
responses.romaji: Kyou no sakana wa Hokkaidou-san desu
responses.english: Today's fish is from Hokkaido
responses.listen_for: さかな (魚, sakana) = fish.
responses.kanji: 今日の魚は北海道産です

phrases.kanji: この食材はどこ産ですか？

phrases.japanese: きせつのしょくざいをつかっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kisetsu no shokuzai wo tsukatte imasu ka?
phrases.notes: きせつ (季節, kisetsu) = season. しゅん (旬, shun) is another key word meaning 'in season/at its best'.

responses.japanese: はい、しゅんのしょくざいをたいせつにしています
responses.romaji: Hai, shun no shokuzai wo taisetsu ni shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we value seasonal (in-season) ingredients
responses.listen_for: しゅん (旬, shun) = in season/at its best.
responses.kanji: はい、旬の食材を大切にしています

responses.japanese: こんげつは〜がしゅんです
responses.english: This month, [X] is in season
responses.listen_for: こんげつ (今月, kongetsu) = this month.
responses.kanji: 今月は〜が旬です

phrases.kanji: 季節の食材を使っていますか？

phrases.japanese: このソースのあじはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono soosu no aji wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: ソース (soosu) = sauce. Overlaps nicely with the flavor vocabulary from the bar scenario (あまい/sweet, からい/spicy, すっぱい/sour).

responses.japanese: みそべーすのあまからいソースです
responses.romaji: Miso beesu no amakarai soosu desu
responses.english: It's a miso-based sweet-and-spicy sauce
responses.listen_for: あまからい (甘辛い, amakarai) = sweet-and-spicy.
responses.kanji: 味噌ベースの甘辛いソースです

responses.japanese: ゆずをつかったさっぱりしたソースです
responses.romaji: Yuzu wo tsukatta sappari shita soosu desu
responses.english: It's a refreshing sauce made with yuzu
responses.listen_for: さっぱり (sappari) = refreshing/light.
responses.kanji: 柚子を使ったさっぱりしたソースです

phrases.kanji: このソースの味は何ですか？

phrases.japanese: セットにもうついているんじゃないですか？
phrases.romaji: Setto ni mou tsuite iru n ja nai desu ka?
phrases.english: Doesn't the set already come with it?
phrases.notes: Situation: you added an extra item (soup, rice, salad) to a set meal that already includes it. Ask before the bill is printed. ついている (付いている, tsuite iru) = is attached / included.

responses.japanese: はい、セットにはもうついております
responses.romaji: Hai, setto ni wa mou tsuite orimasu
responses.english: Yes, the set already includes it
responses.listen_for: ついております (付いております, tsuite orimasu) = is included (polite form of ついている).
responses.kanji: はい、セットにはもう付いております

responses.japanese: では、ごちゅうもんからはずしておきますね
responses.romaji: Dewa, gochuumon kara hazushite okimasu ne
responses.english: Then I'll take it off your order
responses.listen_for: ごちゅうもん (ご注文, gochuumon) = your order. はずす (外す, hazusu) = to remove.
responses.kanji: では、ご注文から外しておきますね

phrases.kanji: セットにもう付いているんじゃないですか？

phrases.japanese: じゃあ、ほかのものにかえてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Jaa, hoka no mono ni kaete mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: Then, can I switch to something else?
phrases.notes: Situation: an item included in your set (drink, side, or dessert) is sold out and the staff tells you. ほか (hoka) = other. かえる (替える, kaeru) = to switch.

responses.japanese: はい、ほかのドリンクはいかがですか？
responses.romaji: Hai, hoka no dorinku wa ikaga desu ka?
responses.english: Yes, how about another drink?
responses.listen_for: いかが = how about (a polite offer). They'll suggest the alternatives available.
responses.kanji: はい、ほかのドリンクはいかがですか？

responses.japanese: 申し訳ございません、そちらは売り切れです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen, sochira wa urikire desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, that one is sold out
responses.listen_for: 売り切れ (urikire) = sold out. そちら = that one (polite).
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございません、そちらは売り切れです

phrases.kanji: じゃあ、ほかのものに替えてもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: ドリンクはコーヒーにかえられますか？
phrases.romaji: Dorinku wa koohii ni kaeraremasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I swap the drink for coffee?
phrases.notes: Situation: the drink in your set is unavailable, or you'd simply prefer coffee. Swaps are often possible but may cost extra. コーヒー (kōhii) = coffee.

responses.japanese: はい、ホットかアイスをおえらびください
responses.romaji: Hai, hotto ka aisu wo oerabi kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please choose hot or iced
responses.listen_for: ホット (hot) and アイス (iced) are the two coffee options. おえらび (お選び) = your choice.
responses.kanji: はい、ホットかアイスをお選びください

responses.japanese: コーヒーは、プラス〇円になります
responses.romaji: Koohii wa, purasu [X] en ni narimasu
responses.english: Coffee is an extra [X] yen
responses.listen_for: プラス (purasu) = plus / extra. 〇 is where the price goes.
responses.kanji: コーヒーは、プラス〇円になります

phrases.kanji: ドリンクはコーヒーに変えられますか？

phrases.japanese: ちゅうもんしていないものが、はいっています
phrases.romaji: Chuumon shite inai mono ga, haitte imasu
phrases.english: There's something on the bill that I didn't order
phrases.notes: Situation: the bill shows an item you didn't order. Say it calmly and ask them to check. 注文 (chuumon) = order.

responses.japanese: 失礼いたしました。すぐに確認いたします
responses.romaji: Shitsurei itashimashita. Sugu ni kakunin itashimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry. I'll check right away
responses.listen_for: 確認 (かくにん, kakunin) = check / confirm.
responses.kanji: 失礼いたしました。すぐに確認いたします

responses.japanese: 申し訳ございません、すぐにおなおししますね
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen, sugu ni o-naoshi shimasu ne
responses.english: I'm very sorry, I'll correct it right away
responses.listen_for: おなおし (お直し, onaoshi) = correction / fix.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございません、すぐにお直ししますね

phrases.kanji: 注文していないものが、入っています

phrases.japanese: これは、ちゅうもんしていません
phrases.notes: Situation: a dish arrives that isn't yours, often a mix-up with a neighbouring table. Point to the dish and keep it polite.

responses.japanese: 失礼しました、すぐにお取り替えします
responses.romaji: Shitsurei shimashita, sugu ni o-torikae shimasu
responses.english: Sorry, I'll replace it right away
responses.listen_for: 取り替え (torikae) = replacement.
responses.kanji: 失礼しました、すぐにお取り替えします

responses.japanese: おまちください、かくにんしてまいります
responses.english: Please wait, I'll go check
responses.listen_for: まいります (参ります) = humble form of 'go / come'. They're going to verify the order.
responses.kanji: お待ちください、確認してまいります

phrases.kanji: これは、注文していません

phrases.japanese: ランチセットは、なんじまでですか？
phrases.romaji: Ranchi setto wa, nanji made desu ka?
phrases.english: Until what time is the lunch set available?
phrases.notes: Situation: you want a lunch set but it may have ended. Lunch sets often stop in the early afternoon. なんじ (何時) = what time.

responses.japanese: じゅうよじまでです。そのあとはディナーになります
responses.romaji: Juuyoji made desu. Sono ato wa dinaa ni narimasu
responses.english: Until 2 PM. After that it's the dinner menu
responses.listen_for: 十四時 (じゅうよじ, juuyoji) = 2 PM. ディナー (dinner) = evening menu.
responses.kanji: 14時までです。そのあとはディナーになります

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありません、本日はもう終了しました
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, honjitsu wa mou shuuryou shimashita
responses.english: I'm sorry, it has already ended today
responses.listen_for: 終了 (しゅうりょう, shuuryou) = ended / finished.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、本日はもう終了しました

phrases.kanji: ランチセットは、何時までですか？

phrases.japanese: ラストオーダーは、なんじですか？
phrases.romaji: Rasuto oodaa wa, nanji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Situation: you want to order something else before the kitchen closes. Last order is usually about 30 minutes before closing.

responses.japanese: にじゅういちじはんまでです
responses.english: Until 9:30 PM
responses.listen_for: はん (半) = half past. 21時半 = 9:30 PM.
responses.kanji: 21時半までです

responses.japanese: まだだいじょうぶですよ、ごゆっくりどうぞ
responses.romaji: Mada daijoubu desu yo, goyukkuri douzo
responses.english: It's still fine, take your time
responses.listen_for: ごゆっくり = take your time. Common when you're still in the restaurant.
responses.kanji: まだ大丈夫ですよ、ごゆっくりどうぞ

phrases.kanji: ラストオーダーは、何時ですか？

phrases.japanese: 〜までいくらですか？
phrases.notes: Fill in the destination name.

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.english: [price] yen
responses.listen_for: Just the number + えん (円). Station machines also display fares on a map — use those to confirm.
responses.kanji: 〜円です

phrases.japanese: 〜はどこですか？
phrases.notes: Most useful navigation phrase.

responses.japanese: まっすぐいって、みぎにまがってください
responses.romaji: Massugu itte, migi ni magatte kudasai
responses.english: Go straight and turn right
responses.listen_for: まっすぐ = straight, みぎ (右, migi) = right, ひだり (左, hidari) = left, まがる (曲がる, magaru) = turn. These four words cover most direction answers.
responses.kanji: まっすぐ行って、右に曲がってください

responses.japanese: あそこです
responses.english: It's over there
responses.listen_for: あそこ = over there (far). They'll usually point. Look where they gesture.

responses.japanese: あるいて〜ふんぐらいです
responses.english: About [X] minutes on foot
responses.listen_for: あるいて (歩いて, aruite) = walking. ふん (分, fun) = minutes. ぐらい = approximately.
responses.kanji: 歩いて〜分ぐらいです

phrases.japanese: このバスは〜にいきますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono basu wa [destination] ni ikimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Replace バス (basu) with でんしゃ (電車, densha) / train if needed.

responses.japanese: はい、このバスでいけます
responses.english: Yes, you can get there on this bus
responses.listen_for: いけます (行けます, ikemasu) = can go. You're on the right bus.
responses.kanji: はい、このバスで行けます

responses.japanese: いいえ、〜ばんのバスにのってください
responses.romaji: Iie, [X] ban no basu ni notte kudasai
responses.english: No, please take bus number [X]
responses.listen_for: ばん (番, ban) = number [X]. のって (乗って, notte) = ride/take. Listen for the bus number.
responses.kanji: いいえ、〜番のバスに乗ってください

phrases.kanji: このバスは〜に行きますか？

phrases.japanese: つぎのえきはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no eki wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Announcements on most lines are bilingual.

responses.japanese: つぎは〜えきです
responses.english: The next station is [station name]
responses.listen_for: つぎわ (次は, tsugi wa) = next is. えき (駅, eki) = [name] station.
responses.kanji: 次は〜駅です

phrases.kanji: 次の駅はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: 〜ばんせんはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Very useful in large stations like Shinjuku.

responses.japanese: 〜ばんせんにあちらです
responses.english: Platform [X] is over there
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the signs — platform numbers are clearly posted.
responses.kanji: 〜番線にあちらです

phrases.kanji: 〜番線はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: タクシーをおねがいします
phrases.notes: Doors open automatically — don't touch them.

responses.japanese: どちらまでですか？
responses.english: Where are you going?
responses.listen_for: どちら = where (polite). Show your destination in Japanese text on your phone — drivers appreciate this.

phrases.kanji: タクシーをお願いします

phrases.japanese: ここでとめてください
phrases.notes: For taxis.

responses.japanese: 〜えんになります
responses.english: That'll be [amount] yen
responses.listen_for: The fare total. Taxis in Japan are metered and reliable. Always pay exact if possible.
responses.kanji: 〜円になります

phrases.kanji: ここで止めてください

phrases.japanese: のりかえはありますか？
phrases.notes: For complex train routes.

responses.japanese: 〜えきでのりかえてください
responses.english: Please transfer at [station]
responses.listen_for: のりかえて (乗り換えて, norikaete) = transfer. えき (駅) = station name. Note the station name carefully.
responses.kanji: 〜駅で乗り換えてください

responses.japanese: のりかえなしでいけます
responses.english: You can go without transferring
responses.listen_for: なし (nashi) = without. Direct route — stay on the train.
responses.kanji: 乗り換えなしで行けます

phrases.kanji: 乗り換えはありますか？

phrases.japanese: でぐちはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Big stations have numbered/lettered exits.

responses.japanese: 〜ばんでぐちがあちらです
responses.english: Exit [number] is over there
responses.listen_for: ばん (番) = number. あちら = over there. All exits are signposted — follow the kanji for your number.
responses.kanji: 〜番出口があちらです

phrases.kanji: 出口はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: Suicaはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Suica wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy a Suica card?
phrases.notes: Get one at the airport.

responses.japanese: けんばいきでおかいもとめいただけます
responses.english: You can purchase one at the ticket machine
responses.listen_for: けんばいき (券売機, kenbaiki) = ticket vending machine. They'll point you to it.
responses.kanji: 券売機でお買い求めいただけます

phrases.kanji: Suicaはどこで買えますか？

phrases.japanese: きっぷをにまいください
phrases.notes: まい (枚, mai) counts flat thin objects like tickets and paper: 1いちまい (枚, ichimai), 2にまい (枚, nimai), 3さんまい (枚, sanmai).

responses.japanese: かたみちですか、おうふくですか？
responses.romaji: Katamichi desu ka, oufuku desu ka?
responses.english: One-way or round-trip?
responses.listen_for: かたみち (片道, katamichi) = one-way, おうふく (往復, oufuku) = round-trip.
responses.kanji: 片道ですか、往復ですか？

phrases.kanji: 切符を2枚ください

phrases.japanese: タクシーはさんにんのれますか？
phrases.english: Can three people fit in this taxi?
phrases.notes: Standard Japanese taxis seat up to 4 passengers; larger groups need a ジャンボタクシー (jumbo taxi).

responses.japanese: はい、だいじょうぶです
responses.english: Yes, that's fine
responses.listen_for: Confirms your group fits.
responses.kanji: はい、大丈夫です

responses.japanese: よにんまでです
responses.english: Up to four people
responses.listen_for: 4よにんまで (人まで, yonin made) = up to 4 people — standard taxi capacity.
responses.kanji: 4人までです

phrases.kanji: タクシーは3人乗れますか？

phrases.japanese: そこは、わたしの指定席です
phrases.romaji: Soko wa, watashi no shiteiseki desu
phrases.notes: Situation: someone is sitting in your reserved seat on a train or bus. 指定席 (shiteiseki) = reserved seat. 自由席 (jiyuuseki) = unreserved seat.

responses.japanese: 失礼しました。切符を拝見できますか？
responses.romaji: Shitsurei shimashita. Kippu wo haiken dekimasu ka?
responses.english: Sorry. May I see your ticket?
responses.listen_for: 拝見 (haiken) = humble 'to look at'. Staff may ask to check your ticket.
responses.kanji: 失礼しました。切符を拝見できますか？

responses.japanese: 座席番号をご確認ください
responses.english: Please check your seat number
responses.listen_for: 座席番号 (zaseki bangou) = seat number. ご確認 = please check.
responses.kanji: 座席番号をご確認ください

phrases.japanese: じゆうせきは、まだあいていますか？
phrases.romaji: Jiyuuseki wa, mada aite imasu ka?
phrases.notes: Situation: reserved seats are sold out and you want to board the unreserved cars instead. 空いている (aite iru) = available.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありません、本日の自由席は満席です
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, honjitsu no jiyuuseki wa manseki desu
responses.english: Sorry, the unreserved cars are full today
responses.listen_for: 満席 (manseki) = full, no seats left.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、本日の自由席は満席です

responses.japanese: 次の電車なら、空いています
responses.romaji: Tsugi no densha nara, aite imasu
responses.english: The next train has seats available
responses.listen_for: 次の電車 (tsugi no densha) = next train. なら = if it's about that one.
responses.kanji: 次の電車なら、空いています

phrases.kanji: 自由席は、まだ空いていますか？

phrases.japanese: のる電車をまちがえました
phrases.english: I got on the wrong train
phrases.notes: Situation: you boarded a train heading in the wrong direction. まちがえる (間違える, machigaeru) = to make a mistake.

responses.japanese: 次の駅でおりて、のりかえてください
responses.romaji: Tsugi no eki de orite, norikaete kudasai
responses.english: Get off at the next station and transfer
responses.listen_for: のりかえ (乗り換え, norikae) = transfer. おりる (降りる, oriru) = get off.
responses.kanji: 次の駅で降りて、乗り換えてください

responses.japanese: この電車は、ちがうほうこうです
responses.romaji: Kono densha wa, chigau houkou desu
responses.english: This train is going the wrong direction
responses.listen_for: ほうこう (方向, houkou) = direction.
responses.kanji: この電車は、違う方向です

phrases.kanji: 乗る電車を間違えました

phrases.japanese: タクシーのりばはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Takushii noriba wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: のりば (noriba) = boarding area. Taxi stands are often outside the main exit of stations and hotels.

responses.japanese: まっすぐいって、みぎです
responses.english: Straight ahead, on the right
responses.listen_for: みぎ (右, migi) = right. ひだり (左) = left.

responses.japanese: あちらのロータリーです
responses.english: It's at the roundabout over there
responses.listen_for: ロータリー (rotary) = the roundabout in front of a station where taxis wait.

phrases.japanese: この住所までいってください
phrases.english: Please take me to this address
phrases.notes: 住所 (juusho) = address. Show the address on your phone if the driver doesn't know the place name.

responses.japanese: はい、かしこまりました
responses.english: Yes, certainly
responses.listen_for: かしこまりました = polite 'understood, certainly'.

responses.japanese: ナビにいれてもいいですか？
responses.romaji: Navi ni irete mo ii desu ka?
responses.english: May I enter it into the navigation?
responses.listen_for: ナビ (navi) = GPS navigation. いれる (入れる) = to enter.

phrases.japanese: 住所をみせてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Juusho wo misete mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I show you the address?
phrases.notes: Use this when the place name isn't understood. Have the Japanese address ready on your phone.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please / here you go.

responses.japanese: ここですか？
responses.english: Is it here?
responses.listen_for: ここ = here. The driver is checking the address with you.

phrases.japanese: すぐもどりますので、ここでまっていてください
phrases.romaji: Sugu modorimasu node, koko de matte ite kudasai
phrases.english: I'll be right back, so please wait here
phrases.notes: まつ (待つ, matsu) = to wait. Useful when you need a quick stop, such as picking up something.

responses.japanese: はい、わかりました
responses.english: Yes, understood
responses.listen_for: わかりました = understood (polite).

responses.japanese: メーターをとめておきますね
responses.english: I'll pause the meter
responses.listen_for: メーター (meter) = fare meter. とめる (止める) = to stop.

phrases.japanese: トランクをあけてください
phrases.notes: トランク (toranku) = trunk / boot. Use it for large suitcases.

responses.japanese: はい、ただいまあけます
responses.english: Yes, opening it now
responses.listen_for: ただいま = right now. あける (開ける) = to open.

responses.japanese: お荷物はどうぞ、お入れください
responses.english: Please put your luggage in
responses.listen_for: お入れください = please put in (polite).

phrases.japanese: カードでしはらえますか？
phrases.notes: 支払い (shiharai) = payment. Not every taxi accepts cards, so ask before the ride ends.

responses.japanese: はい、つかえます
responses.english: Yes, you can use it
responses.listen_for: つかえます (使えます) = can be used.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありません、現金のみです
responses.english: Sorry, cash only
responses.listen_for: 現金 (genkin) = cash. のみ (only).

phrases.japanese: PayPayでしはらえますか？
phrases.notes: QR-code payment apps like PayPay are common. Ask before the ride starts.

responses.japanese: はい、画面のQRコードをよんでください
responses.romaji: Hai, gamen no QR koodo wo yonde kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please scan the QR code on the screen
responses.listen_for: 読む (yomu) = to read / scan. 画面 (gamen) = screen.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ありません、そちらは使えません
responses.english: Sorry, that one can't be used
responses.listen_for: そちら = that one. 使えません = can't be used.

phrases.japanese: おつりはいりません
phrases.notes: Tipping isn't expected in Japan, but rounding up the fare is common and polite.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます
responses.english: Thank you
responses.listen_for: Polite thanks from the driver.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございました。またどうぞ
responses.english: Thank you. Please come again
responses.listen_for: またどうぞ = please come again. A common goodbye.

phrases.japanese: レシートをください
phrases.notes: レシート (receipt). For business expenses, ask for 領収書 (ryoushuusho), the official receipt.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらどうぞ
responses.english: Yes, here you go
responses.listen_for: こちら = here / this (polite).

responses.japanese: 領収書もひつようですか？
responses.english: Do you also need an official receipt?
responses.listen_for: 領収書 (ryoushuusho) = official receipt. 必要 (hitsuyou) = necessary.

phrases.japanese: こちらのみちでいってください
phrases.romaji: Kochira no michi de itte kudasai
phrases.notes: みち (道, michi) = road / route. Use it to point the driver to a route you know.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Polite acknowledgement.

responses.japanese: こうそくどうろをつかいますか？
responses.english: Shall I use the expressway?
responses.listen_for: 高速道路 (kousoku douro) = expressway. 使う (tsukau) = to use.

phrases.japanese: つぎの角をみぎにまがってください
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no kado wo migi ni magatte kudasai
phrases.english: Please turn right at the next corner
phrases.notes: 角 (kado) = corner. 曲がる (magaru) = to turn.

responses.japanese: はい、みぎですね
responses.english: Right, got it
responses.listen_for: 〜ね = checking that you agree.

responses.japanese: もうすこしさきですか？
responses.english: Is it a bit further?
responses.listen_for: さき (先) = further ahead. もうすこし = a little more.

phrases.japanese: いそいでいます。はやくいけますか？
phrases.english: I'm in a hurry. Can we get there quickly?
phrases.notes: いそぐ (急ぐ, isogu) = to hurry. The driver can choose a faster route, but can't guarantee the arrival time.

responses.japanese: はい、がんばります
responses.english: Yes, I'll do my best
responses.listen_for: がんばる = to do one's best.

responses.japanese: じゅうごふんほどでつきます
responses.english: We'll arrive in about 15 minutes
responses.listen_for: 〜ほど = about. 分 (fun) = minutes.

phrases.japanese: アプリでタクシーをよびたいです
phrases.romaji: Apuri de takushii wo yobitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to call a taxi through the app
phrases.notes: よぶ (呼ぶ, yobu) = to call. Apps such as GO and Uber let you book a taxi from your phone.

responses.japanese: お迎えの場所をアプリでご確認ください
responses.romaji: O-mukae no basho wo apuri de gokakunin kudasai
responses.english: Please confirm the pickup location in the app
responses.listen_for: お迎え (omukae) = pickup. 場所 (basho) = place.

responses.japanese: ただいま配車中です
responses.english: We're arranging your ride right now
responses.listen_for: 配車 (haisha) = dispatching a vehicle. 中 (chuu) = in progress.

phrases.japanese: お迎えまでどのくらいかかりますか？
phrases.romaji: O-mukae made dono kurai kakarimasu ka?
phrases.notes: かかる = to take (time). The app usually shows a live countdown.

responses.japanese: あと五分ほどです
responses.english: About five more minutes
responses.listen_for: あと = remaining. 五分 (gofun) = five minutes.

responses.japanese: ドライバーが近くにいます
responses.english: The driver is nearby
responses.listen_for: 近く (chikaku) = nearby.

phrases.japanese: ドライバーの名前と車のナンバーを教えてください
phrases.romaji: Doraibaa no namae to kuruma no nanbaa wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please tell me the driver's name and car plate
phrases.notes: ナンバー (nanbaa) = license plate. Check it matches the car before you get in.

responses.japanese: 田中です。白いプリウスです
responses.english: I'm Tanaka. It's a white Prius
responses.listen_for: 白い (shiroi) = white. Car models are often written in katakana.

responses.japanese: アプリでも車のナンバーを確認できます
responses.romaji: Apuri de mo kuruma no nanbaa wo kakunin dekimasu
responses.english: You can also check the plate in the app
responses.listen_for: 確認 (kakunin) = check.

phrases.japanese: 乗る場所をへんこうしたいです
phrases.romaji: Noru basho wo henkou shitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to change the pickup point
phrases.notes: 乗る (noru) = to board. 変更 (henkou) = change.

responses.japanese: はい、アプリでピンをうごかしてください
responses.romaji: Hai, apuri de pin wo ugokashite kudasai
responses.english: Yes, move the pin in the app
responses.listen_for: ピン (pin) = map marker. 動かす (ugokasu) = to move.

responses.japanese: ドライバーがむかっているので、へんこうできないかもしれません
responses.romaji: Doraibaa ga mukatte iru node, henkou dekinai kamo shiremasen
responses.english: The driver is already on the way, so changing may not be possible
responses.listen_for: 向かう (mukau) = to head toward. かもしれません = might / may.

phrases.japanese: キャンセルりょうはかかりますか？
phrases.notes: キャンセル (kyanseru) = cancel. 料 (ryou) = fee.

responses.japanese: はい、五分いじょうたつとかかります
responses.romaji: Hai, gofun ijou tatsu to kakarimasu
responses.english: Yes, it's charged after five minutes
responses.listen_for: 以上 (ijou) = more than. たつ = to pass.

responses.japanese: いいえ、さいしょの五分はむりょうです
responses.romaji: Iie, saisho no gofun wa muryou desu
responses.english: No, the first five minutes are free
responses.listen_for: 最初 (saisho) = first. 無料 (muryou) = free.

phrases.japanese: クーポンはつかえますか？
phrases.notes: クーポン (kuupon) = coupon. Usually entered in the app before booking.

responses.japanese: はい、アプリでにゅうりょくしてください
responses.romaji: Hai, apuri de nyuuryoku shite kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please enter it in the app
responses.listen_for: 入力 (nyuuryoku) = input / enter.

responses.japanese: このクーポンはつかえません
responses.english: This coupon can't be used
responses.listen_for: 使えません = can't be used.

phrases.japanese: ドライバーにでんわできますか？
phrases.notes: でんわ (電話, denwa) = phone call. Many apps hide the number and route calls through the app.

responses.japanese: はい、アプリのでんわボタンをおしてください
responses.romaji: Hai, apuri no denwa botan wo oshite kudasai
responses.english: Yes, press the call button in the app
responses.listen_for: ボタン (botan) = button.

responses.japanese: アプリのチャットでもれんらくできます
responses.romaji: Apuri no chatto de mo renraku dekimasu
responses.english: You can also message through the app's chat
responses.listen_for: チャット (chat) = message. 連絡 (renraku) = contact.

phrases.japanese: ドライバーがきません
phrases.notes: Use this if the car hasn't arrived after the estimated time.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、いまむかっています
responses.english: I'm sorry, they're on their way now
responses.listen_for: 向かう (mukau) = to head toward. いま = now.

responses.japanese: そちらの場所をおしえてください
responses.romaji: Sochira no basho wo oshiete kudasai
responses.english: Please tell me where you are
responses.listen_for: 教える (oshieru) = to tell.

phrases.japanese: カードのとうろくをかえたいです
phrases.romaji: Kaado no touroku wo kaetai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to change my registered card
phrases.notes: 登録 (touroku) = registration. Payment details are changed in the app settings.

responses.japanese: アプリの支払い設定からかえられます
responses.romaji: Apuri no shiharai settei kara kaeraremasu
responses.english: You can change it in the app's payment settings
responses.listen_for: 設定 (settei) = settings. 支払い (shiharai) = payment.

responses.japanese: サポートにおといあわせください
responses.english: Please contact support
responses.listen_for: サポート (support) = customer support. お問い合わせ = inquiry.

phrases.japanese: りょうしゅうしょをメールでもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Ryoushuusho wo meeru de moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I get the receipt by email?
phrases.notes: 領収書 (ryoushuusho) = official receipt. Apps usually send it automatically after the ride.

responses.japanese: はい、アプリに登録したメールにおくります
responses.romaji: Hai, apuri ni touroku shita meeru ni okurimasu
responses.english: Yes, we'll send it to the email registered in the app
responses.listen_for: 送る (okuru) = to send.

responses.japanese: アプリの履歴からもダウンロードできます
responses.romaji: Apuri no rireki kara mo daunroodo dekimasu
responses.english: You can also download it from the app's history
responses.listen_for: 履歴 (rireki) = history.

phrases.japanese: チェックインをおねがいします
phrases.notes: They'll ask for your passport.

responses.japanese: パスポートをおねがいします
responses.english: Your passport please
responses.listen_for: Standard for all foreign guests. Hand it over.
responses.kanji: パスポートをお願いします

responses.japanese: こちらにサインをおねがいします
responses.english: Please sign here
responses.listen_for: サイン (sain) = signature. They'll show you where.
responses.kanji: こちらにサインをお願いします

responses.japanese: おへやは〜かいです
responses.english: Your room is on floor [X]
responses.listen_for: かい (階, kai) = floor number. 1いっかい (階, ikkai) = 1F. They'll hand you the key card too.
responses.kanji: お部屋は〜階です

phrases.kanji: チェックインをお願いします

phrases.japanese: 〇めいでよやくした〜です
phrases.english: I have a reservation for ___ people under [name]
phrases.notes: Combine the number of guests with your name when checking in as a group. めい (名, mei) is the formal counter for people used in hotels and restaurants.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください、かくにんいたします
responses.english: Please wait a moment, I'll confirm
responses.listen_for: They're pulling up your reservation.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください、確認いたします

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくをかくにんいたしました
responses.english: Yes, I've confirmed your reservation
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認) = confirmed. You're checked in.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約を確認いたしました

phrases.kanji: 〇名で予約した〜です

phrases.japanese: よやくした〜です
phrases.notes: Fill in your name.

responses.japanese: しょうしょうおまちください、かくにんいたします
responses.english: Please wait a moment, I'll confirm
responses.listen_for: They're pulling up your reservation. Wait.
responses.kanji: 少々お待ちください、確認いたします

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくをかくにんいたしました
responses.english: Yes, I've confirmed your reservation
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認) = confirmed. You're checked in.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約を確認いたしました

phrases.kanji: 予約した〜です

phrases.japanese: へやのかぎをなくしました
phrases.notes: Hopefully not needed.

responses.japanese: へやばんごうをおしえていただけますか？
responses.romaji: Heya bangou wo oshiete itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you tell me your room number?
responses.listen_for: へやばんごう (部屋番号, heya bangou) = room number. Tell them your floor and room.
responses.kanji: 部屋番号を教えていただけますか？

phrases.kanji: 部屋の鍵をなくしました

phrases.japanese: タオルをもっとください
phrases.notes: Replace タオル (taoru) with pillow, blanket, etc.

responses.japanese: すぐにおもちいたします
responses.english: I'll bring them right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away. They'll deliver to your room.
responses.kanji: すくにお持ちいたします

phrases.japanese: Wi-Fiのパスワードはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Wi-Fi no pasuwaado wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Often on a card in the room.

responses.japanese: こちらのカードをごらんください
responses.romaji: Kochira no kaado wo goran kudasai
responses.english: Please see this card
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you a card or point to one in the room with the password printed on it.
responses.kanji: こちらのカードをご覧ください

phrases.kanji: Wi-Fiのパスワードは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: チェックアウトはなんじですか？
phrases.romaji: Chekku auto wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Usually 11:00 or 12:00.

responses.japanese: チェックアウトは〜じでございます
responses.romaji: Chekku auto wa [X] ji de gozaimasu
responses.english: Checkout is at [X] o'clock
responses.listen_for: じ (時, ji) = o'clock. Listen for the number before じ (時).
responses.kanji: チェックアウトは〜時でございます

responses.japanese: レイトチェックアウトをごきぼうですか？
responses.romaji: Reito chekku auto wo go-kibou desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like a late checkout?
responses.listen_for: レイトチェックアウト = late checkout. きぼう (希望, kibou) = wish/desire. There's usually a fee.
responses.kanji: レイトチェックアウトをご希望ですか？

phrases.kanji: チェックアウトは何時ですか？

phrases.japanese: にもつをあずかってもらえますか？
phrases.notes: Japanese hotels excel at this.

responses.japanese: はい、なんじまでおあずかりしますか？
responses.romaji: Hai, nanji made oazukari shimasu ka?
responses.english: Yes, until what time shall we hold it?
responses.listen_for: なんじまで (何時まで, nanji made) = until what time. Tell them your pickup time.
responses.kanji: はい、何時までお預かりしますか？

phrases.kanji: 荷物を預かってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ちかくにおすすめのレストランはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Chikaku ni osusume no resutoran wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there any recommended restaurants nearby?
phrases.notes: Hotel staff recommendations are gold.

responses.japanese: 〜がとてもおいしいですよ
responses.english: [Place] is very delicious
responses.listen_for: とても (totemo) = very. They'll name a place. Ask them to write it down: かいてもらえますか？ (書いてもらえますか？, Kaite moraemasu ka?)
responses.kanji: 〜がとても美味しいですよ

phrases.kanji: 近くにおすすめのレストランはありますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりべやをおねがいします
phrases.notes: ふたりべや (二人部屋, futari-beya) = twin/double room. ひとりべや (一人部屋, hitori-beya) = single, さんにんべや (三人部屋, san-nin-beya) = triple.

responses.japanese: ツインとダブル、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Tsuin to daburu, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Twin or double, which would you prefer?
responses.listen_for: ツイン (tsuin) = two separate beds, ダブル (daburu) = one large shared bed.

phrases.kanji: 二人部屋をお願いします

phrases.japanese: さんにんべやはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a room for three?
phrases.notes: Triple rooms are less common in Japan — many hotels max out at 2 per room, so you may need an extra bed or a separate room.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、まんしつです
responses.english: I'm sorry, we're fully booked
responses.listen_for: まんしつ (満室, manshitsu) = fully booked rooms — different from まんせき (満席, manseki) = full seats.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、満室です

responses.japanese: エキストラベッドをごよういできます
responses.english: We can provide an extra bed
responses.listen_for: エキストラベッド (ekisutora beddo) = extra bed, often a solution for a third guest.
responses.kanji: エキストラベッドをご用意できます

phrases.kanji: 三人部屋はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ながめのいいへやはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Nagame no ii heya wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a room with a nice view?
phrases.notes: ながめ (眺め, nagame) = view/scenery. Ask for やまがわ (山側, yamagawa) / mountain-side or うみがわ (海側, umigawa) / ocean-side specifically.

responses.japanese: はい、うみがわのおへやがございます
responses.romaji: Hai, umigawa no oheya ga gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, we have ocean-view rooms
responses.listen_for: うみがわ (海側, umigawa) = ocean-facing side.
responses.kanji: はい、海側のお部屋がございます

responses.japanese: ついかりょうきんでアップグレードできます
responses.english: You can upgrade for an extra fee
responses.listen_for: アップグレード (appugureedo) = upgrade.
responses.kanji: 追加料金でアップグレードできます

phrases.kanji: 眺めのいい部屋はありますか？

phrases.japanese: きつえんのおへやはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kitsuen no oheya wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Most Japanese hotels now default to non-smoking (きんえん, 禁煙) rooms — smoking rooms are increasingly rare and may cost extra.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、ぜんしつきんえんです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, zenshitsu kin'en desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, all rooms are non-smoking
responses.listen_for: ぜんしつ (全室, zenshitsu) = all rooms.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、全室禁煙です

responses.japanese: きつえんかいがございます
responses.english: There is a smoking floor
responses.listen_for: きつえんかい (喫煙階, kitsuen-kai) = smoking floor.
responses.kanji: 喫煙階がございます

phrases.kanji: 喫煙のお部屋はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ちょうしょくつきのプランはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Choushoku-tsuki no puran wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a plan that includes breakfast?
phrases.notes: ちょうしょくつき (朝食付き, choushoku-tsuki) = breakfast included. Compare with すどまり (素泊まり, sudomari) / room-only, no meals.

responses.japanese: はい、ちょうしょくつきプランにへんこうできます
responses.romaji: Hai, choushoku-tsuki puran ni henkou dekimasu
responses.english: Yes, I can change it to the breakfast-included plan
responses.listen_for: へんこう (変更, henkou) = change/modify.
responses.kanji: はい、朝食付きプランに変更できます

responses.japanese: ちょうしょくは〇かいでろくじからです
responses.romaji: Choushoku wa [X] kai de rokuji kara desu
responses.english: Breakfast is on floor [X] from 6am
responses.listen_for: かい (階, kai) = floor number.
responses.kanji: 朝食は〇階で6時からです

phrases.kanji: 朝食付きのプランはありますか？

phrases.japanese: ベッドをついかできますか？
phrases.english: Can you add an extra bed?
phrases.notes: ついか (追加, tsuika) = add/additional. Useful for families needing an extra bed or crib.

responses.japanese: はい、ついかりょうきんがかかります
responses.english: Yes, there's an additional fee
responses.listen_for: ついかりょうきん (追加料金, tsuika ryoukin) = additional fee.
responses.kanji: はい、追加料金がかかります

responses.japanese: ベビーベッドもごよういできます
responses.english: We can also prepare a baby crib
responses.listen_for: ベビーベッド (bebii beddo) = baby crib.
responses.kanji: ベビーベッドもご用意できます

phrases.kanji: ベッドを追加できますか？

phrases.japanese: たかいかいのへやをおねがいします
phrases.romaji: Takai kai no heya wo onegaishimasu
phrases.english: A room on a high floor, please
phrases.notes: Useful if you want a view or to avoid street noise. ひくいかい (低い階, hikui kai) = low floor for the opposite preference.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、たかいかいでごようういたします
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, takai kai de goyoui itashimasu
responses.english: Certainly, I'll prepare a room on a high floor
responses.listen_for: たかいかい (高い階, takai kai) = high floor.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、高い階でご用意いたします

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、ざんねんながらそのかいはまんしつです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, zannen nagara sono kai wa manshitsu desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, unfortunately that floor is fully booked
responses.listen_for: まんしつ (満室, manshitsu) = fully booked.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、残念ながらその階は満室です

phrases.kanji: 高い階の部屋をお願いします

phrases.japanese: へやは、もうつかえますか？
phrases.notes: Situation: you arrive early and the room isn't ready. 部屋 (heya) = room. 使える (tsukaeru) = usable.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ございません、ただいま清掃中です。もうしばらくお待ちください
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen, tadaima seisouchuu desu. Mou shibaraku omachi kudasai
responses.english: I'm sorry, it's being cleaned right now. Please wait a little longer
responses.listen_for: 清掃中 (seisouchuu) = being cleaned. もうしばらく = a little while longer.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございません、ただいま清掃中です。もうしばらくお待ちください

responses.japanese: お荷物は、おあずかりしておきますね
responses.romaji: O-nimotsu wa, o-azukari shite okimasu ne
responses.english: I'll keep your luggage for you
responses.listen_for: あずかる (預かる, azukaru) = to hold / keep for someone.
responses.kanji: お荷物は、お預かりしておきますね

phrases.kanji: 部屋は、もう使えますか？

phrases.japanese: ふとんを、もういっくみいただけますか？
phrases.romaji: Futon wo, mou ikkumi itadakemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could I have one more set of futon bedding?
phrases.notes: Situation: you need extra bedding for a companion. 〜組 (kumi) is the counter for sets of bedding.

responses.japanese: 申し訳ございません、ただいま在庫がございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen, tadaima zaiko ga gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we're out of stock right now
responses.listen_for: 在庫 (zaiko) = stock. ただいま = right now.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございません、ただいま在庫がございません

responses.japanese: あしたまでにごよういできます
responses.english: We can arrange it by tomorrow
responses.listen_for: ご用意 (goyoui) = arranging / preparing something.
responses.kanji: 明日までにご用意できます

phrases.kanji: 布団を、もう一組いただけますか？

phrases.japanese: ちょうしょくは、べつりょうきんですか？
phrases.notes: Situation: you want to know whether breakfast is included before booking or checking in. 別料金 (betsu ryoukin) = separate charge.

responses.japanese: はい、おひとりさまセンゴヒャクえんです
responses.romaji: Hai, ohitori sama sengohyaku en desu
