responses.english: Yes, it's 1,500 yen per person
responses.listen_for: お一人様 (おひとりさま, ohitorisama) = per person.
responses.kanji: はい、お一人様千五百円です

responses.japanese: 朝食付きのプランなら、無料になります
responses.romaji: Choushoku tsuki no puran nara, muryou ni narimasu
responses.english: With the breakfast plan, it's free
responses.listen_for: 付き (tsuki) = including. 無料 (muryou) = free of charge.
responses.kanji: 朝食付きのプランなら、無料になります

phrases.kanji: 朝食は、別料金ですか？

phrases.japanese: カウンターにすわってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kauntaa ni suwatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I sit at the bar counter?
phrases.notes: Sitting at the counter is the move in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ、こちらへ
responses.english: Yes, please, come this way
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please go ahead. こちらへ = this way. You're in.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、カウンターはまんせきです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kauntaa wa manseki desu
responses.english: Sorry, the counter is full
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = full. Ask: テーブルせきはありますか？ (テーブル席はありますか？) (Is there a table?)
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、カウンターは満席です

phrases.kanji: カウンターに座ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: 〇にんでテーブルにすわれますか？
phrases.english: Can ___ of us sit at a table?
phrases.notes: Use this when entering a bar as a group. Some standing bars (立ち飲み/tachinomi) may only have counter seating.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらへどうぞ
responses.english: Yes, this way please
responses.listen_for: Follow them to the table or counter.

responses.japanese: テーブルはしょうしょうおまちいただけますか？
responses.romaji: Teeburu wa shoushou omachi itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you wait a moment for a table?
responses.listen_for: They're clearing a table. Say はい to wait.
responses.kanji: テーブルは少々お待ちいただけますか？

phrases.kanji: 〇人でテーブルに座れますか？

phrases.japanese: おすすめのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Osusume no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have a recommended cocktail?
phrases.notes: This will get you the bartender's best work.

responses.japanese: こんやは〜がおすすめです
responses.english: Tonight I recommend [cocktail]
responses.listen_for: こんや (今夜, konya) = tonight. They'll name the drink. Nod and say それをおねがいします (お願いします).
responses.kanji: 今夜は〜がおすすめです

responses.japanese: どんなおさけがおすきですか？
responses.romaji: Donna osake ga osuki desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of drinks do you like?
responses.listen_for: Great sign — they want to personalize. Describe: のtすぇえt (甘くない, not sweet), フルーツィー (fruity), stろんg (強い, strong), ぃght (軽い, light).
responses.kanji: どんなお酒がお好きですか？

phrases.japanese: ウイスキーのリストをみせてください
phrases.romaji: Uisukii no risuto wo misete kudasai
phrases.english: Can I see the whisky list?
phrases.notes: Japan has incredible domestic whisky.

responses.japanese: こちらがウイスキーリストです
responses.english: Here is our whisky list
responses.listen_for: They'll hand you the list. Take your time — these lists can be extensive.

responses.japanese: こくさんとゆにゅう、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kokusan to yunyuu, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer domestic or imported?
responses.listen_for: こくさん (国産, kokusan) = domestic/Japanese. ゆにゅう (輸入, yunyuu) = imported. You're here for こくさん (国産).
responses.kanji: 国産と輸入、どちらがよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: ウイスキーのリストを見せてください

phrases.japanese: これはどんなあじですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa donna aji desu ka?
phrases.notes: Key flavour words: すぇえt (甘い, sweet), dry (辛口, dry), びってr (苦い, bitter), そうr (酸っぱい, sour), フルーツィー (fruity).

responses.japanese: あまくて、すこしフルーツィーです
responses.english: It's sweet and a little fruity
responses.listen_for: あまい (甘い) = sweet, すこし (少し) = a little, フルーツィー = fruity. Combine these words to understand the profile.
responses.kanji: 甘くて、少しフルーツィーです

responses.japanese: からくちでスモーキーなあじわいです
responses.romaji: Karakuchi de sumoookii na ajiwai desu
responses.english: It has a dry, smoky flavor
responses.listen_for: からくち (辛口, karakuchi) = dry. スモーキー = smoky. あじわい (味わい, ajiwai) = flavor/taste profile.
responses.kanji: 辛口でスモーキーな味わいです

responses.japanese: かんきつけいのかおりとハーブのようなあとあじがあります
responses.romaji: Kankitsu-kei no kaori to haabu no you na ato-aji ga arimasu
responses.english: It has a citrus aroma with an herbal finish
responses.listen_for: かんきつ (柑橘, kankitsu) = citrus. かおり (香り, kaori) = aroma. あとあじ (後味, atoaji) = finish/aftertaste. You're getting a real cocktail description.
responses.kanji: 柑橘系の香りとハーブのような後味があります

phrases.kanji: これはどんな味ですか？

phrases.japanese: もういっぱいおねがいします
phrases.notes: いっぱい (一杯) = one glass/drink.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received. Same again is coming.

responses.japanese: おなじものでよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Onaji mono de yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: The same as before?
responses.listen_for: おなじ (同じ, onaji) = same. They're confirming you want a repeat. Say はい or point to something new on the menu.
responses.kanji: 同じものでよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: もう一杯お願いします

phrases.japanese: あまくないものがすきです
phrases.romaji: Amaku nai mono ga suki desu
phrases.notes: Great for directing the bartender.

responses.japanese: では、〜はいかがですか？
responses.english: Then, how about [cocktail]?
responses.listen_for: では (dewa) = then/in that case. いかが = how about? They're tailoring a recommendation. Say おねがいします (お願いします).

phrases.kanji: 甘くないものが好きです

phrases.japanese: これはなにのベーススピリッツですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nani no beesu supirittsu desu ka?
phrases.english: What is the base spirit in this?
phrases.notes: Shows genuine cocktail knowledge.

responses.japanese: ベースは〜をつかっています
responses.english: The base uses [spirit]
responses.listen_for: つかっています (使っています, tsukatte imasu) = is using. They'll name the spirit. You might also hear じかせい (自家製, jikasei) = house-made.
responses.kanji: ベースは〜を使っています

phrases.kanji: これは何のベーススピリッツですか？

phrases.japanese: にほんのウイスキーをためしてみたいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no uisukii wo tameshite mitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to try a Japanese whisky
phrases.notes: Opens the door to Nikka, Suntory, craft expressions.

responses.japanese: シングルモルトとブレンデッド、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Shinguru moruto to burendeddo, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you prefer single malt or blended?
responses.listen_for: シングルモルト = single malt. ブレンデッド = blended. A real whisky conversation just started.

responses.japanese: ニッカとサントリー、どちらのほうがすきですか？
responses.romaji: Nikka to Santori, dochira no hou ga suki desu ka?
responses.english: Do you prefer Nikka or Suntory?
responses.listen_for: The two big houses. If you don't know yet, say まだいどんtkのwいぇt (わかりません (分かりません), I don't know yet).
responses.kanji: ニッカとサントリー、どちらの方が好きですか？

phrases.kanji: 日本のウイスキーを試してみたいです

phrases.japanese: ハイボールをおねがいします
phrases.notes: Japan's most popular bar drink. Ridiculously well-made.

responses.japanese: ウイスキーはなにになさいますか？
responses.romaji: Uisukii wa nani ni nasaimasu ka?
responses.english: Which whisky would you like?
responses.listen_for: なにになさいますか (何になさいますか) = what will you have? They're asking which whisky for your highball.
responses.kanji: ウイスキーは何になさいますか？

responses.japanese: こさはいかがしますか？
responses.english: How strong would you like it?
responses.listen_for: こさ (濃さ, kosa) = strength/concentration. こいめ (濃いめ, koime) = stronger, うすめ (薄め, usume) = weaker, ふつう (普通, futsuu) = standard.
responses.kanji: 濃さはいかがしますか？

phrases.kanji: ハイボールをお願いします

phrases.japanese: かんぱい！
phrases.notes: Make eye contact with each person as you clink.

responses.japanese: かんぱい！
responses.english: Cheers!
responses.listen_for: They'll echo it back. Make eye contact — not doing so is considered rude.
responses.kanji: 乾杯！

phrases.kanji: 乾杯！

phrases.japanese: ノンアルコールのカクテルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Non-arukooru no kakuteru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Mocktail culture is growing in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、モクテルをごよういしております
responses.romaji: Hai, mokuteru wo go-youi shite orimasu
responses.english: Yes, we have mocktails available
responses.listen_for: モクテル = mocktail. ごようい (ご用意, go-youi) = prepared/available.
responses.kanji: はい、モクテルをご用意しております

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、アルコールのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, arukooru nomi desu
responses.english: Sorry, we only serve alcohol
responses.listen_for: のみ = only. Not every bar does mocktails yet, especially traditional ones.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、アルコールのみです

phrases.japanese: バーテンダーさんはどれくらいこのバーではたらいていますか？
phrases.romaji: Baatendaa-san wa dorekurai kono baa de hataraite imasu ka?
phrases.english: How long have you been working at this bar?
phrases.notes: Great conversation starter. Japanese bartenders train for years.

responses.japanese: 〜ねんになります
responses.english: It's been [X] years
responses.listen_for: ねん (年, nen) = years. A bartender saying 10ねん (年, juunen) / 10 years or more is not unusual.
responses.kanji: 〜年になります

responses.japanese: しゅぎょうは〜ねんしました
responses.english: I trained for [X] years
responses.listen_for: しゅぎょう (修行, shugyou) = training/apprenticeship. This is the craft tradition — they apprenticed under a master.
responses.kanji: 修行は〜年しました

phrases.kanji: バーテンダーさんはどれくらいこのバーで働いていますか？

phrases.japanese: このカクテルのつくりかたをおしえてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kakuteru no tsukurikata wo oshiete moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you tell me how this cocktail is made?
phrases.notes: Japanese bartenders will give you a thorough, proud answer.

responses.japanese: まず〜をつかって、つぎに〜をくわえます
responses.romaji: Mazu [ingredient] wo tsukatte, tsugi ni [ingredient] wo kuwaemasu
responses.english: First I use [ingredient], then I add [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: まず (mazu) = first. つぎに (次に, tsugi ni) = next. くわえます (加えます, kuwaemasu) = add.
responses.kanji: まず〜を使って、次に〜を加えます

phrases.kanji: このカクテルの作り方を教えてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: こんやのスペシャルはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Konya no supesharu wa nan desu ka?
phrases.notes: Seasonal and nightly specials are common.

responses.japanese: こんやは〜をつかったきせつのカクテルです
responses.romaji: Konya wa [ingredient] wo tsukatta kisetsu no kakuteru desu
responses.english: Tonight it's a seasonal cocktail using [ingredient]
responses.listen_for: きせつ (季節, kisetsu) = seasonal. つかった (使った, tsukatta) = using. This is the bartender's creative pick.
responses.kanji: 今夜は〜を使った季節のカクテルです

phrases.kanji: 今夜のスペシャルは何ですか？

phrases.japanese: おみずもいっしょにいただけますか？
phrases.romaji: Omizu mo issho ni itadakemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could I also have some water?
phrases.notes: Stay hydrated — Japanese cocktails are deceptively smooth.

responses.japanese: はい、もちろんです
responses.english: Yes, of course
responses.listen_for: もちろんです = of course. Completely normal to ask.

phrases.kanji: お水も一緒にいただけますか？

phrases.japanese: ふたりぶんおねがいします
phrases.notes: 〜にんぶん (人分, -nin bun) = portions for X people. Useful for sharing plates: ふたりぶん (二人分, futari-bun), さんにんぶん (三人分, san-nin bun).

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received for the group.

phrases.kanji: 二人分お願いします

phrases.japanese: さんにんできました
phrases.notes: 〜にんできました (人で来ました, -nin de kimashita) = we came as a group of X. Useful when a host asks your party size.

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people?
responses.listen_for: Polite way to ask party size — answer with ひとり/ふたり/さんにん (一人/二人/三人) etc.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

responses.japanese: カウンターせきになりますがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kauntaa-seki ni narimasu ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: It will be counter seating, is that okay?
responses.listen_for: Common for small bars when tables don't fit your group size.
responses.kanji: カウンター席になりますがよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 三人で来ました

phrases.japanese: アルコールどすうはどれくらいですか？
phrases.romaji: Arukooru dosuu wa dorekurai desu ka?
phrases.english: How much alcohol content does this have?
phrases.notes: どすう (度数, dosuu) = percentage/proof. Useful before committing to a strong pour.

responses.japanese: やく〜パーセントです
responses.english: It's about [X] percent
responses.listen_for: やく (約, yaku) = approximately. Listen for the number before パーセント.
responses.kanji: 約〜パーセントです

responses.japanese: ウイスキーベースなのですこしつよめです
responses.romaji: Uisukii beesu nanode sukoshi tsuyome desu
responses.english: Since it's whisky-based, it's a bit strong
responses.listen_for: つよめ (強め, tsuyome) = stronger side. Sip slowly.
responses.kanji: ウイスキーベースなので少し強めです

phrases.kanji: アルコール度数はどれくらいですか？

phrases.japanese: あまくちとからくち、どちらがにんきですか？
phrases.romaji: Amakuchi to karakuchi, dochira ga ninki desu ka?
phrases.english: Sweet or dry, which is more popular?
phrases.notes: あまくち (甘口, amakuchi) = sweet/mild, からくち (辛口, karakuchi) = dry. A useful vocabulary pair for describing taste preference.

responses.japanese: さいきんはからくちがにんきです
responses.romaji: Saikin wa karakuchi ga ninki desu
responses.english: Dry has been popular recently
responses.listen_for: さいきん (最近, saikin) = recently.
responses.kanji: 最近は辛口が人気です

responses.japanese: どちらもにんきですが、おきゃくさまのこのみによります
responses.romaji: Dochira mo ninki desu ga, okyakusama no konomi ni yorimasu
responses.english: Both are popular, it depends on the customer's taste
responses.listen_for: このみ (好み, konomi) = preference/taste.
responses.kanji: どちらも人気ですが、お客様の好みによります

phrases.kanji: 甘口と辛口、どちらが人気ですか？

phrases.japanese: ロックでおねがいします
phrases.notes: ロック (rokku) = on the rocks (with ice). Pair with すとれーと (straight/neat) or みずわり (水割り, mizuwari) / cut with water.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました
responses.english: Certainly
responses.listen_for: Order received.

responses.japanese: こおりはおおめ、すくなめ、どちらがいいですか？
responses.romaji: Koori wa oome, sukuname, dochira ga ii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like more ice or less?
responses.listen_for: おおめ (多め, oome) = more. すくなめ (少なめ, sukuname) = less.
responses.kanji: 氷は多め、少なめ、どちらがいいですか？

phrases.kanji: ロックでお願いします

phrases.japanese: みずわりでおねがいします
phrases.notes: みずわり (水割り, mizuwari) = whisky cut with still water, the classic Japanese way to drink whisky long and easy.

responses.japanese: のうどはどうされますか？
responses.english: How would you like the concentration?
responses.listen_for: のうど (濃度, noudo) = concentration/strength.
responses.kanji: 濃度はどうされますか？

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、すこしうすめにつくりますね
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, sukoshi usume ni tsukurimasu ne
responses.english: Certainly, I'll make it a little weaker
responses.listen_for: うすめ (薄め, usume) = weaker/diluted side.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、少し薄めに作りますね

phrases.kanji: 水割りでお願いします

phrases.japanese: ピートこうがつよいものはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Piito kou ga tsuyoi mono wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have something with a strong peat aroma?
phrases.notes: ピートこう (ピート香, piito kou) = peat aroma, a common descriptor for Islay-style smoky whisky.

responses.japanese: はい、とてもスモーキーなめいがらがございます
responses.romaji: Hai, totemo sumookii na meigara ga gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, we have a very smoky brand
responses.listen_for: めいがら (銘柄, meigara) = brand/label name.
responses.kanji: はい、とてもスモーキーな銘柄がございます

responses.japanese: アイラのものがおすすめです
responses.romaji: Aira no mono ga osusume desu
responses.english: I'd recommend something from Islay
responses.listen_for: アイラ (Aira) = Islay, the Scottish island famous for peaty whisky.

phrases.kanji: ピート香が強いものはありますか？

phrases.japanese: じゅくせいねんすうはどれくらいですか？
phrases.romaji: Jukusei nensuu wa dorekurai desu ka?
phrases.english: How many years has this been aged?
phrases.notes: じゅくせいねんすう (熟成年数, jukusei nensuu) = number of years aged — key vocabulary for whisky and shochu connoisseurs.

responses.japanese: 〜ねんじゅくせいです
responses.english: It's aged [X] years
responses.listen_for: ねん (年, nen) = years. Listen for the number right before it.
responses.kanji: 〜年熟成です

responses.japanese: ねんすうひょうじのないノンエイジものです
responses.romaji: Nensuu hyouji no nai non-eiji mono desu
responses.english: It's a no-age-statement (NAS) release
responses.listen_for: ねんすうひょうじ (年数表示, nensuu hyouji) = age statement. ノンエイジ = no-age-statement.
responses.kanji: 年数表示のないノンエイジものです

phrases.kanji: 熟成年数はどれくらいですか？

phrases.japanese: このおつまみはおさけにあいますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono otsumami wa osake ni aimasu ka?
phrases.english: Does this snack pair well with the drink?
phrases.notes: おつまみ (otsumami) = small bar snacks meant to accompany alcohol.

responses.japanese: はい、とてもあいますよ
responses.english: Yes, it pairs really well
responses.listen_for: あいます (合います, aimasu) = goes well with/matches.
responses.kanji: はい、とても合いますよ

responses.japanese: からいおつまみのほうがあうとおもいます
responses.romaji: Karai otsumami no hou ga au to omoimasu
responses.english: I think a spicier snack would pair better
responses.listen_for: からい (辛い, karai) = spicy.
responses.kanji: 辛いおつまみの方が合うと思います

phrases.kanji: このおつまみはお酒に合いますか？

phrases.japanese: すこしつよめにつくってもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Sukoshi tsuyome ni tsukutte moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you make it a bit stronger?
phrases.notes: つよめ (強め, tsuyome) = stronger/more concentrated; the opposite is うすめ (薄め, usume) = weaker.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、つよめでつくりますね
responses.english: Certainly, I'll make it strong
responses.listen_for: Order noted — expect a stiffer pour.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、強めで作りますね

responses.japanese: どのくらいつよめがごのみですか？
responses.romaji: Dono kurai tsuyome ga gonomi desu ka?
responses.english: About how strong would you prefer?
responses.listen_for: ごのみ (お好み, gonomi) = preference. Describe how strong you'd like it.
responses.kanji: どのくらい強めがお好みですか？

phrases.kanji: 少し強めに作ってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: そのカクテルは、売り切れですか？
phrases.romaji: Sono kakuteru wa, urikire desu ka?
phrases.notes: Situation: the cocktail or spirit on the menu has run out for the night. Ask for a recommendation to replace it.

responses.japanese: はい、申し訳ございません。本日は終わってしまいました
responses.romaji: Hai, moushiwake gozaimasen. Honjitsu wa owatte shimaimashita
responses.english: Yes, I'm sorry. We've run out for today
responses.listen_for: 終わってしまいました (owatte shimaimashita) = has run out (てしまう = unfortunately).
responses.kanji: はい、申し訳ございません。本日は終わってしまいました

responses.japanese: かわりに、こちらはいかがですか？
responses.romaji: Kawari ni, kochira wa ikaga desu ka?
responses.english: How about this one instead?
responses.listen_for: かわりに (代わりに, kawari ni) = instead. こちら = this one (they'll point to an alternative).
responses.kanji: 代わりに、こちらはいかがですか？

phrases.kanji: そのカクテルは、売り切れですか？

phrases.japanese: 〜にいきたいんですが
phrases.notes: The んですが softens it into a request.

responses.japanese: ここからあるいて〜ぶんぐらいです
responses.romaji: Koko kara aruite [X] fun gurai desu
responses.english: It's about [X] minutes walk from here
responses.listen_for: あるいて (歩いて, aruite) = walking. ふん (分) = minutes. ぐらい = about/approximately.
responses.kanji: ここから歩いて〜分ぐらいです

responses.japanese: でんしゃでいったほうがいいですよ
responses.romaji: Densha de itta hou ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's better to go by train
responses.listen_for: でんしゃ (電車, densha) = train. ほうがいい (方がいい) = better to. They're steering you to public transport.
responses.kanji: 電車で行った方がいいですよ

phrases.kanji: 〜に行きたいんですが

phrases.japanese: まっすぐいってください
phrases.notes: Key direction words: まっすぐ/みぎ/ひだり (右/左).

responses.japanese: 〜メートルさきに〜があります
responses.english: [X] meters ahead there is [landmark]
responses.listen_for: メートル = meters. さき (先, saki) = ahead. They're giving you a landmark to aim for.
responses.kanji: 〜メートル先に〜があります

phrases.kanji: まっすぐ行ってください

phrases.japanese: ここからとおいですか？
phrases.notes: ちかいです (近いです, chikai desu) = it is close.

responses.japanese: いいえ、ちかいですよ。あるいて〜ふんです
responses.romaji: Iie, chikai desu yo. Aruite [X] fun desu
responses.english: No, it's close. [X] minutes on foot
responses.listen_for: ちかい (近い, chikai) = close/nearby. あるいて (歩いて) = walking. The number before ふん (分) is your walk time.
responses.kanji: いいえ、近いですよ。歩いて〜分です

responses.japanese: すこしとおいです。バスかでんしゃがいいですよ
responses.romaji: Sukoshi tooi desu. Basu ka densha ga ii desu yo
responses.english: It's a bit far. Bus or train would be better
responses.listen_for: すこしとおい (少し遠い, sukoshi tooi) = a bit far. か = or. They're recommending transport.
responses.kanji: 少し遠いです。バスか電車がいいですよ

phrases.kanji: ここから遠いですか？

phrases.japanese: ちずをえがいてもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you draw me a map?
phrases.notes: Japanese people are incredibly helpful — many will walk you there.

responses.japanese: はい、ちょっとまってください
responses.english: Yes, please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: ちょっとまってください (ちょっと待ってください) = wait a moment. They're grabbing a pen or phone.
responses.kanji: はい、ちょっと待ってください

responses.japanese: いっしょにいきましょうか？
responses.english: Shall we go together?
responses.listen_for: いっしょに (一緒に, issho ni) = together. いきましょうか (行きましょうか) = shall we go? They're offering to escort you. Say ありがとうございます!
responses.kanji: 一緒に行きましょうか？

phrases.kanji: 地図を描いてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: トイレはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Japanese public toilets are world-class.

responses.japanese: あちらです
responses.english: It's over there
responses.listen_for: あちら = over there. They'll point. Follow the direction.

responses.japanese: 〜かいにございます
responses.english: It's on floor [X]
responses.listen_for: かい (階, kai) = floor. In department stores toilets are often on a specific floor.
responses.kanji: 〜階にございます

phrases.japanese: たすけてください！
phrases.notes: Loud and clear. People will respond.

responses.japanese: どうしましたか？
responses.english: What happened?
responses.listen_for: どうしましたか = what's wrong / what happened? Be ready to point or show a translation.

phrases.kanji: 助けてください！

phrases.japanese: きゅうきゅうしゃをよんでください
phrases.notes: Emergency numbers: 119 (ambulance/fire), 110 (police).

responses.japanese: すぐによびます
responses.english: I'll call right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ = immediately. Help is being called.
responses.kanji: すぐに呼びます

phrases.kanji: 救急車を呼んでください

phrases.japanese: パスポートをなくしました
phrases.notes: Go to the nearest こうばん (交番, koban) / police box first.

responses.japanese: こうばんにいってください
responses.english: Please go to the police box
responses.listen_for: こうばん (交番, kouban) = small police box/koban. These are everywhere in Japan and very helpful.
responses.kanji: 交番に行ってください

responses.japanese: いつ、どこでなくしましたか？
responses.english: When and where did you lose it?
responses.listen_for: いつ = when. どこ = where. Answer as best you can.

phrases.japanese: ぐあいがわるいです
phrases.notes: いたい (痛い, itai) = it hurts. Point at where.

responses.japanese: どこがいたいですか？
responses.english: Where does it hurt?
responses.listen_for: どこ = where. いたい (痛い) = hurt/pain. Point at the affected area.
responses.kanji: どこが痛いですか？

responses.japanese: びょういんにいったほうがいいです
responses.romaji: Byouin ni itta hou ga ii desu
responses.english: You should go to a hospital
responses.listen_for: びょういん (病院, byouin) = hospital. ほうがいい (方がいい) = should/better to.
responses.kanji: 病院に行った方がいいです

phrases.kanji: 具合が悪いです

phrases.japanese: たいしかんにでんわしてください
phrases.notes: Know your country's embassy number before you go.

responses.japanese: わかりました。どこのくにですか？
responses.romaji: Wakarimashita. Doko no kuni desu ka?
responses.english: Understood. Which country?
responses.listen_for: どこのどこのくに (国, doko no kuni) = which country. State your country clearly.
responses.kanji: 分かりました。どこの国ですか？

phrases.kanji: 大使館に電話してください

phrases.japanese: どろぼうです！
phrases.notes: 泥棒 (dorobou) = thief. The police number is 110 (ひゃくとおばん).

responses.japanese: けいさつをよびます
responses.english: I'll call the police
responses.listen_for: 呼ぶ (yobu) = to call.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですか？
responses.english: Are you okay?
responses.listen_for: 大丈夫 (daijoubu) = okay / alright.

phrases.japanese: かじです！
phrases.notes: 火事 (kaji) = fire. The fire and ambulance number is 119 (ひゃくじゅうきゅうばん).

responses.japanese: ひゃくじゅうきゅうばんにでんわします
responses.english: I'll call 119
responses.listen_for: 119 = fire and ambulance number.

responses.japanese: にげてください！
responses.english: Please evacuate!
responses.listen_for: 逃げる (nigeru) = to run away / escape.

phrases.japanese: じしんです！
phrases.notes: 地震 (jishin) = earthquake. Stay away from windows and get under a sturdy table or door frame.

responses.japanese: たいへんです、ひなんしてください
responses.english: It's dangerous, please evacuate
responses.listen_for: 避難 (hinan) = evacuation.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶです、もうおさまりました
responses.english: It's okay, it has stopped
responses.listen_for: おさまる (収まる) = to settle down / stop.

phrases.japanese: ひなんじょはどこですか？
phrases.notes: 避難所 (hinanjo) = evacuation shelter. Look for signs with a green or white symbol.

responses.japanese: あちらのこうえんです
responses.english: It's the park over there
responses.listen_for: 公園 (kouen) = park.

responses.japanese: ついてきてください
responses.english: Please follow me
responses.listen_for: ついてくる = to follow.

phrases.japanese: けがをしました
phrases.notes: 怪我 (kega) = injury. 痛い (itai) = it hurts.

responses.japanese: どこをけがしましたか？
responses.english: Where are you injured?
responses.listen_for: どこ = where.

responses.japanese: すぐに救急車をよびます
responses.english: I'll call an ambulance right away
responses.listen_for: 救急車 (kyuukyuusha) = ambulance.

phrases.japanese: おいしゃさんをよんでください
phrases.notes: 医者 (isha) = doctor. 病院 (byouin) = hospital.

responses.japanese: すぐにおいしゃさんをよびます
responses.english: I'll call a doctor right away
responses.listen_for: お医者さん = doctor (polite).

responses.japanese: びょういんにいきましょう
responses.english: Let's go to the hospital
responses.listen_for: 病院 (byouin) = hospital.

phrases.japanese: たおれました。たすけてください
phrases.notes: 倒れる (taoreru) = to collapse. Call for help first, then check breathing.

responses.japanese: えーいーでぃーをもってきてください
responses.english: Please bring the AED
responses.listen_for: AED = automated external defibrillator (heart defibrillator).

responses.japanese: きゅうきゅうしゃをよびました
responses.english: We've called an ambulance
responses.listen_for: 呼びました (yobimashita) = called (past tense).

phrases.japanese: でんわがつながりません
phrases.notes: つながる (繋がる) = to connect. Tourist information centers can help when you have no phone signal.

responses.japanese: こうしゅうでんわがありますよ
responses.english: There's a public phone
responses.listen_for: 公衆電話 (koushuu denwa) = public phone.

responses.japanese: かんこうあんないじょでたすけてもらえます
responses.english: The tourist information center can help you
responses.listen_for: 観光案内所 (kankou annaijo) = tourist information center.

phrases.japanese: スマートフォンをなくしました
phrases.notes: なくす (無くす) = to lose. Report lost items to the police box (交番) or the police.

responses.japanese: こうばんにいってください
responses.english: Please go to the police box
responses.listen_for: 交番 (kouban) = small local police box.

responses.japanese: おまわりさんにきいてください
responses.english: Please ask a police officer
responses.listen_for: お巡りさん (omawarisan) = police officer (friendly).

phrases.japanese: くるまがぶつかりました
phrases.english: I've been in a car accident
phrases.notes: 事故 (jiko) = accident. 交通事故 (koutsuu jiko) = traffic accident.

responses.japanese: けがはありませんか？
responses.english: Are you hurt?
responses.listen_for: けが = injury.

responses.japanese: けいさつにれんらくしてください
responses.english: Please contact the police
responses.listen_for: 連絡 (renraku) = contact.

phrases.japanese: みちにまよいました
phrases.notes: A good opener if you approach a police box (こうばん, 交番, kouban) for directions.

responses.japanese: どちらへいきたいですか？
responses.english: Where would you like to go?
responses.listen_for: どちら (dochira) = where (polite). Name your destination.
responses.kanji: どちらへ行きたいですか？

responses.japanese: ちずでおしえますね
responses.english: I'll show you on a map
responses.listen_for: ちず (地図, chizu) = map.
responses.kanji: 地図で教えますね

phrases.kanji: 道に迷いました

phrases.japanese: さいふをぬすまれました
phrases.notes: Report to the nearest こうばん (交番, kouban) as soon as possible — needed for insurance and embassy support.

responses.japanese: いつ、どこでなくなりましたか？
responses.english: When and where did it go missing?
responses.listen_for: いつ = when. どこ = where.
responses.kanji: いつ、どこで無くなりましたか？

responses.japanese: ひがいとどけをさくせいします
responses.english: We'll file a damage/theft report
responses.listen_for: ひがいとどけ (被害届, higai todoke) = police damage/incident report.
responses.kanji: 被害届を作成します

phrases.kanji: 財布を盗まれました

phrases.japanese: じこにあいました
phrases.notes: For traffic accidents, also call 110 (police) and 119 (ambulance) if anyone is injured.

responses.japanese: けがはありませんか？
responses.english: Are you injured?
responses.listen_for: けが (怪我, kega) = injury.
responses.kanji: 怪我はありませんか？

responses.japanese: あいてのかたのれんらくさきをおしえてください
responses.romaji: Aite no kata no renrakusaki wo oshiete kudasai
responses.english: Please tell me the other party's contact information
responses.listen_for: れんらくさき (連絡先, renrakusaki) = contact information.
responses.kanji: 相手の方の連絡先を教えてください

phrases.kanji: 事故にあいました

phrases.japanese: パスポートをみせます
phrases.notes: Foreign visitors are legally required to carry passport ID in Japan — always keep it on you.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます、かくにんさせていただきます
responses.english: Thank you, I'll go ahead and confirm it
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check.
responses.kanji: ありがとうございます、確認させていただきます

responses.japanese: たいざいきかんをおしえてください
responses.english: Please tell me your length of stay
responses.listen_for: たいざいきかん (滞在期間, taizai kikan) = duration of stay.
responses.kanji: 滞在期間を教えてください

phrases.kanji: パスポートを見せます

phrases.japanese: なにもわるいことはしていません
phrases.romaji: Nani mo warui koto wa shite imasen
phrases.notes: Stay calm and polite — this phrase asserts your position without sounding confrontational.

responses.japanese: わかりました、いくつかしつもんさせてください
responses.english: Understood, let me ask a few questions
responses.listen_for: しつもん (質問, shitsumon) = question.
responses.kanji: 分かりました、いくつか質問させてください

responses.japanese: かくにんのためのしつもんです
responses.romaji: Kakunin no tame no shitsumon desu
responses.english: These are just confirmation questions
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirmation — routine, not an accusation.
responses.kanji: 確認のための質問です

phrases.kanji: 何も悪いことはしていません

phrases.japanese: つうやくをよんでもらえますか？
phrases.notes: Police stations can usually arrange phone interpretation services for English and other languages.

responses.japanese: はい、でんわつうやくをてはいします
responses.romaji: Hai, denwa tsuuyaku wo tehai shimasu
responses.english: Yes, I'll arrange phone interpretation
responses.listen_for: てはい (手配, tehai) = arrange.
responses.kanji: はい、電話通訳を手配します

responses.japanese: なにごがひつようですか？
responses.english: Which language do you need?
responses.listen_for: なにご (何語, nanigo) = which language.
responses.kanji: 何語が必要ですか？

phrases.kanji: 通訳を呼んでもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: これはなんのばっきんですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nan no bakkin desu ka?
phrases.notes: ばっきん (罰金, bakkin) = fine/penalty — a common question for minor traffic or bicycle violations.

responses.japanese: ちゅうりんいはんのばっきんです
responses.english: It's a fine for illegal bicycle parking
responses.listen_for: いはん (違反, ihan) = violation.
responses.kanji: 駐輪違反の罰金です

responses.japanese: しょうさいはこのしょるいにかいてあります
responses.romaji: Shousai wa kono shorui ni kaite arimasu
responses.english: The details are written on this document
responses.listen_for: しょるい (書類, shorui) = document/paperwork.
responses.kanji: 詳細はこの書類に書いてあります

phrases.kanji: これは何の罰金ですか？

phrases.japanese: こうばんはどこですか？
phrases.notes: こうばん (交番, kouban) = small neighborhood police box, found on almost every major street corner — the easiest place to ask for help.

responses.japanese: つぎのかどにございます
responses.english: It's at the next corner
responses.listen_for: かど (角, kado) = corner.
responses.kanji: 次の角にございます

responses.japanese: えきのまえにこうばんがあります
responses.romaji: Eki no mae ni kouban ga arimasu
responses.english: There's a police box in front of the station
responses.listen_for: まえ (前, mae) = in front of.
responses.kanji: 駅の前に交番があります

phrases.kanji: 交番はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: おとしものをとどけたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to turn in a lost item
phrases.notes: Japan has a strong lost-and-found culture — turning items in at a こうばん (交番, kouban) is normal and expected.

responses.japanese: どこでひろいましたか？
responses.english: Where did you find it?
responses.listen_for: ひろいました (拾いました, hiroimashita) = found/picked up.
responses.kanji: どこで拾いましたか？

responses.japanese: こちらのようしにごきにゅうください
responses.romaji: Kochira no youshi ni gokinyuu kudasai
responses.english: Please fill out this form
responses.listen_for: ようし (用紙, youshi) = form/paper.
responses.kanji: こちらの用紙にご記入ください

phrases.kanji: 落とし物を届けたいです

phrases.japanese: いち、に、さん、よん、ご、ろく、なな、はち、きゅう、じゅう
phrases.romaji: Ichi, ni, san, shi, go, roku, nana, hachi, kyuu, juu
phrases.notes: 100 = ひゃく (百, hyaku), 1000 = せん (千, sen), 10000 = まん (万, man).

responses.japanese: 〜えんです
responses.english: [amount] yen
responses.listen_for: Numbers you need most: ひゃく (百, 100), せん (千, 1000), まん (万, 10,000). Most prices fall between 500–5000.
responses.kanji: 〜円です

phrases.kanji: 一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九、十

phrases.japanese: にんずうのかぞえかた
phrases.english: How to count people — the essential counters
phrases.notes: Japanese uses special words for counting people. 1 and 2 are irregular; from 3 onward, use number + にん (人, nin). Formal contexts (hotels, restaurants) use めい (名, mei) instead of にん (人). ひとり/いちめい (一人/一名, hitori/ichimei) = one, ふたり/にめい (二人/二名, futari/nimei) = two, さんにん/さんめい (三人/三名, san-nin/sanmei) = three — にん (人) is everyday, めい (名) is formal (hotel/restaurant).

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people? (polite — what staff will ask)
responses.listen_for: なんめいさま (何名様, nanmei-sama) is the question that prompts you to answer with one of these counters. Hold up fingers as you answer.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

responses.japanese: なんにんですか？
responses.english: How many people? (casual)
responses.listen_for: The everyday version of the same question, using にん (人) instead of the formal めい (名).
responses.kanji: 何人ですか？

phrases.kanji: 人数の数え方

phrases.japanese: なんじですか？
phrases.notes: じ (時, ji) = o'clock, ふん (分, fun) = minutes.

responses.japanese: 〜じ〜ふんです
responses.english: It is [hour]:[minutes]
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before ほうr (時, hour) and before みぬてs (分, minutes). E.g., 3さんじはん (時半, sanji han) = 3:30.
responses.kanji: 〜時〜分です

phrases.kanji: 何時ですか？

phrases.japanese: 〜じによやくがあります
phrases.notes: Useful when arriving at a restaurant or hotel.

responses.japanese: おなまえをおねがいします
responses.english: Your name please
responses.listen_for: おなまえ (お名前, onamae) = name. Say your name clearly or show it written.
responses.kanji: お名前をお願いします

phrases.kanji: 〜時に予約があります

phrases.japanese: ひとり、ふたり、さんにん
phrases.english: One person, two people, three people
phrases.notes: The people-counter にん (人, nin) is irregular for 1 and 2: ひとり (一人, hitori), ふたり (二人, futari). From three onward it's regular: さんにん (三人, san-nin), よにん (四人, yo-nin), ごにん (五人, go-nin). Staff use the polite form 〜めいさま (名様, -mei-sama) instead, e.g. おひとりさま (お一人様, o-hitori-sama).

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people (polite)?
responses.listen_for: Answer with ひとり/ふたり/さんにん (一人/二人/三人) etc., or just hold up fingers.
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

phrases.kanji: 一人、二人、三人

phrases.japanese: ひとつ、ふたつ、みっつ
phrases.notes: The generic item-counter つ (tsu) is used for food orders, souvenirs, and other countable objects when you don't know the specific counter: ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ, よっつ, いつつ (一つ, 二つ, 三つ, 四つ, 五つ)... It stops being used after とお (十, too) = 10.

responses.japanese: いくつになさいますか？
responses.english: How many would you like?
responses.listen_for: いくつ (ikutsu) = how many — answer with ひとつ/ふたつ/みっつ (一つ/二つ/三つ).

phrases.kanji: 一つ、二つ、三つ

phrases.japanese: なんじにひらきますか？
phrases.notes: 開く (hiraku) = to open. 営業時間 (eigyou jikan) = opening hours.

responses.japanese: ごぜんじゅうじにひらきます
responses.english: We open at 10 AM
responses.listen_for: 午前 (gozen) = AM. 十時 (juuji) = 10 o'clock.

responses.japanese: じゅうじからです
responses.english: From 10 o'clock
responses.listen_for: 〜から = from.

phrases.japanese: なんじにしまりますか？
phrases.notes: 閉まる (shimaru) = to close. Some shops close before the posted time if business is slow.

responses.japanese: よるくじにしまります
responses.english: We close at 9 PM
responses.listen_for: 夜 (yoru) = evening / night. 九時 (kuji) = 9 o'clock.

responses.japanese: ラストオーダーはくじはんです
responses.romaji: Rasuto oodaa wa kuji han desu
responses.english: Last order is at 9:30
responses.listen_for: 半 (han) = half past.

phrases.japanese: いま、えいぎょうしていますか？
phrases.notes: 営業 (eigyou) = open for business. 今 (ima) = now.

responses.japanese: はい、やっています
responses.english: Yes, we're open
responses.listen_for: やっている = is open (casual).

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、いまはしまっています
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, ima wa shimatte imasu
responses.english: Sorry, we're closed right now
responses.listen_for: しまっている = is closed.

phrases.japanese: まだあいていますか？
phrases.notes: まだ (mada) = still. あいている (開いている) = is open.

responses.japanese: はい、あと三十分はやっています
responses.romaji: Hai, ato sanjuppun wa yatte imasu
responses.english: Yes, we're open for another 30 minutes
responses.listen_for: あと = remaining. 三十分 (sanjuppun) = 30 minutes.

responses.japanese: もうすぐしめます
responses.english: We're closing soon
responses.listen_for: もうすぐ = soon. しめます (閉めます) = we close (we shut it).

phrases.japanese: あしたもえいぎょうしていますか？
phrases.romaji: Ashita mo eigyou shite imasu ka?
phrases.notes: 明日 (ashita) = tomorrow. も = too.

responses.japanese: はい、あしたもやっています
responses.english: Yes, we're open tomorrow too
responses.listen_for: 明日 (ashita) = tomorrow.

responses.japanese: あしたはおやすみです
responses.english: We're closed tomorrow
responses.listen_for: お休み (oyasumi) = closed / day off.

phrases.japanese: にちようびはおやすみですか？
phrases.notes: お休み (oyasumi) = closed / day off. Many shops close one day a week.

responses.japanese: はい、にちようびはおやすみです
responses.english: Yes, we're closed on Sundays
responses.listen_for: 日曜日 (nichiyoubi) = Sunday.

responses.japanese: いいえ、まいにちあいています
responses.english: No, we're open every day
responses.listen_for: 毎日 (mainichi) = every day.

phrases.japanese: またあしたきてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Mata ashita kite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: 来る (kuru) = to come. また = again.

responses.japanese: はい、おまちしております
responses.english: Yes, we'll be waiting for you
responses.listen_for: お待ちしております = we look forward to seeing you (polite).

responses.japanese: ぜひまたどうぞ
responses.english: Please do come back
responses.listen_for: ぜひ = by all means.

phrases.japanese: なんじにまたくればいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Nanji ni mata kureba ii desu ka?
phrases.english: What time should I come back?
phrases.notes: 〜ればいいですか = should I ...? Use this to ask for a suggested time.

responses.japanese: はちじいこうでしたら、いつでもどうぞ
responses.romaji: Hachiji ikou deshitara, itsu demo douzo
responses.english: After 8 o'clock, any time is fine
responses.listen_for: 以降 (ikou) = from that time onward.

responses.japanese: じゅうじごろがおすすめです
responses.english: Around 10 o'clock is best
responses.listen_for: ごろ (頃) = around. おすすめ = recommended.

phrases.japanese: もうしまっていますか？
phrases.notes: もう = already.

responses.japanese: はい、もうへいてんしました
responses.english: Yes, we've already closed
responses.listen_for: 閉店 (heiten) = closed for business.

responses.japanese: まだ、あとじゅっぷんあります
responses.english: Not yet, there are ten more minutes
responses.listen_for: まだ = not yet. あと = remaining.

phrases.japanese: どのくらいかかりますか？
phrases.notes: かかる = to take (time). Use it for waits, trips, and treatments.

responses.japanese: およそじゅうごふんです
responses.english: About 15 minutes
responses.listen_for: およそ = approximately. 十五分 (juugofun) = 15 minutes.

responses.japanese: いちじかんほどかかります
responses.english: It takes about an hour
responses.listen_for: 一時間 (ichijikan) = one hour.

phrases.japanese: さいごのでんしゃは、なんじですか？
phrases.romaji: Saigo no densha wa, nanji desu ka?
phrases.english: What time is the last train?
phrases.notes: 最後 (saigo) = last. 電車 (densha) = train.

responses.japanese: じゅういちじごじゅうごふんです
responses.english: It's 11:55 PM
responses.listen_for: 時 (ji) = o'clock. 分 (fun) = minutes.

responses.japanese: えきのじこくひょうでかくにんできます
responses.romaji: Eki no jikokuhyou de kakunin dekimasu
responses.english: You can check the timetable at the station
responses.listen_for: 時刻表 (jikokuhyou) = timetable.

phrases.japanese: じゅうじごろにまたきます
phrases.notes: ごろ (頃) = around. Use it when you don't need an exact time.

responses.japanese: わかりました、おまちしております
responses.english: Understood, we'll be waiting
responses.listen_for: わかりました = understood (polite).

responses.japanese: そのじかんは、もうよやくがいっぱいです
responses.romaji: Sono jikan wa, mou yoyaku ga ippai desu
responses.english: That time is already fully booked
responses.listen_for: 予約 (yoyaku) = reservation. いっぱい = full.

phrases.japanese: いつからいつまでですか？
phrases.romaji: Itsu kara itsu made desu ka?
phrases.notes: 〜から = from. 〜まで = until.

responses.japanese: ごぜんくじからごごろくじまでです
responses.romaji: Gozen kuji kara gogo rokuji made desu
responses.english: From 9 AM until 6 PM
responses.listen_for: 午後 (gogo) = PM. から = from. まで = until.

responses.japanese: どようびとにちようびは、じゅうじからです
responses.romaji: Doyoubi to nichiyoubi wa, juuji kara desu
responses.english: On Saturdays and Sundays, it's from 10 AM
responses.listen_for: 土曜日 (doyoubi) = Saturday. 日曜日 (nichiyoubi) = Sunday.

phrases.japanese: きょうはなんようびですか？
phrases.english: What day of the week is it today?
phrases.notes: 曜日 (youbi) = day of the week. Days: 月 (getsu), 火 (ka), 水 (sui), 木 (moku), 金 (kin), 土 (do), 日 (nichi).

responses.japanese: きょうはきんようびです
responses.english: Today is Friday
responses.listen_for: 金曜日 (kinyoubi) = Friday.

responses.japanese: あしたはどようびです
responses.english: Tomorrow is Saturday
responses.listen_for: 土曜日 (doyoubi) = Saturday.

phrases.japanese: げつようびはおやすみですか？
phrases.notes: 月曜日 (getsuyoubi) = Monday.

responses.japanese: はい、げつようびはおやすみです
responses.english: Yes, we're closed on Mondays
responses.listen_for: お休み = closed.

responses.japanese: いいえ、げつようびもあいています
responses.english: No, we're open on Mondays too
responses.listen_for: 〜も = too.

phrases.japanese: きょうはやっていますか？
phrases.notes: 今日 (kyou) = today.

responses.japanese: はい、きょうはじゅうじからです
responses.romaji: Hai, kyou wa juuji kara desu
responses.english: Yes, today it's from 10 AM
responses.listen_for: 今日 (kyou) = today.

responses.japanese: きょうはりんじきゅうぎょうです
responses.english: We're temporarily closed today
responses.listen_for: 臨時 (rinji) = temporary. 休業 (kyuugyou) = closed for business.

phrases.japanese: あした、またきます
phrases.notes: 明日 (ashita) = tomorrow.

responses.japanese: はい、あしたおまちしています
responses.english: Yes, we'll be waiting for you tomorrow
responses.listen_for: お待ちしています = we'll be waiting.

responses.japanese: あさってでもだいじょうぶですよ
responses.english: The day after tomorrow is fine too
responses.listen_for: 明後日 (asatte) = the day after tomorrow.

phrases.japanese: あさって、またきます
phrases.english: I'll come back the day after tomorrow
phrases.notes: 明後日 (asatte) = the day after tomorrow.

responses.japanese: はい、あさってまでにごよういしておきます
responses.romaji: Hai, asatte made ni go-youi shite okimasu
responses.english: Yes, we'll have it ready by the day after tomorrow
responses.listen_for: 用意 (youi) = preparation.

responses.japanese: あさっては、おやすみです
responses.english: We're closed the day after tomorrow
responses.listen_for: お休み = closed.

phrases.japanese: きのうはやっていましたか？
phrases.notes: 昨日 (kinou) = yesterday.

responses.japanese: はい、きのうはじゅうじからはちじまでやっていました
responses.romaji: Hai, kinou wa juuji kara hachiji made yatte imashita
responses.english: Yes, yesterday we were open from 10 to 8
responses.listen_for: 昨日 (kinou) = yesterday.

responses.japanese: いいえ、きのうはおやすみでした
responses.english: No, we were closed yesterday
responses.listen_for: でした = past tense.

phrases.japanese: しゅうまつはやっていますか？
phrases.english: Are you open on the weekend?
phrases.notes: 週末 (shuumatsu) = weekend.

responses.japanese: はい、どようびとにちようびもあいています
responses.romaji: Hai, doyoubi to nichiyoubi mo aite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we're open on Saturday and Sunday too
responses.listen_for: 土曜日 (doyoubi) = Saturday. 日曜日 (nichiyoubi) = Sunday.

responses.japanese: しゅうまつはこんでいます
responses.english: It's busy on weekends
responses.listen_for: 混む (komu) = to be crowded.

phrases.japanese: しゅくじつはやっていますか？
phrases.english: Are you open on public holidays?
phrases.notes: 祝日 (shukujitsu) = public holiday. Many shops close or change their hours on these days.

responses.japanese: はい、しゅくじつもあけています
responses.english: Yes, we're open on public holidays
responses.listen_for: あける (開ける) = to be open (for business).

responses.japanese: しゅくじつはおやすみになります
responses.english: We're closed on public holidays
responses.listen_for: なります = is (polite).

phrases.japanese: らいしゅうもやっていますか？
phrases.english: Will you be open next week too?
phrases.notes: 来週 (raishuu) = next week.

responses.japanese: はい、らいしゅうもやっています
responses.english: Yes, we'll be open next week too
responses.listen_for: 来週 (raishuu) = next week.

responses.japanese: らいしゅうはきゅうぎょうびがあります
responses.english: We have a closing day next week
responses.listen_for: 休業日 (kyuugyoubi) = closing day.

phrases.japanese: まいにちあいていますか？
phrases.notes: 毎日 (mainichi) = every day.

responses.japanese: はい、まいにちあいています
responses.english: Yes, we're open every day
responses.listen_for: 毎日 = every day.

responses.japanese: いいえ、げつようびはおやすみです
responses.english: No, we're closed on Mondays
responses.listen_for: 月曜日 = Monday.

phrases.japanese: なんようびがおやすみですか？
phrases.notes: 何曜日 (nanyoubi) = which day of the week.

responses.japanese: すいようびがおやすみです
responses.english: We're closed on Wednesdays
responses.listen_for: 水曜日 (suiyoubi) = Wednesday.

responses.japanese: まいしゅうもくようびがおやすみです
responses.english: We're closed every Thursday
responses.listen_for: 毎週 (maishuu) = every week. 木曜日 (mokuyoubi) = Thursday.

phrases.japanese: きょうはなんがつなんにちですか？
phrases.romaji: Kyou wa nangatsu nannichi desu ka?
phrases.notes: 月 (gatsu) = month. 日 (nichi / ka) = day of the month.

responses.japanese: じゅういちがつろくにちです
responses.english: It's November 6th
responses.listen_for: 十一月 (juuichigatsu) = November. 六日 (rokunichi) = the 6th.

phrases.japanese: なんがつですか？
phrases.notes: 何月 (nangatsu) = which month.

responses.japanese: じゅういちがつです
responses.english: It's November
responses.listen_for: 十一月 = November.

responses.japanese: らいげつはじゅうにがつです
responses.english: Next month is December
responses.listen_for: 来月 (raigetsu) = next month.

phrases.japanese: らいげつ、またきます
phrases.notes: 来月 (raigetsu) = next month. 先月 (sengetsu) = last month. 今月 (kongetsu) = this month.

responses.japanese: はい、らいげつおまちしています
responses.english: Yes, we'll be waiting next month
responses.listen_for: 来月 (raigetsu) = next month.

responses.japanese: らいげつはおやすみになります
responses.english: We'll be closed next month
responses.listen_for: なります = will be (polite).

phrases.japanese: こんげつのイベントはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kongetsu no ibento wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there any events this month?
phrases.notes: 今月 (kongetsu) = this month. イベント (ibento) = event.

responses.japanese: はい、らいしゅうまつりがあります
responses.english: Yes, there's a festival next week
responses.listen_for: 祭り (matsuri) = festival.

responses.japanese: こんげつはとくにありません
responses.english: No special events this month
responses.listen_for: 特に (tokuni) = especially / in particular.

phrases.japanese: なんがつがいちばんあついですか？
phrases.romaji: Nangatsu ga ichiban atsui desu ka?
phrases.notes: 一番 (ichiban) = most. 暑い (atsui) = hot.

responses.japanese: はちがつがいちばんあついです
responses.english: August is the hottest
responses.listen_for: 八月 (hachigatsu) = August.

responses.japanese: しちがつからはちがつがいちばんあつくなります
responses.romaji: Shichigatsu kara hachigatsu ga ichiban atsuku narimasu
responses.english: July to August gets the hottest
responses.listen_for: から = from.

phrases.japanese: さくらはいつさきますか？
phrases.notes: 咲く (saku) = to bloom. Cherry blossoms usually bloom from late March to early April.

responses.japanese: さんがつのおわりからしがつのはじめです
responses.romaji: Sangatsu no owari kara shigatsu no hajime desu
responses.english: From late March to early April
responses.listen_for: 終わり (owari) = end. 初め (hajime) = beginning.

responses.japanese: としによってちがいます
responses.english: It depends on the year
responses.listen_for: 〜によって = depending on.

phrases.japanese: ゴールデンウィークはいつですか？
phrases.romaji: Gooruden wiiku wa itsu desu ka?
phrases.notes: ゴールデンウィーク (Golden Week) = a cluster of national holidays from late April to early May.

responses.japanese: しがつのおわりからごがつのはじめです
responses.romaji: Shigatsu no owari kara gogatsu no hajime desu
responses.english: From late April to early May
responses.listen_for: 五月 (gogatsu) = May.

responses.japanese: おみせがこんでいるかもしれません
responses.romaji: Omise ga konde iru kamo shiremasen
responses.english: Shops might be crowded
responses.listen_for: 混む (komu) = to be crowded.

phrases.japanese: おぼんはやっていますか？
phrases.notes: お盆 (Obon) = mid-August holiday period when many shops and businesses close.

responses.japanese: はちがつちゅうじゅんはおやすみです
responses.english: We're closed in mid-August
responses.listen_for: 中旬 (chuujun) = middle of the month.

responses.japanese: はちがつじゅうさんにちからじゅうろくにちまでです
responses.romaji: Hachigatsu juusannichi kara juurokunichi made desu
responses.english: From August 13th to 16th
responses.listen_for: 十三日 (juusannichi) = the 13th.

phrases.japanese: ことしのじゅうにがつのえいぎょうじかんはかわりますか？
phrases.romaji: Kotoshi no juunigatsu no eigyou jikan wa kawarimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do the hours change in December this year?
phrases.notes: 今年 (kotoshi) = this year. 変わる (kawaru) = to change.

responses.japanese: はい、じゅうにがつははちじまでです
responses.romaji: Hai, juunigatsu wa hachiji made desu
responses.english: Yes, in December we close at 8 PM
responses.listen_for: 十二月 (juunigatsu) = December.

responses.japanese: じゅうにがつまつはおやすみです
responses.english: We're closed at the end of December
responses.listen_for: 末 (matsu) = end.

phrases.japanese: つきのなまえをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Tsuki no namae wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Can you teach me the month names?
phrases.notes: Months are 一月 (ichigatsu) to 十二月 (juunigatsu). Just add 月 (gatsu) to the number.

responses.japanese: いちがつ、にがつ、さんがつ……
responses.english: January, February, March...
responses.listen_for: 月 (gatsu) is attached to the number of the month.

responses.japanese: ひとつずつおぼえるといいですよ
responses.romaji: Hitotsu zutsu oboeru to ii desu yo
responses.english: It's good to memorize them one at a time
responses.listen_for: おぼえる (覚える) = to memorize.

phrases.japanese: にほんごはすこししかはなせません
phrases.english: I can only speak a little Japanese
phrases.notes: 〜しか〜ません = only ... (with a negative). Say this early to set expectations.

responses.japanese: そうですか、ゆっくりはなしますね
responses.romaji: Sou desu ka, yukkuri hanashimasu ne
responses.english: I see, I'll speak slowly
responses.listen_for: ゆっくり = slowly.

responses.japanese: えいごはわかりますか？
responses.english: Do you understand English?
responses.listen_for: 英語 (eigo) = English. わかる = to understand.

phrases.japanese: えいごではなせますか？
phrases.notes: 英語 (eigo) = English. Ask this first when you need help.

responses.japanese: すこしならはなせます
responses.english: I can speak a little
responses.listen_for: すこし = a little.

responses.japanese: ごめんなさい、はなせません
responses.english: Sorry, I can't speak it
responses.listen_for: ごめんなさい = sorry (apologetic).

phrases.japanese: もういちどいってください
phrases.notes: もう一度 (mou ichido) = once more.

responses.japanese: はい、ゆっくりいいますね
responses.english: Yes, I'll say it slowly
responses.listen_for: 言います (iimasu) = say.

responses.japanese: こちらにかいてあります
responses.english: It's written here
responses.listen_for: 書いてあります = is written.

phrases.japanese: ゆっくりはなしてください
phrases.notes: ゆっくり = slowly.

responses.japanese: わかりました。ゆっくりはなします
responses.english: Understood. I'll speak slowly
responses.listen_for: わかりました = understood (polite).

responses.japanese: えいごでかいてみます
responses.english: I'll try writing it in English
responses.listen_for: 書いてみます = will try writing.

phrases.japanese: かいてもらえますか？
phrases.notes: 書く (kaku) = to write. Writing often works better than speaking.

responses.japanese: はい、かんじでかいてみますね
responses.romaji: Hai, kanji de kaite mimasu ne
responses.english: Yes, I'll write it in kanji
responses.listen_for: 漢字 (kanji) = Chinese characters used in Japanese.

responses.japanese: スマホにかきましょうか？
responses.english: Shall I type it on my phone?
responses.listen_for: スマホ = smartphone.

phrases.japanese: これをみせてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wo misete mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: Use it with a phone screen or a printed card.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please / go ahead.

responses.japanese: なにですか？
responses.english: What is it?
responses.listen_for: 何 (nan) = what.

phrases.japanese: ほんやくアプリをつかってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Honyaku apuri wo tsukatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I use a translation app?
phrases.notes: 翻訳 (honyaku) = translation. 翻訳アプリ (honyaku apuri) = translation app.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please / go ahead.

responses.japanese: ゆっくりつかってください
responses.english: Please take your time with it
responses.listen_for: ゆっくり = at your own pace.

phrases.japanese: わかりません
phrases.notes: 分かる (wakaru) = to understand. Short and clear.

responses.japanese: すみません、もういちどいいますね
responses.english: Sorry, let me say it again
responses.listen_for: すみません = sorry / excuse me.

responses.japanese: えいごのたんごはわかりますか？
responses.romaji: Eigo no tango wa wakarimasu ka?
responses.english: Do you understand the English words?
responses.listen_for: 単語 (tango) = word.

phrases.japanese: えいごのメニューはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: メニュー (menu). Many restaurants have picture menus even without English.

responses.japanese: すみません、えいごのメニューはありません
responses.romaji: Sumimasen, eigo no menyuu wa arimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we don't have an English menu
responses.listen_for: 〜はありません = there isn't any.

responses.japanese: しゃしんのメニューならあります
responses.english: We have a menu with pictures
responses.listen_for: 写真 (shashin) = photo.

phrases.japanese: こまっています。たすけてください
phrases.english: I'm in trouble. Please help me
phrases.notes: 困る (komaru) = to be in trouble.

responses.japanese: どうしましたか？
responses.english: What happened?
responses.listen_for: どうした = what happened.

responses.japanese: えいごのかたをよびましょうか？
responses.romaji: Eigo no kata wo yobimashou ka?
responses.english: Shall I call someone who speaks English?
responses.listen_for: 呼ぶ (yobu) = to call.

phrases.japanese: ちかくにえいごがはなせるひとはいますか？
phrases.romaji: Chikaku ni eigo ga hanaseru hito wa imasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there someone nearby who speaks English?
phrases.notes: 近く (chikaku) = nearby. 人 (hito) = person.

responses.japanese: すみません、わかりません
responses.english: Sorry, I don't know
responses.listen_for: わかりません = I don't know / understand.

responses.japanese: スタッフにきいてみます
responses.english: I'll ask a staff member
responses.listen_for: 聞いてみます (kiite mimasu) = will try asking.

phrases.japanese: これはなんといいますか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa nan to iimasu ka?
phrases.notes: 〜といいますか = what do you call ...? Point at the object while asking.

responses.japanese: これは、おちゃといいます
responses.english: This is called 'ocha' (tea)
responses.listen_for: 〜といいます = is called.

responses.japanese: ひらがなでかきますね
responses.english: I'll write it in hiragana
responses.listen_for: ひらがな (hiragana) = Japanese phonetic script.

phrases.japanese: えをみせてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: E wo misete mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I point to a picture?
phrases.notes: 絵 (e) = picture. Pointing at a picture menu or a photo works well.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please / go ahead.

responses.japanese: これですね
responses.english: This one, right?
responses.listen_for: 〜ですね = checking that you understand.

phrases.japanese: やさしいにほんごではなしてください
phrases.notes: やさしい (yasashii) = easy / simple. 日本語 (nihongo) = Japanese language.

responses.japanese: わかりました、かんたんにいいますね
responses.english: Understood, I'll say it simply
responses.listen_for: 簡単 (kantan) = simple.

responses.japanese: むずかしいことばはつかわないようにします
responses.romaji: Muzukashii kotoba wa tsukawanai you ni shimasu
responses.english: I'll avoid difficult words
responses.listen_for: 難しい (muzukashii) = difficult. 言葉 (kotoba) = words.

phrases.japanese: ATMはどこにありますか？
phrases.romaji: ATM wa doko ni arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: ATM (ee-tii-emu). Post office and 7-Eleven ATMs usually accept foreign cards.

responses.japanese: セブンイレブンのATMがあります
responses.romaji: Sebun Irebun no ATM ga arimasu
responses.english: There's a 7-Eleven ATM
responses.listen_for: セブンイレブン (7-Eleven) = convenience store chain with ATMs.

responses.japanese: あちらのゆうびんきょくにもあります
responses.romaji: Achira no yuubinkyoku ni mo arimasu
responses.english: There's also one at the post office over there
responses.listen_for: 郵便局 (yuubinkyoku) = post office.

phrases.japanese: げんきんをおろしたいです
phrases.notes: 現金 (genkin) = cash. おろす (下ろす) is the everyday word for withdrawing money.

responses.japanese: カードをいれて、あんしょうばんごうをにゅうりょくしてください
responses.romaji: Kaado wo irete, anshou bangou wo nyuuryoku shite kudasai
responses.english: Insert your card and enter your PIN
responses.listen_for: 暗証番号 (anshou bangou) = PIN.

responses.japanese: いちにちのげんどがくがあります
responses.english: There's a daily withdrawal limit
responses.listen_for: 限度額 (gendogaku) = limit.

phrases.japanese: このカードはつかえますか？
phrases.notes: Many small shops and restaurants only take cash. Look for Visa, Mastercard, or JCB signs.

responses.japanese: はい、つかえます
responses.english: Yes, you can use it
responses.listen_for: 使えます (tsukaemasu) = can be used.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、げんきんのみです
responses.english: Sorry, cash only
responses.listen_for: のみ (only) = cash only.

phrases.japanese: カードがつかえませんでした
phrases.notes: 〜ませんでした = didn't ... (past). Use it when a payment fails.

responses.japanese: もういちどおためしください
responses.english: Please try again
responses.listen_for: お試し (otameshi) = trying (polite).

responses.japanese: ほかのカードでおねがいします
responses.english: Please try another card
responses.listen_for: ほか = other.

phrases.japanese: えんにりょうがえしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to exchange my money into yen
phrases.notes: 両替 (ryougae) = currency exchange. Banks and some hotels exchange money; bring your passport.

responses.japanese: パスポートはおもちですか？
responses.english: Do you have your passport?
responses.listen_for: パスポート = passport.

responses.japanese: どのつうかですか？
responses.english: Which currency is it?
responses.listen_for: 通貨 (tsuuka) = currency.

phrases.japanese: こまかいおかねにくずしてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Komakai okane ni kuzushite moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you break this into smaller bills or coins?
phrases.notes: 小銭 (kozeni) = coins. 崩す (kuzusu) = to break a large bill into smaller money.

responses.japanese: はい、ちょっとおまちください
responses.english: Yes, please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: ちょっと = a little.

responses.japanese: すみません、こぜにがありません
responses.english: Sorry, we don't have any coins
responses.listen_for: 小銭 (kozeni) = coins.

phrases.japanese: おつりがたりません
phrases.notes: おつり (お釣り) = change. 足りない (tarinai) = not enough.

responses.japanese: しつれいしました。かくにんします
responses.english: Sorry about that. I'll check
responses.listen_for: 確認 (kakunin) = check.

responses.japanese: もういちどかぞえますね
responses.english: Let me count it again
responses.listen_for: 数える (kazoeru) = to count.

phrases.japanese: せんえんさつはありますか？
phrases.notes: 札 (satsu) = bill. 千円札 (sen'en satsu) = 1,000-yen bill. Larger bills are often hard to use in small shops.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらどうぞ
responses.english: Yes, here you go
responses.listen_for: こちら = here (polite).

responses.japanese: いいえ、ごせんえんさつならあります
responses.english: No, but we have 5,000-yen bills
responses.listen_for: 五千円札 (gosen'en satsu) = 5,000-yen bill.

phrases.japanese: にゅうこくかんさつはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Nyuukoku kansatsu wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: 入国審査 (nyuukoku shinsa) = immigration inspection. 税関 (zeikan) = customs.

responses.japanese: あちらのレーンへどうぞ
responses.english: Please go to that lane over there
responses.listen_for: レーン (lane) = line.

responses.japanese: パスポートをみせてください
responses.english: Please show your passport
responses.listen_for: 見せる (miseru) = to show.

phrases.japanese: たいざいのもくてきは、かんこうです
phrases.romaji: Taizai no mokuteki wa, kankou desu
phrases.english: The purpose of my stay is sightseeing
phrases.notes: 滞在 (taizai) = stay. 目的 (mokuteki) = purpose. 観光 (kankou) = sightseeing.

responses.japanese: なんにちたいざいしますか？
responses.english: How many days will you stay?
responses.listen_for: 何日 (nannichi) = how many days.

responses.japanese: どこにとまりますか？
responses.english: Where will you stay?
responses.listen_for: 泊まる (tomaru) = to stay overnight.

phrases.japanese: にもつうけとりはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Nimotsu uketori wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: 荷物受け取り (nimotsu uketori) = baggage claim. Check the screen for your flight number.

responses.japanese: でんこうけいじばんをみてください
responses.english: Please check the flight information screen
responses.listen_for: 電光掲示板 (denkou keijiban) = electronic display board.

responses.japanese: あちらのターンテーブルです
responses.english: It's at the carousel over there
responses.listen_for: ターンテーブル (turntable) = baggage carousel.

phrases.japanese: しんこくするものがあります
phrases.notes: 申告 (shinkoku) = declaration. Choose the red lane if you have items to declare, the green lane if you don't.

responses.japanese: なにをもっていますか？
responses.english: What are you carrying?
responses.listen_for: 持つ (motsu) = to carry.

responses.japanese: あかいレーンへどうぞ
responses.english: Please go to the red lane
responses.listen_for: 赤い (akai) = red.

phrases.japanese: ひこうきがおくれていますか？
phrases.notes: 遅れる (okureru) = to be delayed. Check the screen or ask at the airline counter.

responses.japanese: はい、さんじっぷんおくれています
responses.english: Yes, it's delayed by 30 minutes
responses.listen_for: 〜分 (fun) = minutes.

responses.japanese: こちらのカウンターでかくにんしてください
responses.romaji: Kochira no kauntaa de kakunin shite kudasai
responses.english: Please check at this counter
responses.listen_for: カウンター (counter).

phrases.japanese: くうこうから、まちまでどうやっていけますか？
phrases.romaji: Kuukou kara, machi made dou yatte ikemasu ka?
phrases.english: How do I get from the airport to the city?
phrases.notes: 空港 (kuukou) = airport. 街 (machi) = town / city.

responses.japanese: くうこうきゅうこうでいけます
responses.english: You can take the airport express
responses.listen_for: 空港急行 (kuukou kyuukou) = airport express train.

responses.japanese: リムジンバスもあります
responses.english: There's also a limousine bus
responses.listen_for: リムジンバス (limousine bus).

phrases.japanese: でんしゃのきっぷはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Densha no kippu wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy a train ticket?
phrases.notes: 切符 (kippu) = ticket. 買う (kau) = to buy.

responses.japanese: あちらのじどうはんばいきでかえます
responses.romaji: Achira no jidou hanbaiki de kaemasu
responses.english: You can buy it at the ticket machines over there
responses.listen_for: 自動販売機 (jidou hanbaiki) = vending machine.

responses.japanese: スイカをかえば、でんしゃにものれます
responses.romaji: Suika wo kaeba, densha ni mo noremasu
responses.english: If you buy a Suica card, you can also ride the train with it
responses.listen_for: スイカ (Suica) = IC transit card.

phrases.japanese: てにもつをあずけられますか？
phrases.english: Can I leave my luggage here?
phrases.notes: 手荷物 (tenimotsu) = hand luggage. コインロッカー (koin rokkaa) = coin locker.

responses.japanese: はい、ロッカーかあずかりじょがあります
responses.romaji: Hai, rokkaa ka azukarijo ga arimasu
responses.english: Yes, there are lockers or a luggage storage counter
responses.listen_for: 預かり所 (azukarijo) = storage counter.

responses.japanese: ひとつにつき、さんびゃくえんです
responses.romaji: Hitotsu ni tsuki, sanbyaku en desu
responses.english: It's 300 yen per bag
responses.listen_for: 一つにつき (hitotsu ni tsuki) = per item.

phrases.japanese: わすれものをさがしています
phrases.english: I'm looking for something I left behind
phrases.notes: 忘れ物 (wasuremono) = lost item. 探す (sagasu) = to search.

responses.japanese: どんなものですか？
responses.english: What does it look like?
responses.listen_for: どんな = what kind.

responses.japanese: いつ、どこでなくしましたか？
responses.english: When and where did you lose it?
responses.listen_for: いつ = when. どこ = where.

phrases.japanese: かばんをでんしゃにわすれました
phrases.english: I left my bag on the train
phrases.notes: 電車 (densha) = train. 忘れる (wasureru) = to leave behind.

responses.japanese: えきのインフォメーションにおといあわせください
responses.romaji: Eki no infoomeeshon ni o-toiawase kudasai
responses.english: Please contact the station information desk
responses.listen_for: インフォメーション (information) = information desk.

responses.japanese: えきのわすれものセンターへどうぞ
responses.romaji: Eki no wasuremono sentaa e douzo
responses.english: Please go to the station's lost-and-found center
responses.listen_for: センター (center).

phrases.japanese: わすれものセンターはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Wasuremono sentaa wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Tokyo's central lost-and-found is in Shinjuku. Stations often have their own center as well.

responses.japanese: あちらのけいさつしょにあります
responses.english: It's at the police station over there
responses.listen_for: 警察署 (keisatsusho) = police station.

responses.japanese: えきのこうばんできいてください
responses.romaji: Eki no kouban de kiite kudasai
responses.english: Please ask at the station's police box
responses.listen_for: 交番 (kouban) = police box.

phrases.japanese: きってをかいたいです
phrases.notes: 切手 (kitte) = postage stamp. 郵便局 (yuubinkyoku) = post office.

responses.japanese: はい、なんまいですか？
responses.english: Yes, how many sheets?
responses.listen_for: 〜枚 (mai) = counter for flat things.

responses.japanese: はがきのきってもありますよ
responses.romaji: Hagaki no kitte mo arimasu yo
responses.english: We also have postcard stamps
responses.listen_for: はがき (hagaki) = postcard.

phrases.japanese: このにもつを、がいこくにおくれますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono nimotsu wo, gaikoku ni okuremasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I send this package overseas?
phrases.notes: 郵便 (yuubin) = mail. 国際 (kokusai) = international. EMS = fast international post.

responses.japanese: はい、EMSでおくれます
responses.english: Yes, you can send it by EMS
responses.listen_for: EMS = Express Mail Service.

responses.japanese: ながさとおもさをはかります
responses.english: I'll measure the length and weight
responses.listen_for: 重さ (omosa) = weight. 測る (hakaru) = to measure.

phrases.japanese: はやくとどくほうほうはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hayaku todoku houhou wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a faster way to send it?
phrases.notes: 早く (hayaku) = quickly. 速達 (sokutatsu) = express mail within Japan.

responses.japanese: そくたつにすると、あしたつきます
responses.romaji: Sokutatsu ni suru to, ashita tsukimasu
responses.english: If you use express, it arrives tomorrow
responses.listen_for: 速達 (sokutatsu) = express.

responses.japanese: ふつうのゆうびんは、いっしゅうかんほどかかります
responses.romaji: Futsuu no yuubin wa, isshuukan hodo kakarimasu
responses.english: Regular mail takes about a week
responses.listen_for: 週間 (shuukan) = week.

phrases.japanese: てがみをだしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to send a letter
phrases.notes: 手紙 (tegami) = letter. 出す (dasu) = to send / post.

responses.japanese: あちらのポストにいれてください
responses.romaji: Achira no posuto ni irete kudasai
responses.english: Please put it in the mailbox over there
responses.listen_for: ポスト (post) = mailbox.

responses.japanese: そくたつですか、ふつうですか？
responses.romaji: Sokutatsu desu ka, futsuu desu ka?
responses.english: Express or regular?
responses.listen_for: 普通 (futsuu) = regular.

phrases.japanese: ゆうびんきょくのえいぎょうじかんはなんじですか？
phrases.romaji: Yuubinkyoku no eigyou jikan wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.english: What are the post office hours?
phrases.notes: 郵便局 (yuubinkyoku) = post office. 営業時間 (eigyou jikan) = opening hours.

responses.japanese: へいじつはくじからごじまでです
responses.romaji: Heijitsu wa kuji kara goji made desu
responses.english: On weekdays it's from 9 to 5
responses.listen_for: 平日 (heijitsu) = weekday.

responses.japanese: どようびはごごさんじまでです
responses.romaji: Doyoubi wa gogo sanji made desu
responses.english: On Saturdays it's until 3 PM
responses.listen_for: 午後 (gogo) = PM.

phrases.japanese: にもつをつぎのホテルにおくりたいです
phrases.romaji: Nimotsu wo tsugi no hoteru ni okuritai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to send my luggage to the next hotel
phrases.notes: たっきゅうびん (宅急便, takkyuubin) luggage forwarding between hotels/airports is extremely common and reliable in Japan, usually arriving the next day.

responses.japanese: つぎのホテルのじゅうしょをおしえてください
responses.romaji: Tsugi no hoteru no juusho wo oshiete kudasai
responses.english: Please tell me the address of the next hotel
responses.listen_for: じゅうしょ (住所, juusho) = address.
responses.kanji: 次のホテルの住所を教えてください

responses.japanese: とうちゃくはあすになります
responses.english: It will arrive tomorrow
responses.listen_for: とうちゃく (到着, touchaku) = arrival.
responses.kanji: 到着は明日になります

phrases.kanji: 荷物を次のホテルに送りたいです

phrases.japanese: くうこうまでにもつをおくれますか？
phrases.romaji: Kuukou made nimotsu wo okuremasu ka?
phrases.english: Can you send my luggage to the airport?
phrases.notes: Many hotels and konbini offer くうこうたっきゅうびん (空港宅急便, kuukou takkyuubin) airport delivery services — ask a day or two ahead.

responses.japanese: はい、フライトのじかんをおしえてください
responses.romaji: Hai, furaito no jikan wo oshiete kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please tell me your flight time
responses.listen_for: フライト (furaito) = flight.
responses.kanji: はい、フライトの時間を教えてください

responses.japanese: まえじつまでのおもうしこみがひつようです
responses.romaji: Maejitsu made no omoushikomi ga hitsuyou desu
responses.english: Application is needed by the day before
responses.listen_for: まえじつ (前日, maejitsu) = the day before.
responses.kanji: 前日までのお申し込みが必要です

phrases.kanji: 空港まで荷物を送れますか？

phrases.japanese: とうちゃくまでなんにちかかりますか？
phrases.romaji: Touchaku made nan nichi kakarimasu ka?
phrases.english: How many days will it take to arrive?
phrases.notes: Within the same region it's often next-day (よくじつ, 翌日); longer distances (e.g. Tokyo to Hokkaido/Okinawa) can take 2 days.

responses.japanese: よくじつにとうちゃくします
responses.english: It will arrive the next day
responses.listen_for: よくじつ (翌日, yokujitsu) = the following day.
responses.kanji: 翌日に到着します

responses.japanese: とおいちいきなのでふつかかかります
responses.english: Since it's a distant area, it will take two days
responses.listen_for: ちいき (地域, chiiki) = region/area.
responses.kanji: 遠い地域なので2日かかります

phrases.kanji: 到着まで何日かかりますか？

phrases.japanese: りょうきんはおもさでかわりますか？
phrases.romaji: Ryoukin wa omosa de kawarimasu ka?
phrases.english: Does the price change based on weight?
phrases.notes: おもさ (重さ, omosa) = weight. Price is usually based on a combination of size (three-dimensional measurement) and weight.

responses.japanese: はい、おもさとおおきさでかわります
responses.romaji: Hai, omosa to ookisa de kawarimasu
responses.english: Yes, it changes based on weight and size
responses.listen_for: おおきさ (大きさ, ookisa) = size.
responses.kanji: はい、重さと大きさで変わります

responses.japanese: にじゅっキロまでこのりょうきんです
responses.english: Up to 20kg is this price
responses.listen_for: キロ (kiro) = kilogram.
responses.kanji: 20キロまでこの料金です

phrases.kanji: 料金は重さで変わりますか？

phrases.japanese: でんぴょうのかきかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Denpyou no kakikata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please show me how to fill out this slip
phrases.notes: でんぴょう (伝票, denpyou) = shipping slip/invoice — needs sender/recipient address, phone number, and delivery date.

responses.japanese: おなまえとじゅうしょをここにかいてください
responses.romaji: Onamae to juusho wo koko ni kaite kudasai
responses.english: Please write your name and address here
responses.listen_for: おなまえ (お名前, onamae) = name.
responses.kanji: お名前と住所をここに書いてください

responses.japanese: とどけさきのでんわばんごうもひつようです
responses.romaji: Todokesaki no denwa bangou mo hitsuyou desu
responses.english: The recipient's phone number is also required
responses.listen_for: とどけさき (届け先, todokesaki) = delivery destination/recipient.
responses.kanji: 届け先の電話番号も必要です

phrases.kanji: 伝票の書き方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: われものがはいっています
phrases.notes: われもの (割れ物, waremono) = fragile items — mention this so staff mark the package accordingly.

responses.japanese: わかりました、われものちゅういのシールをはります
responses.romaji: Wakarimashita, waremono chuui no shiiru wo harimasu
responses.english: Understood, I'll put a fragile warning sticker on it
responses.listen_for: ちゅうい (注意, chuui) = caution/warning.
responses.kanji: 分かりました、割れ物注意のシールを貼ります

responses.japanese: ていねいにとりあつかいます
responses.english: We'll handle it carefully
responses.listen_for: ていねいに (丁寧に, teinei ni) = carefully/politely.
responses.kanji: 丁寧に取り扱います

phrases.kanji: 割れ物が入っています

phrases.japanese: ふくろはいくらですか？
phrases.notes: 袋 (fukuro) = bag. レジぶくろ (regi bukuro) = plastic bag at the register. Many shops charge for it.

responses.japanese: いちまいじゅうえんです
responses.english: It's 10 yen per bag
responses.listen_for: 一枚 (ichimai) = one bag.

responses.japanese: ふくろはいりませんか？
responses.english: Don't you need a bag?
responses.listen_for: いりません = don't need.

phrases.japanese: マイバッグをもってきました
phrases.notes: マイバッグ (mai baggu) = reusable bag. 持って来る (motte kuru) = to bring.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます、ふくろはだいじょうぶですね
responses.romaji: Arigatou gozaimasu, fukuro wa daijoubu desu ne
responses.english: Thank you, you don't need a bag then
responses.listen_for: 〜ね = checking you agree.

responses.japanese: レジぶくろはごりようになりますか？
responses.romaji: Regi bukuro wa goriyou ni narimasu ka?
responses.english: Would you like a plastic bag?
responses.listen_for: ご利用 (goriyou) = use (polite).

phrases.japanese: はしはいりません
phrases.notes: Convenience stores and supermarkets often ask whether you need chopsticks to reduce waste.

responses.japanese: わかりました
responses.english: Understood
responses.listen_for: わかりました = understood (polite).

responses.japanese: スプーンとフォークはよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Supuun to fooku wa yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Do you want a spoon and fork?
responses.listen_for: よろしい (yoroshii) = is it fine / do you want.

phrases.japanese: このかごをつかってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kago wo tsukatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: かご (kago) = basket. Supermarkets usually have baskets at the entrance.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: どうぞ = please / go ahead.

responses.japanese: レジのまえにおいてください
responses.romaji: Reji no mae ni oite kudasai
responses.english: Please put it back in front of the register
responses.listen_for: 置く (oku) = to place.

phrases.japanese: ふくろにつめてもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you pack it into the bag?
phrases.notes: 詰める (tsumeru) = to pack. Some shops pack for you; others have a packing counter.

responses.japanese: はい、おまかせください
responses.english: Yes, leave it to us
responses.listen_for: お任せ (omakase) = leave it to me.

responses.japanese: セルフレジのほうでつめてください
responses.romaji: Serufu reji no hou de tsumete kudasai
responses.english: Please pack it at the self-checkout
responses.listen_for: セルフレジ (self register) = self-checkout.

phrases.japanese: とりあえずビールをください
phrases.notes: とりあえず = for now / to start with. Izakaya customers usually order a first drink right away.

responses.japanese: はい、かしこまりました
responses.english: Yes, certainly
responses.listen_for: かしこまりました = understood (polite).

responses.japanese: なまとびんがありますよ
responses.romaji: Nama to bin ga arimasu yo
responses.english: We have draft and bottled
responses.listen_for: 生 (nama) = draft beer.

phrases.japanese: かんぱいしましょう！
phrases.notes: 乾杯 (kanpai) = cheers. Wait for the toast before you start drinking.

responses.japanese: かんぱい！
responses.english: Cheers!
responses.listen_for: 乾杯 = cheers.

responses.japanese: おつかれさまです
responses.english: Good work / thanks for today
responses.listen_for: お疲れさま = thanks for your effort.

phrases.japanese: にほんしゅをおすすめでおねがいします
phrases.notes: 日本酒 (nihonshu) = sake. 辛口 (karakuchi) = dry. 甘口 (amakuchi) = sweet.

responses.japanese: こちらのからくちはいかがですか？
responses.romaji: Kochira no karakuchi wa ikaga desu ka?
responses.english: How about this dry one?
responses.listen_for: 辛口 (karakuchi) = dry.

responses.japanese: おかんにもできますよ
responses.english: We can also serve it warm
responses.listen_for: お燗 (okan) = warmed sake.

phrases.japanese: カラオケのへやをよやくしたいです
phrases.romaji: Karaoke no heya wo yoyaku shitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to book a karaoke room
phrases.notes: 部屋 (heya) = room. 予約 (yoyaku) = reservation. Many places let you walk in when rooms are free.

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people?
responses.listen_for: 何名 (nanmei) = how many people.

responses.japanese: いまからなら、すぐにはいれます
responses.romaji: Ima kara nara, sugu ni hairemasu
responses.english: If it's now, you can go in right away
responses.listen_for: すぐ = right away.

phrases.japanese: いちじかんのプランはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Ichijikan no puran wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have a one-hour plan?
phrases.notes: プラン (puran) = plan. フリータイム (furii taimu) = unlimited time for a set price.

responses.japanese: はい、いちじかんとフリータイムがあります
responses.romaji: Hai, ichijikan to furii taimu ga arimasu
responses.english: Yes, there's a one-hour plan and free time
responses.listen_for: フリータイム = unlimited time.

responses.japanese: よじかんからのフリータイムがおとくです
responses.romaji: Yojikan kara no furii taimu ga otoku desu
responses.english: Free time starting from 4 hours is better value
responses.listen_for: お得 (otoku) = good value.

phrases.japanese: ドリンクバーはついていますか？
phrases.romaji: Dorinku baa wa tsuite imasu ka?
phrases.english: Does it include a drink bar?
phrases.notes: ドリンクバー (drink bar) = self-serve drink station, often free with the room.

responses.japanese: はい、ドリンクバーはついています
responses.romaji: Hai, dorinku baa wa tsuite imasu
responses.english: Yes, the drink bar is included
responses.listen_for: 付いている = included.

responses.japanese: ドリンクは、べつにかかります
responses.english: Drinks are charged separately
responses.listen_for: 別に (betsu ni) = separately.

phrases.japanese: なんじかんまでいられますか？
phrases.english: How many hours can we stay?
phrases.notes: 時間 (jikan) = time. 〜まで = up to.

responses.japanese: さんじかんまでです
responses.english: Up to three hours
responses.listen_for: 時間 (jikan) = hours.

responses.japanese: じかんがきたらおしらせします
responses.english: We'll let you know when time is up
responses.listen_for: 知らせる (shiraseru) = to inform.

phrases.japanese: えんちょうできますか？
phrases.notes: 延長 (enchou) = extension. Usually billed in 30-minute blocks.

responses.japanese: はい、さんじゅっぷんごとにえんちょうできます
responses.romaji: Hai, sanjuppun goto ni enchou dekimasu
responses.english: Yes, you can extend in 30-minute blocks
responses.listen_for: 〜ごとに (goto ni) = every.

responses.japanese: うけつけでおたずねください
responses.english: Please ask at the front desk
responses.listen_for: お尋ね (otazune) = inquiry.

phrases.japanese: えいごのきょくはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Eigo no kyoku wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: 曲 (kyoku) = song. Song lists are usually on a tablet or the remote screen.

responses.japanese: タブレットでえらべます
responses.english: You can choose on the tablet
responses.listen_for: タブレット (tablet).

responses.japanese: にほんごとえいごのきょくがあります
responses.romaji: Nihongo to eigo no kyoku ga arimasu
responses.english: There are Japanese and English songs
responses.listen_for: 曲 (kyoku) = song.

phrases.japanese: マイクをもういっぽんください
phrases.english: Please give me one more microphone
phrases.notes: マイク (maiku) = microphone. 本 (hon) = counter for long, thin items.

responses.japanese: はい、すぐにおもちします
responses.english: Yes, I'll bring one right away
responses.listen_for: お持ちします = I'll bring (polite).

responses.japanese: ほかのマイクもありますよ
responses.romaji: Hoka no maiku mo arimasu yo
responses.english: We have other microphones too
responses.listen_for: ほか = other.

phrases.japanese: おとをもうすこしちいさくしてください
phrases.romaji: Oto wo mou sukoshi chiisaku shite kudasai
phrases.english: Please turn the volume down a little
phrases.notes: 音 (oto) = sound. 小さく (chiisaku) = quieter.

responses.japanese: はい、ボリュームをさげます
responses.english: Yes, I'll lower the volume
responses.listen_for: 下げる (sageru) = to lower.

responses.japanese: ちょうせつはこちらのボタンです
responses.romaji: Chousetsu wa kochira no botan desu
responses.english: The adjustment is this button here
responses.listen_for: 調節 (chousetsu) = adjustment.

phrases.japanese: せんとうにはいりたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to go to a public bath
phrases.notes: 銭湯 (sentou) = public bath. Unlike onsen, sento are usually in the city and cost a small fee.

responses.japanese: ロッカーのかぎをもってはいってください
responses.romaji: Rokkaa no kagi wo motte haitte kudasai
responses.english: Take the locker key in with you
responses.listen_for: 持って入る (motte hairu) = take in.

responses.japanese: たおるはおかりできます
responses.english: You can rent a towel
responses.listen_for: お借り (okari) = borrow (polite).

phrases.japanese: ぬぎかたをおしえてください
phrases.english: Please show me how it works
