phrases.notes: 脱ぐ (nugu) = to take off clothes. Everyone bathes without clothes, and towels stay out of the water.

responses.japanese: ロッカーでぬいでください
responses.english: Please undress in the locker room
responses.listen_for: 脱ぐ (nugu) = take off clothes.

responses.japanese: たおるはおゆにいれないでください
responses.romaji: Taoru wa oyu ni irenaide kudasai
responses.english: Please don't put the towel in the water
responses.listen_for: お湯 (oyu) = hot water. 入れる = to put in.

phrases.japanese: からだをあらってからはいります
phrases.english: I'll wash myself before getting in
phrases.notes: 体 (karada) = body. 洗う (arau) = to wash. Always wash before entering the bath.

responses.japanese: はい、かけゆでながしてください
responses.english: Yes, rinse off with the shower first
responses.listen_for: かけ湯 (kakeyu) = rinse water. 流す (nagasu) = to rinse.

responses.japanese: せっけんはこちらです
responses.english: The soap is here
responses.listen_for: 石鹸 (sekken) = soap.

phrases.japanese: おゆのおんどはどのくらいですか？
phrases.romaji: Oyu no ondo wa dono kurai desu ka?
phrases.notes: お湯 (oyu) = hot water. 温度 (ondo) = temperature.

responses.japanese: だいたいよんじゅうにどです
responses.english: It's about 42 degrees
responses.listen_for: 度 (do) = degrees.

responses.japanese: すこしあついかもしれません
responses.english: It might be a bit hot
responses.listen_for: 熱い (atsui) = hot.

phrases.japanese: たおるはおゆにつけてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Taoru wa oyu ni tsukete mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: Can I dip the towel in the water?
phrases.notes: The towel is for washing, not for soaking in the bath.

responses.japanese: いいえ、たおるはあたまにのせてください
responses.romaji: Iie, taoru wa atama ni nosete kudasai
responses.english: No, please put the towel on your head
responses.listen_for: 頭 (atama) = head. 乗せる (noseru) = to place on.

responses.japanese: おふろのなかではだめです
responses.romaji: Ofuro no naka de wa dame desu
responses.english: Not in the bath, please
responses.listen_for: だめ (dame) = not allowed.

phrases.japanese: なんじまでおふろにはいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Nanji made ofuro ni hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: What time does the bath close?
phrases.notes: お風呂 (ofuro) = bath. 閉まる (shimaru) = to close.

responses.japanese: よるじゅうじまでです
responses.english: Until 10 PM
responses.listen_for: 夜 (yoru) = night.

responses.japanese: さいごにはいれるのは、くじはんまでです
responses.romaji: Saigo ni hairu no wa, kuji han made desu
responses.english: The last entry is 9:30
responses.listen_for: 最後 (saigo) = last.

phrases.japanese: ロッカーのかぎをなくしてしまいました
phrases.romaji: Rokkaa no kagi wo nakushite shimaimashita
phrases.notes: 鍵 (kagi) = key. ロッカーの鍵 (rokkaa no kagi) = locker key. なくす (無くす) = to lose.

responses.japanese: ロッカーのばんごうをおしえてください
responses.romaji: Rokkaa no bangou wo oshiete kudasai
responses.english: Please tell me your locker number
responses.listen_for: 番号 (bangou) = number.

responses.japanese: すこしおまちください
responses.english: Please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: 少し (sukoshi) = a little.

phrases.japanese: ほかにきをつけることはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Hoka ni ki wo tsukeru koto wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there other things I should be careful about?
phrases.notes: 気をつける (ki wo tsukeru) = to be careful. Tattoos may not be allowed, so check the sign at the entrance.

responses.japanese: ほかのおきゃくさんのめいわくにならないようにしてください
responses.romaji: Hoka no okyakusan no meiwaku ni naranai you ni shite kudasai
responses.english: Please don't bother other customers
responses.listen_for: 迷惑 (meiwaku) = trouble / inconvenience.

responses.japanese: いれずみのあるかたははいれません
responses.romaji: Irezumi no aru kata wa hairemasen
responses.english: People with tattoos can't enter
responses.listen_for: 入れ墨 (irezumi) = tattoo.

phrases.japanese: 〜からきました
phrases.notes: Standard reply when asked where you are from.

responses.japanese: 〜からですか！とおいですね！
responses.romaji: [country] kara desu ka! Tooi desu ne!
responses.english: From [country]! That's far!
responses.listen_for: とおい (遠い, tooi) = far. Japanese locals appreciate knowing where visitors are visiting from.
responses.kanji: 〜からですか！遠いですね！

phrases.kanji: 〜から来ました

phrases.japanese: にほんははじめてです
phrases.english: This is my first time in Japan
phrases.notes: If it's your second time, say: 2にかいめです (回目です, Nikaime desu).

responses.japanese: ようこそにほんへ！たのしんでくださいね
responses.romaji: Youkoso Nihon e! Tanoshinde kudasai ne
responses.english: Welcome to Japan! Please enjoy your stay
responses.listen_for: ようこそ (youkoso) = welcome. たのしんで (楽しんで, tanoshinde) = enjoy.
responses.kanji: ようこそ日本へ！楽しんでくださいね

phrases.kanji: 日本は初めてです

phrases.japanese: にほんのごはんはとてもおいしいです
phrases.romaji: Nihon no gohan wa totemo oishii desu
phrases.notes: Guaranteed warm smile from locals.

responses.japanese: ほんとうですか？なにがいちばんすきですか？
responses.romaji: Hontou desu ka? Nani ga ichiban suki desu ka?
responses.english: Really? What do you like the most?
responses.listen_for: いちばんすき (一番好き, ichiban suki) = favorite/like the most. Name a dish like ラーメン or すし (寿司)!
responses.kanji: 本当ですか？何が一番好きですか？

phrases.kanji: 日本のご飯はとても美味しいです

phrases.japanese: きょうはさむいですね
phrases.notes: Great winter icebreaker in December.

responses.japanese: そうですね、かぜをひかないようにしてくださいね
responses.romaji: Sou desu ne, kaze wo hikanai you ni shite kudasai ne
responses.english: Indeed, make sure you stay warm and don't catch a cold
responses.listen_for: そうですね = 'I agree / indeed'. A universal casual agreement phrase.
responses.kanji: そうですね、風邪を引かないようにしてくださいね

phrases.kanji: 今日は寒いですね

phrases.japanese: タトゥーはだいじょうぶですか？
phrases.notes: Check policies beforehand if you have visible ink.

responses.japanese: シールでかくせばだいじょうぶです
responses.english: It's fine if you cover them with a sticker
responses.listen_for: かくせば (隠せば, kakuseba) = if covered. They may offer cover-up patches.
responses.kanji: シールで隠せば大丈夫です

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、おことわりしております
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, okotowari shite orimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, but tattoos are not permitted
responses.listen_for: おことわり (お断り, okotowari) = refusal / not permitted.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、お断りしております

phrases.kanji: タトゥーは大丈夫ですか？

phrases.japanese: ろてんぶろはどこですか？
phrases.notes: ろてんぶろ (露天風呂, rotenburo) = outdoor open-air bath.

responses.japanese: おくのかいだんをおりたところにございます
responses.romaji: Oku no kaidan wo orita tokoro ni gozaimasu
responses.english: It is located down the stairs at the back
responses.listen_for: おく (奥, oku) = back/inner part, かいだん (階段, kaidan) = stairs.
responses.kanji: 奥の階段を下りたところにございます

phrases.kanji: 露天風呂はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: タトゥーがあってもいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Tatoo ga atte mo hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I enter even if I have a tattoo?
phrases.notes: More direct than a general check — useful when you already know you have visible ink. Many public onsen still ban tattoos due to their old association with the yakuza, though this is slowly changing, especially in tourist areas.

responses.japanese: ちいさいタトゥーならだいじょうぶです
responses.english: It's fine if the tattoo is small
responses.listen_for: ちいさい (小さい, chiisai) = small. Size-based policies are common.
responses.kanji: 小さいタトゥーなら大丈夫です

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、タトゥーのあるほうはごえんりょいただいております
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, tatoo no aru kata wa goenryo itadaite orimasu
responses.english: I'm very sorry, but guests with tattoos are kindly asked not to enter
responses.listen_for: ごえんりょ (ご遠慮, goenryo) = a polite way of saying 'please refrain'. A firm but courteous no.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、タトゥーのある方はご遠慮いただいております

phrases.kanji: タトゥーがあっても入れますか？

phrases.japanese: タトゥーをかくすシールはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Tatoo wo kakusu shiiru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have stickers to cover tattoos?
phrases.notes: Many tattoo-friendly onsen and sento sell or lend cover-up patches (シール/パッチ) at the front desk for guests with small tattoos.

responses.japanese: はい、フロントでおかいもとめいただけます
responses.english: Yes, you can purchase them at the front desk
responses.listen_for: フロント (furonto) = front desk. おかいもとめ (お買い求め, okaimotome) = a polite 'to purchase'.
responses.kanji: はい、フロントでお買い求めいただけます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、ごよういがございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, goyoui ga gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we don't have any available
responses.listen_for: ごようい (ご用意, goyoui) = preparation/availability. A polite way to say 'we don't have that'.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、ご用意がございません

phrases.kanji: タトゥーを隠すシールはありますか？

phrases.japanese: かしきりふろはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have a private bath?
phrases.notes: かしきりぶろ (貸切風呂, kashikiri-buro) = a private/reservable bath, often booked by the hour — the easiest workaround if a facility doesn't allow visible tattoos in the shared baths.

responses.japanese: はい、ごよやくせいになっております
responses.english: Yes, it works on a reservation basis
responses.listen_for: ごよやくせい (ご予約制, goyoyaku-sei) = reservation system. Ask なんじから (何時から, nanji kara) for available times.
responses.kanji: はい、ご予約制になっております

responses.japanese: もうしわけございませんが、かしきりふろはございません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen ga, kashikiri-buro wa gozaimasen
responses.english: I'm sorry, we don't have a private bath
responses.listen_for: A polite no — you may need to look for a different facility.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございませんが、貸切風呂はございません

phrases.kanji: 貸切風呂はありますか？

phrases.japanese: かしきりふろはなんにんまでいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Kashikiri-buro wa nan-nin made hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: How many people can use the private bath?
phrases.notes: Private baths (貸切風呂/家族風呂) are often capped at 2–4 people and booked in time slots — ask at check-in.

responses.japanese: ふたりまでです
responses.english: Up to two people
responses.listen_for: まで (made) = up to/until — listen for the number right before it.
responses.kanji: 二人までです

responses.japanese: さいだいよんめいさままでごりよういただけます
responses.english: Up to a maximum of 4 people
responses.listen_for: めいさま (名様, mei-sama) is the polite counter for people, used by staff.
responses.kanji: 最大4名様までご利用いただけます

phrases.kanji: 貸切風呂は何人まで入れますか？

phrases.japanese: やっきょくはどこですか？
phrases.notes: やっきょく (薬局, yakkyoku) = pharmacy/drugstore. Look for ドラッグストア (doraggu sutoa) signs too — those also sell over-the-counter medicine.

responses.japanese: つぎのかくをみぎにまがったところにあります
responses.romaji: Tsugi no kado wo migi ni magatta tokoro ni arimasu
responses.english: It's just after you turn right at the next corner
responses.listen_for: つぎのかど (次の角, tsugi no kado) = next corner. みぎ/ひだり (右/左, migi/hidari) = right/left.
responses.kanji: 次の角を右に曲がったところにあります

phrases.kanji: 薬局はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: ぐあいがわるいです
phrases.notes: A general catch-all for 'I don't feel well' — use it first, then get more specific if asked.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですか？どこがいたいですか？
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Doko ga itai desu ka?
responses.english: Are you okay? Where does it hurt?
responses.listen_for: どこがどこがいたい (痛い, doko ga itai) = where does it hurt. Point to the area if you don't know the word.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫ですか？どこが痛いですか？

phrases.kanji: 具合が悪いです

phrases.japanese: あたまがいたいです
phrases.notes: Swap あたま (頭, atama) / head for another body part + がいたいです (痛いです) to describe other pain, e.g. のど (喉, nodo) / throat, おなか (お腹, onaka) / stomach.

responses.japanese: ずつうやくをのみましたか？
responses.english: Have you taken any headache medicine?
responses.listen_for: のみました (飲みました, nomimashita) = took/drank. Medicine is 'drunk' (飲む) in Japanese, not 'taken'.
responses.kanji: 頭痛薬を飲みましたか？

phrases.kanji: 頭が痛いです

phrases.japanese: おなかがいたいです
phrases.notes: Very common after trying unfamiliar food or drinking too much.

responses.japanese: たべすぎましたか？それとものみすぎましたか？
responses.english: Did you eat too much? Or drink too much?
responses.listen_for: すぎました (過ぎました, sugimashita) = did too much of something. たべ (食べ, tabe) = eat, のみ (飲み, nomi) = drink.
responses.kanji: 食べ過ぎましたか？それとも飲み過ぎましたか？

phrases.kanji: お腹が痛いです

phrases.japanese: ねつがあります
phrases.notes: ねつ (熱, netsu) = fever/heat. Worth mentioning early since it signals something more serious than a minor ache.

responses.japanese: なんどくらいありますか？
responses.english: About how many degrees is it?
responses.listen_for: なんど (何度, nando) = how many degrees. Japan uses Celsius — 38さんじゅうはちど (度, sanjuu-hachi do) = 38°C.
responses.kanji: 何度くらいありますか？

phrases.kanji: 熱があります

phrases.japanese: かぜをひきました
phrases.notes: かぜ (風邪, kaze) = cold (illness) — note it's a different word from かぜ (風, kaze) / 'wind' despite similar spelling.

responses.japanese: おだいじに。ゆっくりやすんでくださいね
responses.romaji: Odaiji ni. Yukkuri yasunde kudasai ne
responses.english: Take care. Please get plenty of rest
responses.listen_for: おだいじに (お大事に, odaiji ni) = 'get well soon' — the standard thing to say to someone who's sick.
responses.kanji: お大事に。ゆっくり休んでくださいね

phrases.kanji: 風邪をひきました

phrases.japanese: ずつうやくはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have painkillers / headache medicine?
phrases.notes: ずつうやく (頭痛薬, zutsuuyaku) = headache medicine. For general pain relief ask for いたみどめ (痛み止め, itamidome) instead.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらのたなにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, kochira no tana ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, they're on this shelf
responses.listen_for: たな (棚, tana) = shelf. They'll likely point or walk you over.
responses.kanji: はい、こちらの棚にございます

phrases.kanji: 頭痛薬はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ばんそうこうはありますか？
phrases.notes: ばんそうこう (絆創膏, bansoukou) = adhesive bandage/band-aid. Handy after a long day of walking in new shoes.

responses.japanese: はい、レジのちかくにあります
responses.romaji: Hai, reji no chikaku ni arimasu
responses.english: Yes, they're near the register
responses.listen_for: レジ (reji) = cash register/checkout counter.
responses.kanji: はい、レジの近くにあります

phrases.kanji: 絆創膏はありますか？

phrases.japanese: 〇〇にアレルギーがあります
phrases.notes: Useful for both pharmacies and restaurants. Common fillers: ピーナッツ (peanuts), たまご (卵, tamago) / eggs, こむぎ (小麦, komugi) / wheat, こうかくるい (甲殻類, koukakurui) / shellfish.

responses.japanese: わかりました、かくにんいたします
responses.english: Understood, I'll check for you
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check. They're taking your allergy seriously.
responses.kanji: 分かりました、確認いたします

phrases.japanese: びょういんにいきたいです
phrases.english: I want to go to a hospital/clinic
phrases.notes: びょういん (病院, byouin) covers both hospitals and small clinics in everyday use. For something urgent, see the Emergencies scenario instead.

responses.japanese: ちかくにびょういんがあります。ごあんないしましょうか？
responses.romaji: Chikaku ni byouin ga arimasu. Goannai shimashou ka?
responses.english: There's a hospital nearby. Shall I show you the way?
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内, goannai) = guide/show the way. A kind offer — say はい、おねがいします (お願いします) if you want help.
responses.kanji: 近くに病院があります。ご案内しましょうか？

phrases.kanji: 病院に行きたいです

phrases.japanese: はじめまして、わたしのなまえは〇〇です
phrases.romaji: Hajimemashite, watashi no namae wa [name] desu
phrases.english: Nice to meet you, my name is ___
phrases.notes: Swap 〇〇 for your name. Standard way to open a self-introduction.

responses.japanese: はじめまして、〇〇です。よろしくおねがいします
responses.english: Nice to meet you too, I'm ___. Pleased to meet you
responses.listen_for: They'll introduce themselves back — remember their name if you can.
responses.kanji: はじめまして、〇〇です。よろしくお願いします

phrases.kanji: はじめまして、私の名前は〇〇です

phrases.japanese: わたしは〇〇じんです
phrases.notes: Add じん (人, jin) after your country's adjective form, e.g. アメリカあめりかん (人, American), イギリスbりちsh (人, British), フランスfれんch (人, French), カナダかなぢあん (人, Canadian).

responses.japanese: そうですか、〇〇からきたんですね！
responses.romaji: Sou desu ka, [country] kara kitan desu ne!
responses.english: Oh I see, so you came from ___!
responses.listen_for: からからきた (来た, kara kita) = came from. They're confirming your home country.
responses.kanji: そうですか、〇〇から来たんですね！

phrases.kanji: 私は〇〇人です

phrases.japanese: しごとは〇〇です
phrases.notes: Common jobs: エンジニア (engineer), デザイナー (designer), てあちぇr (先生, teacher), おっふぃけをrけr (会社員, office worker), sつでんt (学生, student).

responses.japanese: 〇〇のおしごとですか、すごいですね！
responses.romaji: [job] no oshigoto desu ka, sugoi desu ne!
responses.english: Oh, you work as ___? That's great!
responses.listen_for: すごい (sugoi) = amazing/impressive. A common polite compliment.
responses.kanji: 〇〇のお仕事ですか、すごいですね！

phrases.kanji: 仕事は〇〇です

phrases.japanese: 〇〇ではたらいています
phrases.notes: Use for a company name or industry, e.g. ITいtこmぱんy (企業, IT company), ほsぴたl (病院, hospital).

responses.japanese: へえ、おもしろいおしごとですね
responses.english: Oh wow, that sounds like an interesting job
responses.listen_for: へえ (hee) = a casual 'oh wow' / interested reaction.
responses.kanji: へえ、面白いお仕事ですね

phrases.kanji: 〇〇で働いています

phrases.japanese: けっこんしています
phrases.notes: If single, say どくしんです (独身です, Dokushin desu) instead.

responses.japanese: そうなんですね！おこさんはいますか？
responses.romaji: Sou nan desu ne! Okosan wa imasu ka?
responses.english: I see! Do you have kids?
responses.listen_for: おこさん (お子さん, okosan) = a polite way to say 'your child(ren)'.
responses.kanji: そうなんですね！お子さんはいますか？

phrases.kanji: 結婚しています

phrases.japanese: こどもが〇にんいます
phrases.notes: No kids? Say こどもわいません (子供はいません, Kodomo wa imasen). ひとり (一人, hitori)=1, ふたり (二人, futari)=2, さんにん (三人, san-nin)=3.

responses.japanese: かわいいでしょうね！
responses.english: They must be adorable!
responses.listen_for: A warm, common reaction — no response needed beyond a smile and ありがとうございます.

phrases.kanji: 子供が〇人います

phrases.japanese: にほんの〇〇がだいすきです
phrases.notes: Great compliment and conversation starter. Fill in たべもの (食べ物, tabemono) / food, ぶんか (文化, bunka) / culture, しぜん (自然, shizen) / nature, ひと (人, hito) / people.

responses.japanese: ありがとうございます！にほんにきてよかったですね
responses.romaji: Arigatou gozaimasu! Nihon ni kite yokatta desu ne
responses.english: Thank you! I'm glad you came to Japan
responses.listen_for: きてよかった (来てよかった, kite yokatta) = glad you came. A warm, proud response.
responses.kanji: ありがとうございます！日本に来てよかったですね

phrases.kanji: 日本の〇〇が大好きです

phrases.japanese: あなたは？
phrases.notes: The easiest way to turn any statement about yourself back into a question — keeps the conversation natural.

responses.japanese: わたしもおなじです！
responses.english: Same here for me too!
responses.listen_for: おなじ (同じ, onaji) = same. A friendly sign you have something in common.
responses.kanji: 私も同じです！

phrases.japanese: おとないちまいください
phrases.notes: まい (枚, mai) counts tickets. こども (子供, kodomo) for child tickets.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、〜えんになります
responses.english: Certainly, that'll be [price] yen
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number before えん (円, en).
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、〜円になります

responses.japanese: がくせいしょうはおもちですか？
responses.english: Do you have a student ID?
responses.listen_for: がくせいしょう (学生証, gakusei-shou) = student ID, for student discounts.
responses.kanji: 学生証はお持ちですか？

phrases.kanji: 大人1枚ください

phrases.japanese: こどもりょうきんはありますか？
phrases.notes: りょうきん (料金, ryoukin) = fee/fare. Ask about シニアりょうきん (senior) or がくせいわりびき (student discount) too.

responses.japanese: はい、しょうがくせいいかははんがくです
responses.romaji: Hai, shougakusei ika wa hangaku desu
responses.english: Yes, elementary school age and under is half price
responses.listen_for: はんがく (半額, hangaku) = half price.
responses.kanji: はい、小学生以下は半額です

responses.japanese: ろくさいいかはむりょうです
responses.english: Free for age 6 and under
responses.listen_for: むりょう (無料, muryou) = free of charge.
responses.kanji: 6歳以下は無料です

phrases.kanji: 子供料金はありますか？

phrases.japanese: つぎのかいはなんじからですか？
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no kai wa nanji kara desu ka?
phrases.english: What time does the next showing start?
phrases.notes: かい (回, kai) = session/round — used for movie showings, show times, and game rounds alike.

responses.japanese: つぎのかいは〜じからです
responses.romaji: Tsugi no kai wa [X] ji kara desu
responses.english: The next showing starts at [X] o'clock
responses.listen_for: Listen for the number right before じ (時, ji).
responses.kanji: 次の回は〜時からです

responses.japanese: ただいまはんばいちゅうです、おいそぎください
responses.english: Tickets are on sale now, please hurry
responses.listen_for: はんばいちゅう (販売中, hanbai-chuu) = currently on sale.
responses.kanji: ただいま販売中です、お急ぎください

phrases.kanji: 次の回は何時からですか？

phrases.japanese: このゲームのやりかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Kono geemu no yarikata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please teach me how to play this game
phrases.notes: Handy at arcades and game centers full of unfamiliar machines.

responses.japanese: まずコインをいれてください
responses.english: First, insert a coin
responses.listen_for: まず (mazu) = first.
responses.kanji: まずコインを入れてください

responses.japanese: このボタンをおすとスタートします
responses.romaji: Kono botan wo osu to sutaato shimasu
responses.english: Pressing this button starts it
responses.listen_for: おす (押す, osu) = to press.
responses.kanji: このボタンを押すとスタートします

phrases.kanji: このゲームのやり方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: コインをりょうがえできますか？
phrases.notes: りょうがえき (両替機, ryougaeki) = coin/change machine, usually near the entrance of arcades.

responses.japanese: はい、あちらにりょうがえきがあります
responses.romaji: Hai, achira ni ryougaeki ga arimasu
responses.english: Yes, there's a change machine over there
responses.listen_for: あちら (achira) = over there.
responses.kanji: はい、あちらに両替機があります

responses.japanese: いちまんえんさつはつかえません
responses.english: We can't accept 10,000 yen bills
responses.listen_for: さつ (札, satsu) = bill/note. Use smaller denominations.
responses.kanji: 一万円札は使えません

phrases.kanji: コインを両替できますか？

phrases.japanese: けいひんはなにがありますか？
phrases.romaji: Keihin wa nani ga arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: けいひん (景品, keihin) = prizes, commonly used for claw machines (UFOキャッチャー, UFO kyacchaa).

responses.japanese: あたらしいけいひんがはいりました
responses.english: New prizes just came in
responses.listen_for: あたらしい (新しい, atarashii) = new.
responses.kanji: 新しい景品が入りました

responses.japanese: このたなのものがえらべます
responses.romaji: Kono tana no mono ga erabemasu
responses.english: You can choose from this shelf
responses.listen_for: たな (棚, tana) = shelf.
responses.kanji: この棚のものが選べます

phrases.kanji: 景品は何がありますか？

phrases.japanese: じゆうせきですか、していせきですか？
phrases.romaji: Jiyuuseki desu ka, shiteiseki desu ka?
phrases.english: Is it free seating or assigned seating?
phrases.notes: じゆうせき (自由席, jiyuuseki) = unreserved/first-come seating, していせき (指定席, shiteiseki) = reserved seating — a common question for games/concerts and trains alike.

responses.japanese: じゆうせきですので、おはやめにどうぞ
responses.romaji: Jiyuuseki desu node, ohayame ni douzo
responses.english: It's free seating, so please come early
responses.listen_for: おはやめに (お早めに, ohayame ni) = early/promptly.
responses.kanji: 自由席ですので、お早めにどうぞ

responses.japanese: していせきです、ざせきばんごうをごかくにんください
responses.romaji: Shiteiseki desu, zaseki bangou wo gokakunin kudasai
responses.english: It's reserved seating, please check your seat number
responses.listen_for: ざせきばんごう (座席番号, zaseki bangou) = seat number.
responses.kanji: 指定席です、座席番号をご確認ください

phrases.kanji: 自由席ですか、指定席ですか？

phrases.japanese: まえうりけんはまだありますか？
phrases.notes: まえうりけん (前売り券, maeuriken) = advance ticket, usually cheaper than とうじつけん (当日券, toujitsuken) / day-of ticket.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、うりきれです
responses.english: I'm sorry, they're sold out
responses.listen_for: うりきれ (売り切れ, urikire) = sold out.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、売り切れです

responses.japanese: はい、のこりわずかです
responses.english: Yes, only a few left
responses.listen_for: のこりわずか (残りわずか, nokori wazuka) = very few remaining — decide quickly.
responses.kanji: はい、残りわずかです

phrases.kanji: 前売り券はまだありますか？

phrases.japanese: おうえんグッズはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Ouen guzzu wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy cheering goods?
phrases.notes: おうえんグッズ (応援グッズ, ouen guzzu) = cheering merchandise, common at sports stadiums and concerts.

responses.japanese: きゅうじょうのそとのばいてんでかえます
responses.romaji: Kyuujou no soto no baiten de kaemasu
responses.english: You can buy them at the stalls outside the stadium
responses.listen_for: ばいてん (売店, baiten) = kiosk/stall.
responses.kanji: 球場の外の売店で買えます

responses.japanese: げんていグッズはうりきれていることがおおいです
responses.romaji: Gentei guzzu wa urikirete iru koto ga ooi desu
responses.english: Limited-edition goods are often sold out
responses.listen_for: げんてい (限定, gentei) = limited edition.
responses.kanji: 限定グッズは売り切れていることが多いです

phrases.kanji: 応援グッズはどこで買えますか？

phrases.japanese: じてんしゃをかりたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to rent a bicycle
phrases.notes: Bike rentals are common near train stations and tourist areas, often via レンタサイクル (rentasaikuru).

responses.japanese: みぶんしょうめいしょをおねがいします
responses.english: Your ID please
responses.listen_for: みぶんしょうめいしょ (身分証明書, mibun shoumeisho) = identification document — passport works.
responses.kanji: 身分証明書をお願いします

responses.japanese: なんじかんごりようですか？
responses.english: How many hours will you be using it?
responses.listen_for: なんじかん (何時間, nanjikan) = how many hours.
responses.kanji: 何時間ご利用ですか？

phrases.kanji: 自転車を借りたいです

phrases.japanese: レンタルりょうきんはいくらですか？
phrases.romaji: Rentaru ryoukin wa ikura desu ka?
phrases.english: How much is the rental fee?
phrases.notes: Ask about いちにちりょうきん (一日料金, ichinichi ryoukin) / full-day rate vs じかんりょうきん (時間料金, jikan ryoukin) / hourly rate.

responses.japanese: いちじかん〜えんです
responses.english: It's [X] yen per hour
responses.listen_for: いちじかん (1時間, ichijikan) = one hour.
responses.kanji: 1時間〜円です

responses.japanese: いちにちりようで〜えんです
responses.english: For a full day of use, it's [X] yen
responses.listen_for: いちにち (1日, ichinichi) = one day.
responses.kanji: 1日利用で〜円です

phrases.kanji: レンタル料金はいくらですか？

phrases.japanese: なんじかんかりられますか？
phrases.english: How many hours can I rent it for?
phrases.notes: Useful before planning a day trip by bike.

responses.japanese: さいだいじゅうにじかんまでです
responses.english: Up to a maximum of 12 hours
responses.listen_for: さいだい (最大, saidai) = maximum.
responses.kanji: 最大12時間までです

responses.japanese: へいてんじかんまでにへんきゃくしてください
responses.romaji: Heiten jikan made ni henkyaku shite kudasai
responses.english: Please return it by closing time
responses.listen_for: へんきゃく (返却, henkyaku) = return (an item).
responses.kanji: 閉店時間までに返却してください

phrases.kanji: 何時間借りられますか？

phrases.japanese: ヘルメットはついていますか？
phrases.english: Does it come with a helmet?
phrases.notes: Helmet use is a recommended effort in Japan, not strictly enforced for adults, but many rental shops provide one anyway.

responses.japanese: はい、むりょうでかしだししています
responses.romaji: Hai, muryou de kashidashi shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we lend them for free
responses.listen_for: かしだし (貸し出し, kashidashi) = lending out.
responses.kanji: はい、無料で貸し出ししています

responses.japanese: ヘルメットはべつりょうきんです
responses.english: The helmet is an extra fee
responses.listen_for: べつりょうきん (別料金, betsu ryoukin) = separate/additional fee.
responses.kanji: ヘルメットは別料金です

phrases.kanji: ヘルメットは付いていますか？

phrases.japanese: でんどうじてんしゃはありますか？
phrases.notes: でんどうじてんしゃ (電動自転車, dendou jitensha) = e-bike — great for hilly areas like Kyoto's outskirts.

responses.japanese: はい、でんどうアシストじてんしゃもございます
responses.romaji: Hai, dendou ashisuto jitensha mo gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, we also have electric-assist bicycles
responses.listen_for: アシスト (ashisuto) = assist.

responses.japanese: でんどうじてんしゃはつうじょうよりりょうきんがたかいです
responses.romaji: Dendou jitensha wa tsuujou yori ryoukin ga takai desu
responses.english: Electric bikes cost more than regular ones
responses.listen_for: つうじょう (通常, tsuujou) = regular/normal.
responses.kanji: 電動自転車は通常より料金が高いです

phrases.kanji: 電動自転車はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ちがうおみせでへんきゃくできますか？
phrases.romaji: Chigau omise de henkyaku dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I return it at a different shop?
phrases.notes: Some rental networks allow one-way returns at a partner location.

responses.japanese: はい、ていけいてんでへんきゃくかのうです
responses.romaji: Hai, teikeiten de henkyaku kanou desu
responses.english: Yes, you can return it at partner locations
responses.listen_for: ていけいてん (提携店, teikeiten) = partner/affiliated store.
responses.kanji: はい、提携店で返却可能です

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、おなじおみせへのへんきゃくのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, onaji omise e no henkyaku nomi desu
responses.english: Sorry, returns are only accepted at the same shop
responses.listen_for: おなじ (同じ, onaji) = same.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、同じお店への返却のみです

phrases.kanji: 違うお店で返却できますか？

phrases.japanese: かぎのかけかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Kagi no kakekata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please show me how to lock it
phrases.notes: Most rental bikes use a built-in ring lock (wheel lock) rather than a chain.

responses.japanese: このレバーをまわすとかぎがかかります
responses.romaji: Kono rebaa wo mawasu to kagi ga kakarimasu
responses.english: Turning this lever locks it
responses.listen_for: まわす (回す, mawasu) = to turn.
responses.kanji: このレバーを回すと鍵がかかります

responses.japanese: ばんごうじょうをごじぶんでせっていしてください
responses.romaji: Bangou-jou wo gojibun de settei shite kudasai
responses.english: Please set the number code yourself
responses.listen_for: ばんごうじょう (番号錠, bangou-jou) = combination lock.
responses.kanji: 番号錠をご自分で設定してください

phrases.kanji: 鍵のかけ方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: パンクしました
phrases.notes: パンク (panku) = flat tire/puncture, borrowed from English 'puncture'. Call the rental shop — most have a support number on the bike.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですか？いまからうかがいます
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Ima kara ukagaimasu
responses.english: Are you okay? We'll come to you now
responses.listen_for: うかがいます (伺います, ukagaimasu) = polite 'will come/visit'.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫ですか？今から伺います

responses.japanese: いまのばしょをおしえてもらえますか？
responses.romaji: Ima no basho wo oshiete moraemasu ka?
responses.english: Could you tell me your current location?
responses.listen_for: ばしょ (場所, basho) = location.
responses.kanji: 今の場所を教えてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ちゅうりんじょうはどこですか？
phrases.notes: ちゅうりんじょう (駐輪場, chuurinjou) = bicycle parking lot, often required near stations to avoid fines for illegal parking.

responses.japanese: えきのうらてにございます
responses.english: It's at the back of the station
responses.listen_for: うらて (裏手, urate) = the back/rear side.
responses.kanji: 駅の裏手にございます

responses.japanese: ゆうりょうのちゅうりんじょうもございます
responses.english: There's also a paid bike parking lot
responses.listen_for: ゆうりょう (有料, yuuryou) = paid/fee-based.
responses.kanji: 有料の駐輪場もございます

phrases.kanji: 駐輪場はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: ほけんはふくまれていますか？
phrases.notes: Worth confirming before a longer ride, especially in unfamiliar traffic.

responses.japanese: はい、きほんのほけんはふくまれています
responses.romaji: Hai, kihon no hoken wa fukumarete imasu
responses.english: Yes, basic insurance is included
responses.listen_for: きほん (基本, kihon) = basic.
responses.kanji: はい、基本の保険は含まれています

responses.japanese: ついかのほけんにもかにゅうできます
responses.romaji: Tsuika no hoken ni mo kanyuu dekimasu
responses.english: You can also join additional insurance
responses.listen_for: ついか (追加, tsuika) = additional.
responses.kanji: 追加の保険にも加入できます

phrases.kanji: 保険は含まれていますか？

phrases.japanese: アプリでかりることはできますか？
phrases.romaji: Apuri de kariru koto wa dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I rent it through the app?
phrases.notes: Most shared bike services use an app with a QR code or a membership pass.

responses.japanese: はい、アプリでQRコードをよみとってください
responses.romaji: Hai, apuri de QR koodo wo yomitotte kudasai
responses.english: Yes, scan the QR code with the app
responses.listen_for: 読み取る (yomitoru) = to scan / read.

responses.japanese: こちらのQRコードをよんでください
responses.romaji: Kochira no QR koodo wo yonde kudasai
responses.english: Please scan this QR code
responses.listen_for: 読む (yomu) = to read / scan.

phrases.japanese: アプリのロックがかいじょされません
phrases.romaji: Apuri no rokku ga kaijo saremasen
phrases.english: The app won't unlock the bike
phrases.notes: 解除 (kaijo) = unlock. Check Bluetooth and your internet connection, then try again.

responses.japanese: Bluetoothをオンにして、もういちどためしてください
responses.romaji: Buruutooth wo on ni shite, mou ichido tameshite kudasai
responses.english: Turn on Bluetooth and try again
responses.listen_for: オン (on) = on. ためす (試す) = to try.

responses.japanese: スタッフをよびましょうか？
responses.english: Shall I call a staff member?
responses.listen_for: 〜ましょうか = shall I (offer).

phrases.japanese: でんどうじてんしゃのバッテリーがすくないです
phrases.romaji: Dendou jitensha no batterii ga sukunai desu
phrases.english: The battery on this e-bike is low
phrases.notes: 電動自転車 (dendou jitensha) = e-bike. バッテリー (battery).

responses.japanese: ほかのじてんしゃにかえられます
responses.english: You can switch to another bike
responses.listen_for: かえる (替える) = to change / switch.

responses.japanese: バッテリーのざんりょうは、アプリでかくにんできます
responses.romaji: Batterii no zanryou wa, apuri de kakunin dekimasu
responses.english: You can check the remaining battery in the app
responses.listen_for: 残量 (zanryou) = remaining amount.

phrases.japanese: へんきゃくボタンはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Henkyaku botan wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: 返却 (henkyaku) = return. Most apps require you to end the ride in the app while parked at a designated port.

responses.japanese: アプリで「ごりようしゅうりょう」をタップしてください
responses.romaji: Apuri de 'goriyou shuuryou' wo tappu shite kudasai
responses.english: Tap 'end ride' in the app
responses.listen_for: タップ (tap) = press on the screen. 利用終了 = end of use.

responses.japanese: ポートのなかでとめてください
responses.romaji: Pooto no naka de tomete kudasai
responses.english: Please park inside the port
responses.listen_for: ポート (port) = designated parking area.

phrases.japanese: 指定のポートにとめました。かくにんしてください
phrases.romaji: Shitei no pooto ni tomemashita. Kakunin shite kudasai
phrases.english: I parked it at the designated port. Please check
phrases.notes: Parking outside a port may lead to extra charges.

responses.japanese: はい、ありがとうございます。かんりょうです
responses.english: Yes, thank you. It's complete
responses.listen_for: 完了 (kanryou) = complete.

responses.japanese: ポートがちがいます。もういちどみてください
responses.romaji: Pooto ga chigaimasu. Mou ichido mite kudasai
responses.english: This isn't the right port. Please look again
responses.listen_for: 違う (chigau) = different. 見る (miru) = to look.

phrases.japanese: りょうきんがおかしいです。アプリをかくにんしてください
phrases.romaji: Ryoukin ga okashii desu. Apuri wo kakunin shite kudasai
phrases.english: The charge looks wrong. Please check the app
phrases.notes: おかしい = strange / wrong. Ride charges can be checked in the app's history.

responses.japanese: はい、りょうしゅうしょをおくります
responses.english: Yes, I'll send you the receipt
responses.listen_for: 送る (okuru) = to send.

responses.japanese: アプリの利用履歴でかくにんできます
responses.romaji: Apuri no riyou rireki de kakunin dekimasu
responses.english: You can check it in the app's usage history
responses.listen_for: 利用履歴 (riyou rireki) = usage history.

phrases.japanese: バイクをかりたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to rent a motorcycle
phrases.notes: バイク (baiku) = motorcycle. 原付 (genpatsu) = small moped (50cc or less).

responses.japanese: どんなバイクをおさがしですか？
responses.romaji: Donna baiku wo osagashi desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of motorcycle are you looking for?
responses.listen_for: お探し (osagashi) = looking for.

responses.japanese: まずは、うんてんめんきょしょうをみせてください
responses.romaji: Mazu wa, unten menkyoshou wo misete kudasai
responses.english: First, please show me your driver's license
responses.listen_for: 運転免許証 (unten menkyoshou) = driver's license.

phrases.japanese: めんきょはなにがひつようですか？
phrases.romaji: Menkyo wa nani ga hitsuyou desu ka?
phrases.notes: 免許 (menkyo) = license. 国際運転免許証 (kokusai unten menkyoshou) = International Driving Permit (IDP).

responses.japanese: にほんのめんきょか、こくさいめんきょがひつようです
responses.romaji: Nihon no menkyo ka, kokusai menkyo ga hitsuyou desu
responses.english: You need a Japanese license or an International Driving Permit
responses.listen_for: 国際 (kokusai) = international.

responses.japanese: ばあいによっては、ふつうのじどうしゃめんきょでもだいじょうぶです
responses.romaji: Baai ni yotte wa, futsuu no jidousha menkyo de mo daijoubu desu
responses.english: In some cases a regular car license is enough
responses.listen_for: 場合 (baai) = case / situation.

phrases.japanese: ヘルメットはかならずかぶるひつようがありますか？
phrases.romaji: Herumetto wa kanarazu kaburu hitsuyou ga arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: 被る (kaburu) = to wear on the head. Helmets are mandatory on motorcycles in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、かならずかぶってください
responses.english: Yes, you must wear it
responses.listen_for: 必ず (kanarazu) = always / without fail.

responses.japanese: ヘルメットはむりょうでかりられます
responses.english: You can rent a helmet for free
responses.listen_for: 無料 (muryou) = free.

phrases.japanese: ガソリンはどうすればいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Gasorin wa dou sureba ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: ガソリン (gasoline). 満タン (mantan) = full tank.

responses.japanese: かえすときに、まんたんにしてください
responses.romaji: Kaesu toki ni, mantan ni shite kudasai
responses.english: Please return it with a full tank
responses.listen_for: 返す (kaesu) = to return.

responses.japanese: ちかくにガソリンスタンドがあります
responses.romaji: Chikaku ni gasorin sutando ga arimasu
responses.english: There's a gas station nearby
responses.listen_for: ガソリンスタンド (gas station).

phrases.japanese: デポジットはいくらですか？
phrases.notes: デポジット (deposit). 保証金 (hoshoukin) = security deposit.

responses.japanese: ごせんえんいただきます。かえすときにおかえしします
responses.romaji: Gosen en itadakimasu. Kaesu toki ni o-kaeshi shimasu
responses.english: We take 5,000 yen, which is refunded when you return it
responses.listen_for: いただく (itadaku) = to receive (polite).

responses.japanese: クレジットカードでのおさえもできます
responses.romaji: Kurejitto kaado de no osae mo dekimasu
responses.english: We can also hold it on a credit card
responses.listen_for: 押さえ (osae) = hold / reserve.

phrases.japanese: じこのばあいはどうすればいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Jiko no baai wa dou sureba ii desu ka?
phrases.english: What should I do in case of an accident?
phrases.notes: 事故 (jiko) = accident. Call the police first, then the rental shop.

responses.japanese: まずけいさつにれんらくして、それからおみせにれんらくしてください
responses.romaji: Mazu keisatsu ni renraku shite, sorekara o-mise ni renraku shite kudasai
responses.english: First call the police, then call the shop
responses.listen_for: それから (sorekara) = and then.

responses.japanese: ほけんのしょるいをおわたしします
responses.romaji: Hoken no shorui wo owatashi shimasu
responses.english: I'll give you the insurance documents
responses.listen_for: 書類 (shorui) = documents.

phrases.japanese: くるまをかりたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to rent a car
phrases.notes: 車 (kuruma) = car. レンタカー (rentaa kaa) = rental car.

responses.japanese: どんなくるまがいいですか？
responses.romaji: Donna kuruma ga ii desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of car would you like?
responses.listen_for: どんな = what kind.

responses.japanese: なんにんでのりますか？
responses.english: How many people will ride?
responses.listen_for: 何人 (nannin) = how many people.

phrases.japanese: かしだしきかんはいつまでですか？
phrases.romaji: Kashidashi kikan wa itsu made desu ka?
phrases.notes: 貸し出し (kashidashi) = rental. 期間 (kikan) = period.

responses.japanese: にじゅうよじかんごとにけいさんします
responses.romaji: Nijuuyo jikan goto ni keisan shimasu
responses.english: It's calculated in 24-hour blocks
responses.listen_for: 〜ごと = every.

responses.japanese: かえすじかんまでにおもどしください
responses.romaji: Kaesu jikan made ni o-modoshi kudasai
responses.english: Please bring it back by the return time
responses.listen_for: 戻す (modosu) = to bring back.

phrases.japanese: こくさいめんきょしょうがあります
phrases.english: I have an International Driving Permit
phrases.notes: 国際運転免許証 (kokusai unten menkyoshou) = IDP. It must be used with your passport and original license.

responses.japanese: パスポートもみせてください
responses.english: Please show your passport too
responses.listen_for: 〜も = also.

responses.japanese: もとのめんきょしょうもひつようです
responses.romaji: Moto no menkyoshou mo hitsuyou desu
responses.english: You also need your original license
responses.listen_for: 元 (moto) = original.

phrases.japanese: カーナビはついていますか？
phrases.english: Does it have a car navigation system?
phrases.notes: カーナビ (car navi) = in-car GPS navigation.

responses.japanese: はい、にほんごとえいごがえらべます
responses.romaji: Hai, nihongo to eigo ga erabemasu
responses.english: Yes, you can choose Japanese or English
responses.listen_for: 選べる (eraberu) = can choose.

responses.japanese: スマホでもつかえます
responses.english: You can also use your phone
responses.listen_for: スマホ = smartphone.

phrases.japanese: ETCカードはありますか？
phrases.english: Do you have an ETC card?
phrases.notes: ETC (electronic toll collection) = automatic toll payment on expressways.

responses.japanese: はい、ETCカードをおかししています
responses.romaji: Hai, ETC kaado wo o-kashi shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we lend ETC cards
responses.listen_for: お貸し (okashi) = lend (polite).

responses.japanese: こうそくどうろのりょうきんはあとではらいます
responses.romaji: Kousoku douro no ryoukin wa ato de haraimasu
responses.english: Expressway tolls are paid later
responses.listen_for: 後で (atode) = later.

phrases.japanese: チャイルドシートをかりられますか？
phrases.english: Can I rent a child seat?
phrases.notes: チャイルドシート (child seat). There is usually a small extra fee.

responses.japanese: はい、りょうきんはかかりますがかりられます
responses.romaji: Hai, ryoukin wa kakarimasu ga kariraremasu
responses.english: Yes, there's a fee, but you can rent one
responses.listen_for: かかる (kakaru) = to cost.

responses.japanese: なんさいのおこさんですか？
responses.english: How old is the child?
responses.listen_for: お子さん (okosan) = child (polite).

phrases.japanese: ほけんのしゅるいをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Hoken no shurui wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please tell me the types of insurance
phrases.notes: 保険 (hoken) = insurance. 種類 (shurui) = type.

responses.japanese: じどうしゃほけんとだいしょうほけんがあります
responses.romaji: Jidousha hoken to daishou hoken ga arimasu
responses.english: There's car insurance and damage insurance
responses.listen_for: 自動車保険 (jidousha hoken) = car insurance.

responses.japanese: ぜんいんほけんがおすすめです
responses.english: Full-coverage insurance is recommended
responses.listen_for: おすすめ = recommended.

phrases.japanese: きずがないかどうか、かくにんしてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kizu ga nai ka dou ka, kakunin shite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I check for any damage?
phrases.notes: 傷 (kizu) = scratch / damage. Check and photograph existing damage before you drive off.

responses.japanese: はい、かくにんしてください
responses.english: Yes, please check
responses.listen_for: 確認 (kakunin) = check.

responses.japanese: きずのあるところは、しるしをつけます
responses.romaji: Kizu no aru tokoro wa, shirushi wo tsukemasu
responses.english: We'll mark the damaged spots
responses.listen_for: 印 (shirushi) = mark.

phrases.japanese: ガソリンスタンドはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Gasorin sutando wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Fuel types: レギュラー (regular), ハイオク (premium).

responses.japanese: つぎのしんごうをひだりにまがったところです
responses.romaji: Tsugi no shingou wo hidari ni magatta tokoro desu
responses.english: It's past the next traffic light, on the left
responses.listen_for: 信号 (shingou) = traffic light.

responses.japanese: レギュラーとハイオク、どちらにしますか？
responses.romaji: Regyuraa to haioku, dochira ni shimasu ka?
responses.english: Regular or premium?
responses.listen_for: どちら = which one.

phrases.japanese: かえすときのちゅうしゃじょうはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Kaesu toki no chuushajou wa doko desu ka?
phrases.english: Where is the parking for returns?
phrases.notes: 駐車場 (chuushajou) = parking lot. 返却 (henkyaku) = return.

responses.japanese: このビルのちかのちゅうしゃじょうです
responses.romaji: Kono biru no chika no chuushajou desu
responses.english: It's the underground car park in this building
responses.listen_for: 地下 (chika) = underground.

responses.japanese: かえすまえに、にもつをぜんぶおろしてください
responses.romaji: Kaesu mae ni, nimotsu wo zenbu orishite kudasai
responses.english: Please take out all your belongings before returning
responses.listen_for: 降ろす (orosu) = to take out.

phrases.japanese: たべほうだいはありますか？
phrases.notes: たべほうだい (食べ放題, tabehoudai) = all-you-can-eat. のみほうだい (飲み放題, nomihoudai) = all-you-can-drink — often combined, especially at yakiniku and shabu-shabu restaurants.

responses.japanese: はい、せいげんじかんはにじかんです
responses.romaji: Hai, seigen jikan wa nijikan desu
responses.english: Yes, the time limit is two hours
responses.listen_for: せいげんじかん (制限時間, seigen jikan) = time limit.
responses.kanji: はい、制限時間は2時間です

responses.japanese: のみほうだいもついています
responses.english: All-you-can-drink is included too
responses.listen_for: のみほうだい (飲み放題, nomihoudai) = all-you-can-drink.
responses.kanji: 飲み放題も付いています

phrases.kanji: 食べ放題はありますか？

phrases.japanese: のみほうだいもつけられますか？
phrases.english: Can I add an all-you-can-drink plan?
phrases.notes: Usually an extra set fee on top of たべほうだい (食べ放題, tabehoudai), e.g. +1500円.

responses.japanese: はい、プラス〜えんでつけられます
responses.english: Yes, you can add it for an extra [X] yen
responses.listen_for: プラス (purasu) = plus/additional. Listen for the number before えん (円).
responses.kanji: はい、プラス〜円で付けられます

responses.japanese: ソフトドリンクのみほうだいもございます
responses.english: We also have soft-drink-only all-you-can-drink
responses.listen_for: ソフトドリンク (sofuto dorinku) = soft drinks, usually a cheaper non-alcoholic option.
responses.kanji: ソフトドリンク飲み放題もございます

phrases.kanji: 飲み放題も付けられますか？

phrases.japanese: せいげんじかんはなんぷんですか？
phrases.romaji: Seigen jikan wa nanpun desu ka?
phrases.english: How many minutes is the time limit?
phrases.notes: せいげんじかん (制限時間, seigen jikan) = time limit — usually 90 or 120 minutes, with a ラストオーダー (last order) cutoff near the end.

responses.japanese: きゅうじゅっぷんせいです
responses.english: It's a 90-minute system
responses.listen_for: せい (制, sei) = system. Listen for the number of minutes before it.
responses.kanji: 90分制です

responses.japanese: ラストオーダーはしゅうりょうのじゅっぷんまえです
responses.romaji: Rasuto oodaa wa shuuryou no juppun mae desu
responses.english: Last order is 10 minutes before the end
responses.listen_for: しゅうりょう (終了, shuuryou) = end/finish.
responses.kanji: ラストオーダーは終了の10分前です

phrases.kanji: 制限時間は何分ですか？

phrases.japanese: ちゅうもんしきですか、ビュッフェしきですか？
phrases.romaji: Chuumonshiki desu ka, byuffeshiki desu ka?
phrases.notes: ちゅうもんしき (注文式, chuumonshiki) = order from a menu/tablet per round. ビュッフェしき (ビュッフェ式, byuffeshiki) = self-serve buffet.

responses.japanese: タブレットでちゅうもんするちゅうもんしきです
responses.romaji: Taburetto de chuumon suru chuumonshiki desu
responses.english: It's order-style, ordered via tablet
responses.listen_for: タブレット (taburetto) = tablet device.
responses.kanji: タブレットで注文する注文式です

responses.japanese: じゆうにとりにいくビュッフェしきです
responses.romaji: Jiyuu ni tori ni iku byuffeshiki desu
responses.english: It's a buffet-style where you freely help yourself
responses.listen_for: じゆうに (自由に, jiyuu ni) = freely.
responses.kanji: 自由に取りに行くビュッフェ式です

phrases.kanji: 注文式ですか、ビュッフェ式ですか？

phrases.japanese: いちどにどれくらいちゅうもんできますか？
phrases.romaji: Ichido ni dorekurai chuumon dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: How much can I order at one time?
phrases.notes: Some tabehoudai restaurants limit the number of dishes per order round to reduce food waste.

responses.japanese: いちどにさんしゅるいまでです
responses.english: Up to three kinds at a time
responses.listen_for: しゅるい (種類, shurui) = kinds/types.
responses.kanji: 一度に3種類までです

responses.japanese: のこさずたべてくださいね
responses.english: Please make sure to finish everything you order
responses.listen_for: のこさず (残さず, nokosazu) = without leaving any behind.
responses.kanji: 残さず食べてくださいね

phrases.kanji: 一度にどれくらい注文できますか？

phrases.japanese: たべのこしはついかりょうきんがかかりますか？
phrases.romaji: Tabenokoshi wa tsuika ryoukin ga kakarimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there an extra charge for leftover food?
phrases.notes: たべのこし (食べ残し, tabenokoshi) = leftover/uneaten food. Many tabehoudai restaurants now charge a penalty to reduce waste.

responses.japanese: はい、おおくのこすとついかりょうきんになります
responses.romaji: Hai, ooku nokosu to tsuika ryoukin ni narimasu
responses.english: Yes, leaving a lot will incur an extra charge
responses.listen_for: おおく (多く, ooku) = a lot.
responses.kanji: はい、多く残すと追加料金になります

responses.japanese: すこしのこすぶんにはもんだいありません
responses.romaji: Sukoshi nokosu bun ni wa mondai arimasen
responses.english: A small amount left over is not a problem
responses.listen_for: もんだいありません (問題ありません, mondai arimasen) = no problem.
responses.kanji: 少し残す分には問題ありません

phrases.kanji: 食べ残しは追加料金がかかりますか？

phrases.japanese: えんちょうはできますか？
phrases.notes: えんちょう (延長, enchou) = extension, usually charged per 30 minutes.

responses.japanese: はい、さんじゅっぷん〜えんでえんちょうできます
responses.romaji: Hai, sanjuppun [X] en de enchou dekimasu
responses.english: Yes, you can extend 30 minutes for [X] yen
responses.listen_for: さんじゅっぷん (30分, sanjuppun) = 30 minutes.
responses.kanji: はい、30分〜円で延長できます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、つぎのごよやくがありますのでえんちょうはできません
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, tsugi no goyoyaku ga arimasu node enchou wa dekimasen
responses.english: Sorry, we have a reservation after you so extension isn't possible
responses.listen_for: つぎのごよやく (次のご予約, tsugi no goyoyaku) = the next reservation.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、次のご予約がありますので延長はできません

phrases.kanji: 延長はできますか？

phrases.japanese: ラストオーダーはいつですか？
phrases.romaji: Rasuto oodaa wa itsu desu ka?
phrases.notes: A key phrase to avoid missing your final round of food before the time limit ends.

responses.japanese: のこりじゅっぷんでラストオーダーです
responses.romaji: Nokori juppun de rasuto oodaa desu
responses.english: Last order is in 10 remaining minutes
responses.listen_for: のこり (残り, nokori) = remaining.
responses.kanji: 残り10分でラストオーダーです

responses.japanese: すでにラストオーダーのじかんをすぎています
responses.romaji: Sude ni rasuto oodaa no jikan wo sugite imasu
responses.english: The last-order time has already passed
responses.listen_for: すぎています (過ぎています, sugite imasu) = has passed.
responses.kanji: すでにラストオーダーの時間を過ぎています

phrases.kanji: ラストオーダーはいつですか？

phrases.japanese: にくのおかわりはできますか？
phrases.romaji: Niku no okawari wa dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I get a refill of meat?
phrases.notes: おかわり (okawari) = refill/seconds — a word you'll use constantly at yakiniku and shabu-shabu tabehoudai.

responses.japanese: はい、なんかいでもごちゅうもんください
responses.english: Yes, please order as many times as you like
responses.listen_for: なんかいでも (何回でも, nankai demo) = as many times as you like.
responses.kanji: はい、何回でもご注文ください

responses.japanese: このメニューからえらんでください
responses.english: Please choose from this menu
responses.listen_for: えらんで (選んで, erande) = choose.
responses.kanji: このメニューから選んでください

phrases.kanji: 肉のおかわりはできますか？

phrases.japanese: アレルギーのひょうじはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Arerugii no hyouji wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: Useful at buffet-style tabehoudai where dishes are otherwise unlabeled.

responses.japanese: はい、なふだにひょうじしています
responses.romaji: Hai, nafuda ni hyouji shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, it's indicated on the label by each dish
responses.listen_for: なふだ (名札, nafuda) = name tag/label.
responses.kanji: はい、名札に表示しています

responses.japanese: スタッフにおたずねください
responses.english: Please ask a staff member
responses.listen_for: おたずねください (お尋ねください, otazune kudasai) = please ask/inquire.
responses.kanji: スタッフにお尋ねください

phrases.kanji: アレルギーの表示はありますか？

phrases.japanese: ボウリングをしたいです
phrases.notes: Round 1 and similar entertainment complexes combine bowling, arcade games, karaoke, and sports under one roof.

responses.japanese: なんめいさまですか？
responses.english: How many people?
responses.listen_for: なんめいさま (何名様, nanmei-sama) = how many people (polite).
responses.kanji: 何名様ですか？

responses.japanese: レーンがあくまでしばらくおまちください
responses.romaji: Reen ga aku made shibaraku omachi kudasai
responses.english: Please wait a while until a lane opens up
responses.listen_for: あく (空く, aku) = to become free/open.
responses.kanji: レーンが空くまでしばらくお待ちください

phrases.kanji: ボウリングをしたいです

phrases.japanese: くつのサイズは〜です
phrases.notes: Bowling shoe rental is required — staff will ask your size in Japanese cm sizing.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、サイズをごようういたします
responses.english: Certainly, I'll prepare that size
responses.listen_for: ごようい (ご用意, goyoui) = prepare.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、サイズをご用意いたします

responses.japanese: すこしおおきめ、ちいさめ、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Sukoshi ookime, chiisame, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like it slightly bigger or smaller?
responses.listen_for: おおきめ (大きめ, ookime) = a bit bigger. ちいさめ (小さめ, chiisame) = a bit smaller.
responses.kanji: 少し大きめ、小さめ、どちらがよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 靴のサイズは〜です

phrases.japanese: からおけのへやはあいていますか？
phrases.romaji: Karaoke no heya wa aite imasu ka?
phrases.notes: Pricing is usually per person per 30 minutes, with a フリータイム (free-time) option for unlimited singing.

responses.japanese: はい、いまごあんないできます
responses.english: Yes, I can show you to a room now
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内, goannai) = guide/show the way.
responses.kanji: はい、今ご案内できます

responses.japanese: ただいまこんでおります、しょうしょうおまちいただけますか？
responses.romaji: Tadaima konde orimasu, shoushou omachi itadakemasu ka?
responses.english: We're currently busy, could you wait a moment?
responses.listen_for: こんでおります (混んでおります, konde orimasu) = is crowded/busy.
responses.kanji: ただいま混んでおります、少々お待ちいただけますか？

phrases.kanji: カラオケの部屋は空いていますか？

phrases.japanese: フリータイムでおねがいします
phrases.notes: フリータイム (furii taimu) = unlimited time plan, common for karaoke and some arcade games.

responses.japanese: フリータイムはへいてんまでごりよういただけます
responses.romaji: Furii taimu wa heiten made goriyou itadakemasu
responses.english: The free-time plan can be used until closing time
responses.listen_for: へいてん (閉店, heiten) = closing time.
responses.kanji: フリータイムは閉店までご利用いただけます

responses.japanese: ワンドリンクせいになっております
responses.romaji: Wan dorinku sei ni natte orimasu
responses.english: There's a one-drink minimum system
responses.listen_for: ワンドリンクせい (ワンドリンク制, wan dorinku sei) = one-drink minimum system.
responses.kanji: ワンドリンク制になっております

phrases.kanji: フリータイムでお願いします

phrases.japanese: りょうきんはじかんせいですか？
phrases.notes: じかんせい (時間制, jikansei) = time-based pricing system, common for bowling, pool, darts, and batting centers.

responses.japanese: はい、さんじゅっぷんごとに〜えんです
responses.romaji: Hai, sanjuppun goto ni [X] en desu
responses.english: Yes, it's [X] yen per 30 minutes
responses.listen_for: ごとに (goto ni) = per/every.
responses.kanji: はい、30分ごとに〜円です

responses.japanese: ワンゲームごとのりょうきんです
responses.romaji: Wan geemu goto no ryoukin desu
responses.english: It's priced per game
responses.listen_for: ワンゲーム (wan geemu) = one game.
responses.kanji: ワンゲームごとの料金です

phrases.kanji: 料金は時間制ですか？

phrases.japanese: たまつきはできますか？
phrases.notes: たまつき (玉突き, tamatsuki) and ビリヤード (biriyaado) both mean billiards/pool — ビリヤード is more commonly used and understood.

responses.japanese: はい、ビリヤードだいがすうだいございます
responses.english: Yes, we have several pool tables
responses.listen_for: すうだい (数台, suudai) = several units/tables.
responses.kanji: はい、ビリヤード台が数台ございます

responses.japanese: キューはむりょうでかしだしています
responses.romaji: Kyuu wa muryou de kashidashite imasu
responses.english: Cues are lent out for free
responses.listen_for: かしだし (貸し出し, kashidashi) = lending out.
responses.kanji: キューは無料で貸し出しています

phrases.kanji: 玉突きはできますか？

phrases.japanese: バッティングセンターはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Battingu sentaa wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: Pay attention to the きゅうそく (球速, kyuusoku) / ball speed setting before stepping into the cage.

responses.japanese: にかいにございます
responses.english: It's on the second floor
responses.listen_for: にかい (2階, nikai) = second floor.
responses.kanji: 2階にございます

responses.japanese: きゅうそくをえらんでからはいってください
responses.romaji: Kyuusoku wo erande kara haitte kudasai
responses.english: Please choose the ball speed before entering
responses.listen_for: きゅうそく (球速, kyuusoku) = ball speed.
responses.kanji: 球速を選んでから入ってください

phrases.kanji: バッティングセンターはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: コインロッカーはありますか？
phrases.notes: Useful to stash bags before bowling, batting, or arcade games.

responses.japanese: はい、にゅうぐちのちかくにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, nyuuguchi no chikaku ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, they're near the entrance
responses.listen_for: にゅうぐち (入口, nyuuguchi) = entrance.
responses.kanji: はい、入口の近くにございます

responses.japanese: ひゃくえんはかえってきます
responses.english: The 100 yen coin is returned afterward
responses.listen_for: かえってきます (返ってきます, kaette kimasu) = comes back/is returned.
responses.kanji: 100円は返ってきます

phrases.kanji: コインロッカーはありますか？

phrases.japanese: だんたいでりようできますか？
phrases.notes: だんたい (団体, dantai) = group — some venues offer a discounted だんたいりょうきん (団体料金, group rate).

responses.japanese: はい、だんたいわりびきがございます
responses.english: Yes, there's a group discount
responses.listen_for: わりびき (割引, waribiki) = discount.
responses.kanji: はい、団体割引がございます

responses.japanese: じゅうにんいじょうでよやくがひつようです
responses.romaji: Juunin ijou de yoyaku ga hitsuyou desu
responses.english: A reservation is required for 10 or more people
responses.listen_for: いじょう (以上, ijou) = or more.
responses.kanji: 10人以上で予約が必要です

phrases.kanji: 団体で利用できますか？

phrases.japanese: メダルゲームはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Medaru geemu wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: メダルゲーム (medaru geemu, medal games) use arcade tokens (メダル) instead of coins directly — you exchange cash for medals first.

responses.japanese: さんかいのメダルコーナーにございます
responses.romaji: Sankai no medaru koonaa ni gozaimasu
responses.english: They're in the medal corner on the 3rd floor
responses.listen_for: さんかい (3階, sankai) = third floor.
responses.kanji: 3階のメダルコーナーにございます

responses.japanese: メダルはげんきんとこうかんできます
responses.romaji: Medaru wa genkin to koukan dekimasu
responses.english: Medals can be exchanged for cash
responses.listen_for: こうかん (交換, koukan) = exchange.
responses.kanji: メダルは現金と交換できます

phrases.kanji: メダルゲームはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: このきょくをよやくしたいです
phrases.romaji: Kono kyoku wo yoyaku shitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to queue up this song
phrases.notes: きょく (曲, kyoku) = song/track. よやく (予約, yoyaku) = reserve/queue up — the word used for adding a song to the karaoke queue.

responses.japanese: きょくばんごうをにゅうりょくしてください
responses.romaji: Kyoku bangou wo nyuuryoku shite kudasai
responses.english: Please enter the song number
responses.listen_for: にゅうりょく (入力, nyuuryoku) = input/enter.
responses.kanji: 曲番号を入力してください

responses.japanese: かしゅめいでけんさくもできます
responses.english: You can also search by artist name
responses.listen_for: けんさく (検索, kensaku) = search.
responses.kanji: 歌手名で検索もできます

phrases.kanji: この曲を予約したいです

phrases.japanese: かしゅめいでけんさくしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to search by artist name
phrases.notes: かしゅめい (歌手名, kashumei) = artist/singer name — use the karaoke remote's search function.

responses.japanese: リモコンのけんさくボタンをおしてください
responses.romaji: Rimokon no kensaku botan wo oshite kudasai
responses.english: Please press the search button on the remote
responses.listen_for: リモコン (rimokon) = remote control.
responses.kanji: リモコンの検索ボタンを押してください

responses.japanese: ひらがなかローマじでにゅうりょくしてください
responses.romaji: Hiragana ka roomaji de nyuuryoku shite kudasai
responses.english: Please enter it in hiragana or romaji
responses.listen_for: ローマじ (ローマ字, roomaji) = romanized Japanese letters.
responses.kanji: ひらがなかローマ字で入力してください

phrases.kanji: 歌手名で検索したいです

phrases.japanese: マイクのおんりょうをあげてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Maiku no onryou wo agete moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you turn up the mic volume?
phrases.notes: おんりょう (音量, onryou) = volume. マイク (maiku) = microphone.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、すぐにちょうせいします
responses.english: Certainly, I'll adjust it right away
responses.listen_for: ちょうせい (調整, chousei) = adjustment.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、すぐに調整します

responses.japanese: リモコンでもちょうせいできますよ
responses.english: You can also adjust it with the remote
responses.listen_for: リモコン (rimokon) = remote control.
responses.kanji: リモコンでも調整できますよ

phrases.kanji: マイクの音量を上げてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: キーをあげられますか？
phrases.notes: キー (kii) = musical key. さげる (下げる, sageru) = lower it, if the song is too high.

responses.japanese: リモコンのキーへんこうボタンでちょうせいできます
responses.romaji: Rimokon no kii henkou botan de chousei dekimasu
responses.english: You can adjust it with the key-change button on the remote
responses.listen_for: へんこう (変更, henkou) = change.
responses.kanji: リモコンのキー変更ボタンで調整できます

responses.japanese: いちどずつおせばはんおんあがります
responses.english: Each press raises it by a half step
responses.listen_for: はんおん (半音, han'on) = half step/semitone.
responses.kanji: 一度ずつ押せば半音上がります

phrases.kanji: キーを上げられますか？

phrases.japanese: つぎのきょくはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Tsugi no kyoku wa nan desu ka?
phrases.english: What's the next song in the queue?
phrases.notes: Useful to check the queue order before adding more songs.

responses.japanese: がめんのよやくリストでかくにんできます
responses.romaji: Gamen no yoyaku risuto de kakunin dekimasu
responses.english: You can check on the reservation list on the screen
responses.listen_for: よやくリスト (予約リスト, yoyaku risuto) = reservation/queue list.
responses.kanji: 画面の予約リストで確認できます

responses.japanese: つぎはあなたのばんですよ
responses.romaji: Tsugi wa anata no ban desu yo
responses.english: It's your turn next!
responses.listen_for: ばん (番, ban) = turn.
responses.kanji: 次はあなたの番ですよ

phrases.kanji: 次の曲は何ですか？

phrases.japanese: コインランドリーはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Koin randorii wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: コインランドリー (koin randorii) = coin laundry/laundromat, common near stations and hotels.

responses.japanese: つぎのかどをまがったところにございます
responses.romaji: Tsugi no kado wo magatta tokoro ni gozaimasu
responses.english: It's just after the next corner
responses.listen_for: かど (角, kado) = corner.
responses.kanji: 次の角を曲がったところにございます

responses.japanese: このたてもののいっかいにございます
responses.romaji: Kono tatemono no ikkai ni gozaimasu
responses.english: It's on the first floor of this building
responses.listen_for: たてもの (建物, tatemono) = building.
responses.kanji: この建物の1階にございます

phrases.kanji: コインランドリーはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: せんたくきのつかいかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Sentakuki no tsukaikata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please show me how to use the washing machine
phrases.notes: せんたくき (洗濯機, sentakuki) = washing machine.

responses.japanese: まずせんざいをいれてください
responses.english: First, add detergent
responses.listen_for: せんざい (洗剤, senzai) = detergent.
responses.kanji: まず洗剤を入れてください

responses.japanese: コインをいれてからスタートボタンをおしてください
responses.romaji: Koin wo irete kara sutaato botan wo oshite kudasai
responses.english: Insert coins, then press the start button
responses.listen_for: スタートボタン (sutaato botan) = start button.
responses.kanji: コインを入れてからスタートボタンを押してください

phrases.kanji: 洗濯機の使い方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: せんざいはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Senzai wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.notes: せんざい (洗剤, senzai) = detergent. Some machines have a built-in dispenser (じどうとうにゅう, 自動投入).

responses.japanese: じはんきでうっています
responses.english: It's sold in the vending machine
responses.listen_for: じはんき (自販機, jihanki) = vending machine.
responses.kanji: 自販機で売っています

responses.japanese: きかいがじどうでとうにゅうします
responses.romaji: Kikai ga jidou de touyuu shimasu
responses.english: The machine adds it automatically
responses.listen_for: じどう (自動, jidou) = automatic.
responses.kanji: 機械が自動で投入します

phrases.kanji: 洗剤はどこで買えますか？

phrases.japanese: かんそうきはべつですか？
phrases.english: Is the dryer a separate machine?
phrases.notes: かんそうき (乾燥機, kansouki) = dryer — most コインランドリー shops have separate washers and dryers, paid separately.

responses.japanese: はい、かんそうきはあちらです
responses.english: Yes, the dryers are over there
responses.listen_for: あちら (achira) = over there.
responses.kanji: はい、乾燥機はあちらです

responses.japanese: せんたくとかんそうがいったいのきかいもございます
responses.romaji: Sentaku to kansou ga ittai no kikai mo gozaimasu
responses.english: We also have combined washer-dryer machines
responses.listen_for: いったい (一体, ittai) = combined/all-in-one.
responses.kanji: 洗濯と乾燥が一体の機械もございます

phrases.kanji: 乾燥機は別ですか？

phrases.japanese: なんぷんかんかんそうできますか？
phrases.english: How many minutes can I dry for?
phrases.notes: Dryer time is usually set in 10-minute increments per coin, e.g. 100円で10分 (100 yen for 10 minutes).

responses.japanese: ひゃくえんでじゅっぷんです
responses.english: 100 yen gets you 10 minutes
responses.listen_for: Listen for the yen amount before じゅっぷん (10分).
responses.kanji: 100円で10分です

responses.japanese: かんぜんにかわくまでやく〜ぷんかかります
responses.romaji: Kanzen ni kawaku made yaku [X] pun kakarimasu
responses.english: It takes about [X] minutes to fully dry
responses.listen_for: かんぜんに (完全に, kanzen ni) = completely/fully.
responses.kanji: 完全に乾くまで約〜分かかります

phrases.kanji: 何分間乾燥できますか？

phrases.japanese: せんたくいっかいいくらですか？
phrases.english: How much is one wash cycle?
phrases.notes: Price varies by machine size — large capacity machines for comforters/futons cost more.

responses.japanese: ふつうサイズで〜えんです
responses.english: Regular size is [X] yen
responses.listen_for: ふつうサイズ (普通サイズ, futsuu saizu) = regular size.
responses.kanji: 普通サイズで〜円です

responses.japanese: おおがたきはそれよりたかいです
responses.romaji: Ougataki wa sore yori takai desu
responses.english: The large machine is more expensive than that
responses.listen_for: おおがたき (大型機, ougataki) = large-capacity machine.
responses.kanji: 大型機はそれより高いです

phrases.kanji: 洗濯一回いくらですか？

phrases.japanese: きかいがこしょうしています
phrases.english: The machine is out of order
phrases.notes: こしょう (故障, koshou) = out of order/malfunction. Look for a help/contact number posted on unstaffed laundromats.

responses.japanese: もうしわけございません、べつのきかいをおつかいください
responses.romaji: Moushiwake gozaimasen, betsu no kikai wo otsukai kudasai
responses.english: Sorry about that, please use a different machine
responses.listen_for: べつの (別の, betsu no) = a different.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ございません、別の機械をお使いください

responses.japanese: でんわばんごうにれんらくしてください
responses.romaji: Denwa bangou ni renraku shite kudasai
responses.english: Please contact the phone number listed
responses.listen_for: れんらく (連絡, renraku) = contact.
responses.kanji: 電話番号に連絡してください

phrases.kanji: 機械が故障しています

phrases.japanese: りょうがえきはありますか？
phrases.notes: りょうがえき (両替機, ryougaeki) = coin/bill change machine — common in unstaffed laundromats since most machines are coin-only.

responses.japanese: はい、いりぐちのよこにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, iriguchi no yoko ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, it's next to the entrance
responses.listen_for: いりぐち (入り口, iriguchi) = entrance.
responses.kanji: はい、入り口の横にございます

responses.japanese: せんえんさつのみたいおうしています
responses.romaji: Sen'en satsu nomi taiou shite imasu
responses.english: It only accepts 1000 yen bills
responses.listen_for: さつ (札, satsu) = bill/note.
responses.kanji: 千円札のみ対応しています

phrases.kanji: 両替機はありますか？

phrases.japanese: かんそうきが、とちゅうでとまりました
phrases.notes: Situation: the dryer stopped mid-cycle. 乾燥機 (kansouki) = dryer. 途中 (tochuu) = halfway through.

responses.japanese: もういちどコインをいれると、つづきからまわります
responses.romaji: Mou ichido koin wo ireru to, tsuzuki kara mawarimasu
responses.english: If you insert another coin, it'll continue from where it stopped
responses.listen_for: つづき (続き, tsuzuki) = continuation. まわる (回る) = to run / spin.
responses.kanji: もう一度コインを入れると、続きから回ります

responses.japanese: ドアがしまっているか、かくにんしてください
responses.romaji: Doa ga shimatte iru ka, kakunin shite kudasai
responses.english: Please check that the door is closed
responses.listen_for: 閉まっている (shimatte iru) = is closed. Many dryers stop when the door is open.
responses.kanji: ドアが閉まっているか、確認してください

phrases.kanji: 乾燥機が、途中で止まりました

phrases.japanese: このおみせはなんねんつづいていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono omise wa nan nen tsuzuite imasu ka?
phrases.english: How many years has this shop been running?
phrases.notes: つづいています (続いています, tsuzuite imasu) = has continued/been running. A great conversation opener with any shopkeeper.

responses.japanese: そふのだいからさんだいめです
responses.romaji: Sofu no dai kara sandaime desu
responses.english: We're the third generation since my grandfather's time
responses.listen_for: だい (代, dai) = generation/era.
responses.kanji: 祖父の代から三代目です

responses.japanese: ことしでじゅうねんになります
responses.english: This year marks 10 years
responses.listen_for: ことし (今年, kotoshi) = this year.
responses.kanji: 今年で10年になります

phrases.kanji: このお店は何年続いていますか？

phrases.japanese: いつからこのしごとをしているのですか？
phrases.romaji: Itsu kara kono shigoto wo shite iru no desu ka?
phrases.english: Since when have you been doing this work?
phrases.notes: A slightly more personal version of sk-01, focused on the person rather than the shop itself.

responses.japanese: わかいころからずっとです
responses.english: Ever since I was young
responses.listen_for: わかいころ (若い頃, wakai koro) = younger days.
responses.kanji: 若い頃からずっとです

responses.japanese: べつのしごとをやめてからはじめました
responses.romaji: Betsu no shigoto wo yamete kara hajimemashita
responses.english: I started after quitting a different job
responses.listen_for: やめて (辞めて, yamete) = quitting.
responses.kanji: 別の仕事を辞めてから始めました

phrases.kanji: いつからこの仕事をしているのですか？

phrases.japanese: しょうばいはいかがですか？
phrases.notes: しょうばい (商売, shoubai) = business/trade — a warm, casual way to ask how things are going.

responses.japanese: おかげさまでじゅんちょうです
responses.english: Thankfully, it's going well
responses.listen_for: おかげさまで (おかげ様で, okagesama de) = thankfully/thanks to you.
responses.kanji: おかげさまで順調です

responses.japanese: さいきんはすこしきびしいですが、がんばっています
responses.romaji: Saikin wa sukoshi kibishii desu ga, ganbatte imasu
responses.english: It's been a bit tough lately, but we're doing our best
responses.listen_for: きびしい (厳しい, kibishii) = tough/harsh.
responses.kanji: 最近は少し厳しいですが、頑張っています

phrases.kanji: 商売はいかがですか？

phrases.japanese: がいこくじんのおきゃくさまはおおいですか？
phrases.romaji: Gaikokujin no okyakusama wa ooi desu ka?
phrases.english: Do you get a lot of foreign customers?
phrases.notes: おきゃくさま (お客様, okyakusama) = customer (polite). A natural question that often leads into a longer chat.

responses.japanese: はい、さいきんはとてもおおいです
responses.romaji: Hai, saikin wa totemo ooi desu
responses.english: Yes, there have been a lot recently
responses.listen_for: さいきん (最近, saikin) = recently.
responses.kanji: はい、最近はとても多いです

responses.japanese: かんこうきせつはとくにおおいですね
responses.romaji: Kankou kisetsu wa toku ni ooi desu ne
responses.english: Especially during tourist season there are many
responses.listen_for: かんこうきせつ (観光季節, kankou kisetsu) = tourist season.
responses.kanji: 観光季節は特に多いですね

phrases.kanji: 外国人のお客様は多いですか？

phrases.japanese: どちらのくにからのおきゃくさまがおおいですか？
phrases.romaji: Dochira no kuni kara no okyakusama ga ooi desu ka?
phrases.english: Which country do most of your customers come from?
phrases.notes: A natural follow-up to sk-04.

responses.japanese: アジアのかたがおおいですね
responses.romaji: Ajia no kata ga ooi desu ne
responses.english: There are a lot of people from Asia
responses.listen_for: かた (方, kata) = person (polite).
responses.kanji: アジアの方が多いですね

responses.japanese: さいきんはおうべいのかたもふえています
responses.romaji: Saikin wa oubei no kata mo fuete imasu
responses.english: Recently, people from Europe and America have increased too
responses.listen_for: おうべい (欧米, oubei) = Europe and America.
responses.kanji: 最近は欧米の方も増えています

phrases.kanji: どちらの国からのお客様が多いですか？

phrases.japanese: かぞくでけいえいしているのですか？
phrases.romaji: Kazoku de keiei shite iru no desu ka?
phrases.notes: けいえい (経営, keiei) = management/operation. Common for small restaurants and shops across Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、つまとふたりでやっています
responses.romaji: Hai, tsuma to futari de yatte imasu
responses.english: Yes, my wife and I run it together
responses.listen_for: つま (妻, tsuma) = wife.
responses.kanji: はい、妻と二人でやっています

responses.japanese: むすこがついでくれることになっています
responses.romaji: Musuko ga tsuide kureru koto ni natte imasu
responses.english: My son is going to take over
responses.listen_for: むすこ (息子, musuko) = son.
responses.kanji: 息子が継いでくれることになっています

phrases.kanji: 家族で経営しているのですか？

phrases.japanese: いちばんいそがしいじきはいつですか？
phrases.romaji: Ichiban isogashii jiki wa itsu desu ka?
phrases.notes: じき (時期, jiki) = period/season/time. Useful small talk with any shopkeeper about their yearly rhythm.

responses.japanese: おぼんとおしょうがつがいちばんいそがしいです
responses.romaji: Obon to oshougatsu ga ichiban isogashii desu
responses.english: Obon and New Year's are the busiest
responses.listen_for: おしょうがつ (お正月, oshougatsu) = New Year's holiday.
responses.kanji: お盆とお正月が一番忙しいです

responses.japanese: かんこうシーズンのはるとあきですね
responses.romaji: Kankou shiizun no haru to aki desu ne
responses.english: It's spring and autumn, the tourist season
responses.listen_for: かんこうシーズン (観光シーズン, kankou shiizun) = tourist season.
responses.kanji: 観光シーズンの春と秋ですね

phrases.kanji: 一番忙しい時期はいつですか？

phrases.japanese: どうしてこのしごとをはじめたのですか？
phrases.romaji: Doushite kono shigoto wo hajimeta no desu ka?
phrases.english: Why did you start this work?
phrases.notes: A deeper, more personal question — great once rapport is established.

responses.japanese: りょうりがだいすきだったからです
responses.romaji: Ryouri ga daisuki datta kara desu
responses.english: Because I loved cooking
responses.listen_for: だいすき (大好き, daisuki) = loved/really like.
responses.kanji: 料理が大好きだったからです

responses.japanese: おやのあとをつぐためです
responses.romaji: Oya no ato wo tsugu tame desu
responses.english: To carry on after my parents
responses.listen_for: おや (親, oya) = parent(s).
responses.kanji: 親の後を継ぐためです

phrases.kanji: どうしてこの仕事を始めたのですか？

phrases.japanese: このへんはむかしとくらべてかわりましたか？
phrases.romaji: Kono hen wa mukashi to kurabete kawarimashita ka?
phrases.english: Has this area changed compared to the old days?
phrases.notes: むかし (昔, mukashi) = the past/old days. A great way to hear local history from a longtime shop owner.

responses.japanese: はい、かんこうきゃくがすごくふえました
responses.english: Yes, the number of tourists has increased a lot
responses.listen_for: かんこうきゃく (観光客, kankoukyaku) = tourists.
responses.kanji: はい、観光客がすごく増えました

responses.japanese: むかしのほうがしずかでしたね
responses.romaji: Mukashi no hou ga shizuka deshita ne
responses.english: It used to be quieter back then
responses.listen_for: しずか (静か, shizuka) = quiet.
responses.kanji: 昔の方が静かでしたね

phrases.kanji: この辺は昔と比べて変わりましたか？

phrases.japanese: このしごとのすきなところはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono shigoto no suki na tokoro wa doko desu ka?
phrases.english: What do you like about this job?
phrases.notes: A warm question that often gets a genuinely thoughtful answer.

responses.japanese: おきゃくさまのえがおがみられることです
responses.romaji: Okyakusama no egao ga mirareru koto desu
responses.english: Being able to see customers' smiles
responses.listen_for: えがお (笑顔, egao) = smiling face.
responses.kanji: お客様の笑顔が見られることです

responses.japanese: いろいろなひとにであえることです
responses.romaji: Iroiro na hito ni deaeru koto desu
responses.english: Getting to meet all kinds of people
responses.listen_for: であえる (出会える, deaeru) = being able to meet.
responses.kanji: いろいろな人に出会えることです

phrases.kanji: この仕事の好きなところはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: なんじからなんじまでえいぎょうしていますか？
phrases.romaji: Nanji kara nanji made eigyou shite imasu ka?
phrases.notes: えいぎょう (営業, eigyou) = business operation — more natural phrasing than literally asking 'open/close' when chatting with an owner.

responses.japanese: あさじゅうじからよるはちじまでです
responses.romaji: Asa juuji kara yoru hachiji made desu
responses.english: From 10am to 8pm
responses.listen_for: あさ (朝, asa) = morning. よる (夜, yoru) = night.
responses.kanji: 朝10時から夜8時までです

responses.japanese: ていきゅうびはすいようびです
responses.english: Our regular closing day is Wednesday
responses.listen_for: ていきゅうび (定休日, teikyuubi) = regular closing day.
responses.kanji: 定休日は水曜日です

phrases.kanji: 何時から何時まで営業していますか？

phrases.japanese: またらいねんもきますね
phrases.notes: A warm way to close out a conversation with a shopkeeper you've connected with.

responses.japanese: ぜひまたきてくださいね、まっています
responses.romaji: Zehi mata kite kudasai ne, matte imasu
responses.english: Please do come again, I'll be waiting
responses.listen_for: ぜひ (zehi) = by all means/definitely.
responses.kanji: ぜひまた来てくださいね、待っています

responses.japanese: げんきでかえってくださいね
responses.english: Have a safe trip back home
responses.listen_for: げんきで (元気で, genki de) = safely/in good health.
responses.kanji: 元気で帰ってくださいね

phrases.kanji: また来年も来ますね

phrases.japanese: していせきをよやくしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to reserve a reserved seat
phrases.notes: していせき (指定席, shiteiseki) = reserved seat car. じゆうせき (自由席, jiyuuseki) = unreserved/first-come car — cheaper than the base fare.

responses.japanese: まどがわとつうろがわ、どちらがよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Madogawa to tsuurogawa, dochira ga yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Window or aisle, which would you prefer?
responses.listen_for: まどがわ (窓側, madogawa) = window side. つうろがわ (通路側, tsuurogawa) = aisle side.
responses.kanji: 窓側と通路側、どちらがよろしいですか？

responses.japanese: きんえんしゃとなります、よろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Kin'ensha to narimasu, yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: It will be a non-smoking car, is that okay?
responses.listen_for: きんえんしゃ (禁煙車, kin'ensha) = non-smoking car.
responses.kanji: 禁煙車となります、よろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 指定席を予約したいです

phrases.japanese: じゆうせきはなんごうしゃですか？
phrases.english: Which cars are the unreserved seating?
phrases.notes: ごうしゃ (号車, gousha) = train car number. On the Tokaido Shinkansen, cars 1–3 are typically jiyuuseki.

responses.japanese: いちごうしゃからさんごうしゃまでです
responses.english: Cars 1 through 3
responses.listen_for: ごうしゃ (号車, gousha) = car number.
responses.kanji: 1号車から3号車までです

responses.japanese: ホームのひょうじでごかくにんください
responses.romaji: Hoomu no hyouji de gokakunin kudasai
responses.english: Please check the platform signage
responses.listen_for: ひょうじ (表示, hyouji) = display/signage.
responses.kanji: ホームの表示でご確認ください

phrases.kanji: 自由席は何号車ですか？

phrases.japanese: グリーンしゃのきっぷはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Guriin-sha no kippu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a Green Car ticket available?
phrases.notes: グリーンしゃ (グリーン車, guriin-sha) = first-class-style Green Car, wider seats, extra fee.

responses.japanese: はい、ざんせきがございます
responses.english: Yes, there are seats remaining
responses.listen_for: ざんせき (残席, zanseki) = remaining seats.
responses.kanji: はい、残席がございます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、ほんじつはまんせきです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, honjitsu wa manseki desu
responses.english: Sorry, today it's fully booked
responses.listen_for: まんせき (満席, manseki) = fully booked/no seats.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、本日は満席です

phrases.kanji: グリーン車の切符はありますか？

phrases.japanese: おおきいにもつをよやくしたいです
phrases.romaji: Ookii nimotsu wo yoyaku shitai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to reserve a large-luggage space
phrases.notes: Since 2020, the Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu Shinkansen require a free advance reservation for any suitcase bigger than 160cm (total of 3 dimensions), or staff may charge a fee if you don't book one.

responses.japanese: サイズをはかってもよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Saizu wo hakatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: May I measure the size?
responses.listen_for: はかって (測って, hakatte) = measuring.
responses.kanji: サイズを測ってもよろしいですか？

responses.japanese: さいこうれつのせきをごようういたします
responses.romaji: Saikouretsu no seki wo goyoui itashimasu
responses.english: I'll prepare a seat in the back row
responses.listen_for: さいこうれつ (最後列, saikouretsu) = the very last row.
responses.kanji: 最後列の席をご用意いたします

phrases.kanji: 大きい荷物を予約したいです

phrases.japanese: えきべんはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Ekiben wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy an ekiben (station bento)?
phrases.notes: えきべん (駅弁, ekiben) = regional bento sold at stations, a Shinkansen travel tradition.

responses.japanese: かいさつのてまえにばいてんがあります
responses.romaji: Kaisatsu no temae ni baiten ga arimasu
responses.english: There's a stall before the ticket gate
responses.listen_for: かいさつ (改札, kaisatsu) = ticket gate.
responses.kanji: 改札の手前に売店があります

responses.japanese: しゃないはんばいでもかえます
responses.english: You can also buy from the in-car trolley service
responses.listen_for: しゃないはんばい (車内販売, shanai hanbai) = in-car cart sales.
responses.kanji: 車内販売でも買えます

phrases.kanji: 駅弁はどこで買えますか？

phrases.japanese: のりおくれました、どうすればいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Noriokuremashita, dou sureba ii desu ka?
phrases.english: I missed my train, what should I do?
phrases.notes: のりおくれる (乗り遅れる, noriokureru) = to miss a train/bus.

responses.japanese: じゆうせきなら、つぎのれっしゃにのれます
responses.romaji: Jiyuuseki nara, tsugi no ressha ni noremasu
responses.english: If it's unreserved seating, you can take the next train
responses.listen_for: つぎのれっしゃ (次の列車, tsugi no ressha) = the next train.
responses.kanji: 自由席なら、次の列車に乗れます

responses.japanese: みどりのまどぐちできっぷのへんこうができます
responses.romaji: Midori no madoguchi de kippu no henkou ga dekimasu
responses.english: You can change your ticket at the Green Window (ticket office)
responses.listen_for: みどりのまどぐち (みどりの窓口, midori no madoguchi) = JR ticket office.
responses.kanji: みどりの窓口で切符の変更ができます

phrases.kanji: 乗り遅れました、どうすればいいですか？

phrases.japanese: きっぷをへんこうしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to change my ticket
phrases.notes: へんこう (変更, henkou) = change/modify. Usually one free change is allowed before the original departure time.

responses.japanese: どのれっしゃにへんこうされますか？
responses.romaji: Dono ressha ni henkou saremasu ka?
responses.english: Which train would you like to change to?
responses.listen_for: へんこう (変更, henkou) = change.
responses.kanji: どの列車に変更されますか？

responses.japanese: じょうしゃけんはそのままつかえます
responses.english: The base fare ticket can be used as is
responses.listen_for: じょうしゃけん (乗車券, joushaken) = base fare ticket.
responses.kanji: 乗車券はそのまま使えます

phrases.kanji: 切符を変更したいです

phrases.japanese: このせきはしていせきですか？
