phrases.romaji: Kono seki wa shiteiseki desu ka?
phrases.notes: Useful when you find someone sitting in what you believe is your assigned seat, or vice versa — politely check before sitting.

responses.japanese: いいえ、じゆうせきしゃです
responses.english: No, this is an unreserved car
responses.listen_for: じゆうせきしゃ (自由席車, jiyuuseki-sha) = unreserved car.

responses.japanese: きっぷをかくにんさせてください
responses.english: Let me check your ticket
responses.listen_for: かくにん (確認, kakunin) = confirm/check.
responses.kanji: 切符を確認させてください

phrases.kanji: この席は指定席ですか？

phrases.japanese: しゃないでつうわしてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Shanai de tsuuwa shite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I make a phone call inside the train?
phrases.notes: Phone calls are considered bad etiquette in the main train cars in Japan — there's usually a デッキ (dekki, deck/vestibule area between cars) for calls.

responses.japanese: でっきでおねがいします
responses.english: Please use the deck/vestibule area
responses.listen_for: でっき (deck) = the space between train cars.

responses.japanese: マナーモードにごきょうりょくください
responses.english: Please cooperate by using silent mode
responses.listen_for: マナーモード (manaa moodo) = silent/manner mode.
responses.kanji: マナーモードにご協力ください

phrases.kanji: 車内で通話してもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: ざせきをたおしてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Zaseki wo taoshite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: Common courtesy is to glance back and say すみません (sumimasen) before reclining, especially if someone's eating or working.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞ
responses.english: Yes, go ahead
responses.listen_for: A simple green light.

responses.japanese: すこしだけでもだいじょうぶですか？
responses.romaji: Sukoshi dake demo daijoubu desu ka?
responses.english: Is it okay if it's just a little?
responses.listen_for: すこしだけ (少しだけ, sukoshi dake) = just a little.

phrases.kanji: 座席を倒してもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: たいふうでれっしゃはとまっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Taifuu de ressha wa tomatte imasu ka?
phrases.english: Are trains stopped because of the typhoon?
phrases.notes: たいふう (台風, taifuu) = typhoon. Common in late summer/early autumn — always check train status apps too.

responses.japanese: はい、げんざいうんてんをみあわせています
responses.romaji: Hai, genzai unten wo miawasete imasu
responses.english: Yes, service is currently suspended
responses.listen_for: みあわせています (見合わせています, miawasete imasu) = currently suspended.
responses.kanji: はい、現在運転を見合わせています

responses.japanese: すこしおくれていますが、うんこうしています
responses.romaji: Sukoshi okurete imasu ga, unkou shite imasu
responses.english: It's running a bit late, but operating
responses.listen_for: うんこう (運行, unkou) = in operation.
responses.kanji: 少し遅れていますが、運行しています

phrases.kanji: 台風で列車は止まっていますか？

phrases.japanese: じしんがありました
phrases.notes: じしん (地震, jishin) = earthquake. A phrase to state the situation calmly to those around you.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですか？けがはありませんか？
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu ka? Kega wa arimasen ka?
responses.english: Are you okay? Any injuries?
responses.listen_for: けが (怪我, kega) = injury.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫ですか？怪我はありませんか？

responses.japanese: つくえのしたにかくれてください
responses.romaji: Tsukue no shita ni kakurete kudasai
responses.english: Please take cover under a desk/table
responses.listen_for: かくれて (隠れて, kakurete) = take cover/hide.
responses.kanji: 机の下に隠れてください

phrases.kanji: 地震がありました

phrases.japanese: いまそとにでてもあんぜんですか？
phrases.romaji: Ima soto ni dete mo anzen desu ka?
phrases.english: Is it safe to go outside right now?
phrases.notes: あんぜん (安全, anzen) = safe. A key question during or after a natural event.

responses.japanese: まだきけんですので、なかでおまちください
responses.romaji: Mada kiken desu node, naka de omachi kudasai
responses.english: It's still dangerous, so please wait inside
responses.listen_for: きけん (危険, kiken) = dangerous.
responses.kanji: まだ危険ですので、中でお待ちください

responses.japanese: はい、もうあんぜんです
responses.english: Yes, it's already safe now
responses.listen_for: あんぜん (安全, anzen) = safe.
responses.kanji: はい、もう安全です

phrases.kanji: 今外に出ても安全ですか？

phrases.japanese: ひなんばしょはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Hinan basho wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: ひなんばしょ (避難場所, hinan basho) = designated evacuation site, usually a school or public hall — look for blue/green signage.

responses.japanese: ちかくのしょうがっこうがひなんじょです
responses.romaji: Chikaku no shougakkou ga hinanjo desu
responses.english: The nearby elementary school is the evacuation shelter
responses.listen_for: ひなんじょ (避難所, hinanjo) = evacuation shelter.
responses.kanji: 近くの小学校が避難所です

responses.japanese: ひなんけいろにしたがってすすんでください
responses.romaji: Hinan keiro ni shitagatte susunde kudasai
responses.english: Please proceed following the evacuation route
responses.listen_for: ひなんけいろ (避難経路, hinan keiro) = evacuation route.
responses.kanji: 避難経路に従って進んでください

phrases.kanji: 避難場所はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: きょうのてんきはどうですか？
phrases.romaji: Kyou no tenki wa dou desu ka?
phrases.notes: A simple everyday check-in question, useful before heading out or when making small talk.

responses.japanese: きょうはいちにちあめのよほうです
responses.romaji: Kyou wa ichinichi ame no yohou desu
responses.english: The forecast is rain all day today
responses.listen_for: よほう (予報, yohou) = forecast.
responses.kanji: 今日は一日雨の予報です

responses.japanese: ごごからはれるそうです
responses.english: I heard it'll clear up from the afternoon
responses.listen_for: はれる (晴れる, hareru) = to clear up/become sunny.
responses.kanji: 午後から晴れるそうです

phrases.kanji: 今日の天気はどうですか？

phrases.japanese: これはめずらしいてんきですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa mezurashii tenki desu ka?
phrases.notes: めずらしい (珍しい, mezurashii) = unusual/rare. Great for small talk with locals about whether current conditions are normal.

responses.japanese: はい、このじきにしてはめずらしいです
responses.romaji: Hai, kono jiki ni shite wa mezurashii desu
responses.english: Yes, it's unusual for this time of year
responses.listen_for: じき (時期, jiki) = time/season.
responses.kanji: はい、この時期にしては珍しいです

responses.japanese: いえ、まいとしこうなんですよ
responses.romaji: Ie, maitoshi kou nan desu yo
responses.english: No, it's like this every year
responses.listen_for: まいとし (毎年, maitoshi) = every year.

phrases.kanji: これは珍しい天気ですか？

phrases.japanese: けいほうがでています
phrases.notes: けいほう (警報, keihou) = warning (stronger than 注意報/chuuihou, advisory). Pay attention to J-Alert phone notifications.

responses.japanese: どのしゅるいのけいほうですか？
responses.romaji: Dono shurui no keihou desu ka?
responses.english: What kind of warning is it?
responses.listen_for: しゅるい (種類, shurui) = kind/type.
responses.kanji: どの種類の警報ですか？

responses.japanese: おおあめけいほうがでています
responses.english: A heavy rain warning has been issued
responses.listen_for: おおあめ (大雨, ooame) = heavy rain.
responses.kanji: 大雨警報が出ています

phrases.kanji: 警報が出ています

phrases.japanese: ひなんかんこくがでましたか？
phrases.english: Has an evacuation advisory been issued?
phrases.notes: ひなんかんこく (避難勧告, hinan kankoku) = evacuation advisory, one level below the stronger 避難指示 (hinan shiji) / evacuation order.

responses.japanese: はい、このちいきにでています
responses.romaji: Hai, kono chiiki ni dete imasu
responses.english: Yes, it's been issued for this area
responses.listen_for: ちいき (地域, chiiki) = area/region.
responses.kanji: はい、この地域に出ています

responses.japanese: いいえ、まだでていません
responses.english: No, not yet
responses.listen_for: まだ (mada) = not yet.

phrases.kanji: 避難勧告が出ましたか？

phrases.japanese: スマホにきんきゅうじしんそくほうがきました
phrases.romaji: Sumaho ni kinkyuu jishin sokuhou ga kimashita
phrases.english: I got an emergency earthquake alert on my phone
phrases.notes: きんきゅうじしんそくほう (緊急地震速報, kinkyuu jishin sokuhou) = the J-Alert early earthquake warning that buzzes loudly on Japanese phones seconds before shaking.

responses.japanese: すぐにあたまをまもってください
responses.romaji: Sugu ni atama wo mamotte kudasai
responses.english: Please protect your head right away
responses.listen_for: まもって (守って, mamotte) = protect.
responses.kanji: すぐに頭を守ってください

responses.japanese: ゆれがくるまえにかぐからはなれてください
responses.romaji: Yure ga kuru mae ni kagu kara hanarete kudasai
responses.english: Please move away from furniture before the shaking arrives
responses.listen_for: ゆれ (揺れ, yure) = shaking/tremor.
responses.kanji: 揺れが来る前に家具から離れてください

phrases.kanji: スマホに緊急地震速報が来ました

phrases.japanese: たいふうはいつすぎますか？
phrases.notes: すぎる (過ぎる, sugiru) = to pass. Good conversational follow-up after a typhoon warning.

responses.japanese: よるにはすぎるよほうです
responses.romaji: Yoru ni wa sugiru yohou desu
responses.english: The forecast says it'll pass by tonight
responses.listen_for: よる (夜, yoru) = night.
responses.kanji: 夜には過ぎる予報です

responses.japanese: あしたのあさまでつづくそうです
responses.romaji: Ashita no asa made tsuzuku sou desu
responses.english: I heard it'll continue until tomorrow morning
responses.listen_for: つづく (続く, tsuzuku) = to continue.
responses.kanji: 明日の朝まで続くそうです

phrases.kanji: 台風はいつ過ぎますか？

phrases.japanese: すみません、うるさいです
phrases.notes: うるさい (urusai) = noisy. Say it politely; staff usually respond quickly.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、すぐにたしかめます
responses.english: I'm sorry, I'll check right away
responses.listen_for: 確かめる (tashikameru) = to check.

responses.japanese: おとをちいさくするようにつたえます
responses.romaji: Oto wo chiisaku suru you ni tsutaemasu
responses.english: I'll tell them to keep it quieter
responses.listen_for: 伝える (tsutaeru) = to pass on.

phrases.japanese: エアコンがききません
phrases.notes: エアコン (eakon) = air conditioner. 効く (kiku) = to work / take effect.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、すぐにみにいきます
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, sugu ni mi ni ikimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, I'll go take a look right away
responses.listen_for: 見に行く (miniiku) = go to see.

responses.japanese: ほかのへやにかえられますか？
responses.romaji: Hoka no heya ni kaeraremasu ka?
responses.english: Could we switch to another room?
responses.listen_for: 変える (kaeru) = to change.

phrases.japanese: さむいです、どうにかできますか？
phrases.romaji: Samui desu, dou ni ka dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: It's too cold, can you do something?
phrases.notes: 寒い (samui) = cold. どうにかできますか = can you do something about it?

responses.japanese: はい、おんどをあげます
responses.english: Yes, I'll raise the temperature
responses.listen_for: 温度 (ondo) = temperature. 上げる (ageru) = to raise.

responses.japanese: ブランケットをおもちします
responses.english: I'll bring a blanket
responses.listen_for: ブランケット (blanket).

phrases.japanese: このりょうりがつめたいです
phrases.notes: 冷たい (tsumetai) = cold. 温かい (atatakai) = warm.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、あたためなおします
responses.english: I'm sorry, I'll reheat it
responses.listen_for: 温め直す (atatamenaosu) = reheat.

responses.japanese: すぐにおもちします
responses.english: I'll bring a new one right away
responses.listen_for: お持ち (omochi) = bring (polite).

phrases.japanese: りょうきんがまちがっているとおもいます
phrases.romaji: Ryoukin ga machigatte iru to omoimasu
phrases.english: I think the charge is wrong
phrases.notes: 料金 (ryoukin) = charge. 間違っている (machigatte iru) = is wrong.

responses.japanese: はい、もういちどかくにんいたします
responses.english: Yes, I'll check again
responses.listen_for: 確認 (kakunin) = check.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、すぐにしゅうせいします
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, sugu ni shuusei shimasu
responses.english: I'm sorry, I'll correct it right away
responses.listen_for: 修正 (shuusei) = correction.

phrases.japanese: かえしたいのですが、できますか？
phrases.romaji: Kaeshitai no desu ga, dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: I'd like to return this. Is that possible?
phrases.notes: 返品 (henpin) = return of goods. 〜のですが = a polite lead-in before a request.

responses.japanese: レシートはおもちですか？
responses.english: Do you have the receipt?
responses.listen_for: お持ち = have (polite).

responses.japanese: なにか、もんだいがありましたか？
responses.english: Was there a problem?
responses.listen_for: 問題 (mondai) = problem.

phrases.japanese: かねをかえしてもらえますか？
phrases.notes: 返金 (henkin) = refund. Refund rules differ by shop, so ask first.

responses.japanese: はい、おかえしできます
responses.english: Yes, we can refund it
responses.listen_for: お返し (okaeshi) = return / refund (polite).

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、かえせないきまりです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, kaesenai kimari desu
responses.english: I'm sorry, but it's our policy not to refund
responses.listen_for: 決まり (kimari) = rule / policy.

phrases.japanese: マネージャーをよんでください
phrases.notes: マネージャー (manager). 店長 (tenchou) = store manager. Stay calm; this is a normal request.

responses.japanese: すぐにおよびします
responses.english: I'll call them right away
responses.listen_for: お呼び (oyobi) = call (polite).

responses.japanese: てんちょうをよびますので、おまちください
responses.romaji: Tenchou wo yobimasu node, omachi kudasai
responses.english: I'll call the store manager, so please wait
responses.listen_for: 店長 (tenchou) = store manager.

phrases.japanese: れつをまちがえました、すみません
phrases.english: I got in the wrong line, sorry
phrases.notes: まちがえました (間違えました, machigaemashita) = made a mistake. れつ (列, retsu) = line/queue.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶですよ、あちらにならんでください
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu yo, achira ni narande kudasai
responses.english: No problem, please line up over there
responses.listen_for: ならんで (並んで, narande) = line up.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫ですよ、あちらに並んでください

responses.japanese: きにしないでください
responses.english: Please don't worry about it
responses.listen_for: きにしない (気にしない, ki ni shinai) = not worry/mind.

phrases.kanji: 列を間違えました、すみません

phrases.japanese: しらずにしつれいなことをしてしまいました
phrases.romaji: Shirazu ni shitsurei na koto wo shite shimaimashita
phrases.notes: しつれい (失礼, shitsurei) = rude/impolite. A sincere way to acknowledge a cultural misstep after the fact.

responses.japanese: きにしないでください、しらなくてとうぜんです
responses.romaji: Ki ni shinaide kudasai, shiranakute touzen desu
responses.english: Please don't worry, it's natural not to know
responses.listen_for: とうぜん (当然, touzen) = natural/to be expected.
responses.kanji: 気にしないでください、知らなくて当然です

responses.japanese: つぎからきをつければだいじょうぶですよ
responses.romaji: Tsugi kara ki wo tsukereba daijoubu desu yo
responses.english: As long as you're careful next time, it's fine
responses.listen_for: きをつける (気をつける, ki wo tsukeru) = be careful.
responses.kanji: 次から気をつければ大丈夫ですよ

phrases.kanji: 知らずに失礼なことをしてしまいました

phrases.japanese: わるぎはなかったんです
phrases.notes: わるぎ (悪気, warugi) = ill intent/malice. Useful to clarify a misunderstanding wasn't intentional.

responses.japanese: わかっていますよ、だいじょうぶです
responses.english: I understand, it's okay
responses.listen_for: わかっています (分かっています, wakatte imasu) = understood.
responses.kanji: 分かっていますよ、大丈夫です

responses.japanese: きにしていませんので、ごあんしんください
responses.romaji: Ki ni shite imasen node, goanshin kudasai
responses.english: I'm not bothered by it, please don't worry
responses.listen_for: ごあんしん (ご安心, goanshin) = rest assured.
responses.kanji: 気にしていませんので、ご安心ください

phrases.kanji: 悪気はなかったんです

phrases.japanese: ごめいわくをおかけしてもうしわけありません
phrases.romaji: Gomeiwaku wo okake shite moushiwake arimasen
phrases.english: I'm sorry for causing you trouble
phrases.notes: ごめいわく (ご迷惑, gomeiwaku) = trouble/inconvenience — a much deeper, more formal apology than すみません, used after a real inconvenience was caused.

responses.japanese: いえいえ、きにしないでください
responses.english: No no, please don't worry about it
responses.listen_for: いえいえ (ieie) = not at all.

responses.japanese: だれにでもあることです
responses.romaji: Dare ni demo aru koto desu
responses.english: It can happen to anyone
responses.listen_for: だれにでも (誰にでも, dare ni demo) = to anyone.
responses.kanji: 誰にでもあることです

phrases.kanji: ご迷惑をおかけして申し訳ありません

phrases.japanese: どうすればよかったですか？
phrases.english: What should I have done instead?
phrases.notes: A humble, learning-focused question that shows genuine effort to understand local customs.

responses.japanese: つぎはこうすればだいじょうぶですよ
responses.romaji: Tsugi wa kou sureba daijoubu desu yo
responses.english: Next time, if you do it this way, it'll be fine
responses.listen_for: つぎは (次は, tsugi wa) = next time.
responses.kanji: 次はこうすれば大丈夫ですよ

responses.japanese: とくにきをつけることはありませんよ
responses.romaji: Toku ni ki wo tsukeru koto wa arimasen yo
responses.english: There's nothing in particular you need to worry about
responses.listen_for: とくに (特に, toku ni) = particularly/especially.
responses.kanji: 特に気をつけることはありませんよ

phrases.kanji: どうすれば良かったですか？

phrases.japanese: にほんのマナーがまだよくわかりません
phrases.romaji: Nihon no manaa ga mada yoku wakarimasen
phrases.english: I still don't understand Japanese manners very well
phrases.notes: マナー (manaa) = manners/etiquette. An honest, disarming admission that often prompts kind explanations.

responses.japanese: すこしずつおぼえていけばだいじょうぶですよ
responses.romaji: Sukoshi zutsu oboete ikeba daijoubu desu yo
responses.english: It's fine as long as you learn little by little
responses.listen_for: すこしずつ (少しずつ, sukoshi zutsu) = little by little.
responses.kanji: 少しずつ覚えていけば大丈夫ですよ

responses.japanese: わからないことはきいてくださいね
responses.romaji: Wakaranai koto wa kiite kudasai ne
responses.english: Please ask if there's anything you don't understand
responses.listen_for: きいて (聞いて, kiite) = ask.

phrases.kanji: 日本のマナーがまだよく分かりません

phrases.japanese: きがつかずにすみませんでした
phrases.romaji: Ki ga tsukazu ni sumimasen deshita
phrases.notes: きがつく (気が付く, ki ga tsuku) = to notice. Useful when you accidentally bumped into someone, blocked a path, etc.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶです、おきになさらないでください
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu, oki ni nasaranaide kudasai
responses.english: It's fine, please don't worry about it
responses.listen_for: おきになさらないで (お気になさらないで, oki ni nasaranaide) = please don't let it bother you.
responses.kanji: 大丈夫です、お気になさらないでください

phrases.kanji: 気が付かずにすみませんでした

phrases.japanese: ごかいさせてしまったかもしれません
phrases.english: I may have caused a misunderstanding
phrases.notes: ごかい (誤解, gokai) = misunderstanding. Useful to proactively clear the air during a conversation.

responses.japanese: そうだったんですね、わかりました
responses.english: I see, that explains it, understood
responses.listen_for: わかりました (分かりました, wakarimashita) = understood.
responses.kanji: そうだったんですね、分かりました

responses.japanese: きちんとせつめいしてくれてありがとうございます
responses.romaji: Kichinto setsumei shite kurete arigatou gozaimasu
responses.english: Thank you for explaining it clearly
responses.listen_for: せつめい (説明, setsumei) = explanation.
responses.kanji: きちんと説明してくれてありがとうございます

phrases.kanji: 誤解させてしまったかもしれません

phrases.japanese: もうしませんので、ゆるしてください
phrases.english: I won't do it again, please forgive me
phrases.notes: ゆるす (許す, yurusu) = to forgive. A stronger, more contrite apology for a bigger misstep.

responses.japanese: だいじょうぶです、きにしないでください
responses.romaji: Daijoubu desu, ki ni shinaide kudasai
responses.english: It's okay, please don't worry about it
responses.listen_for: A reassuring, standard response.

responses.japanese: そんなにあやまらなくてもだいじょうぶですよ
responses.romaji: Sonna ni ayamaranakute mo daijoubu desu yo
responses.english: You don't need to apologize that much
responses.listen_for: あやまる (謝る, ayamaru) = to apologize.
responses.kanji: そんなに謝らなくても大丈夫ですよ

phrases.kanji: もうしませんので、許してください

phrases.japanese: いいわけではないのですが
phrases.romaji: Iiwake dewa nai no desu ga
phrases.english: This isn't meant as an excuse, but...
phrases.notes: いいわけ (言い訳, iiwake) = excuse. A softening phrase before explaining the context behind a mistake, without sounding defensive.

responses.japanese: じじょうはわかりました
responses.english: I understand the circumstances
responses.listen_for: じじょう (事情, jijou) = circumstances.
responses.kanji: 事情は分かりました

responses.japanese: せつめいしてくれてたすかります
responses.english: It helps that you explained
responses.listen_for: たすかります (助かります, tasukarimasu) = that helps/is a relief.

phrases.kanji: 言い訳ではないのですが

phrases.japanese: しゃしんをとってもらえますか？
phrases.english: Could you take a photo for me?
phrases.notes: Hand over your phone or camera after asking.

responses.japanese: はい、いいですよ！はい、チーズ！
responses.romaji: Hai, ii desu yo! Hai, chiizu!
responses.english: Yes, sure! Say cheese!
responses.listen_for: チーズ (chiizu) = cheese! Smile for the shutter.

phrases.kanji: 写真を撮ってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ここでしゃしんをとってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Koko de shashin wo totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I take a photo here?
phrases.notes: Crucial at temples, shrines, or private collections.

responses.japanese: すみません、さつえいきんしです
responses.english: Sorry, photography is prohibited
responses.listen_for: さつえいきんし (撮影禁止, satsuei kinshi) = no photography allowed.
responses.kanji: すみません、撮影禁止です

phrases.kanji: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: おまいりのしかたをおしえてもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Omairi no shikata wo oshiete moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Could you teach me how to pray properly?
phrases.notes: おまいり (お参り, omairi) = shrine/temple visit and worship. Standard shrine method: にれい、にはく、いちれい (二礼二拍手一礼, nirei nihakushu ichirei) = two bows, two claps, one bow.

responses.japanese: にかいおじぎして、にかいてをたたきます
responses.romaji: Nikai ojigi shite, nikai te wo tatakimasu
responses.english: Bow twice, then clap your hands twice
responses.listen_for: おじぎ (お辞儀, ojigi) = bow.
responses.kanji: 二回お辞儀して、二回手を叩きます

responses.japanese: さいごにもういちどおじぎをします
responses.romaji: Saigo ni mou ichido ojigi wo shimasu
responses.english: Finally, bow once more
responses.listen_for: さいごに (最後に, saigo ni) = finally/lastly.
responses.kanji: 最後にもう一度お辞儀をします

phrases.kanji: お参りの仕方を教えてもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: とりいをくぐるときのマナーはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Torii wo kuguru toki no manaa wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there etiquette for passing through the torii gate?
phrases.notes: とりい (鳥居, torii) = shrine gate marking sacred ground. まんなか (真ん中, mannaka) / the center of the path is considered the kami's path — walk to the side.

responses.japanese: さんどうのまんなかはあるかないでください
responses.romaji: Sandou no mannaka wa arukanaide kudasai
responses.english: Please don't walk in the middle of the approach path
responses.listen_for: さんどう (参道, sandou) = shrine approach path.
responses.kanji: 参道の真ん中は歩かないでください

responses.japanese: くぐるまえにかるくおじぎをします
responses.romaji: Kuguru mae ni karuku ojigi wo shimasu
responses.english: Give a light bow before passing through
responses.listen_for: かるく (軽く, karuku) = lightly.
responses.kanji: くぐる前に軽くお辞儀をします

phrases.kanji: 鳥居をくぐる時のマナーはありますか？

phrases.japanese: ちょうずのつかいかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Chouzu no tsukaikata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please teach me how to use the purification fountain
phrases.notes: ちょうず (手水, chouzu) = the water basin for ritual hand/mouth purification before approaching the main shrine.

responses.japanese: みぎてでひしゃくをもち、ひだりてをきよめます
responses.romaji: Migite de hishaku wo mochi, hidarite wo kiyomemasu
responses.english: Hold the ladle with your right hand and purify your left hand
responses.listen_for: ひしゃく (柄杓, hishaku) = ladle.
responses.kanji: 右手で柄杓を持ち、左手を清めます

responses.japanese: さいごにひしゃくのえをたてにながします
responses.romaji: Saigo ni hishaku no e wo tate ni nagashimasu
responses.english: Finally, rinse the ladle's handle by tilting it upright
responses.listen_for: たてに (縦に, tate ni) = vertically/upright.
responses.kanji: 最後に柄杓の柄を縦に流します

phrases.kanji: 手水の使い方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: おみくじをひきたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to draw an omikuji fortune
phrases.notes: おみくじ (omikuji) = paper fortune slips, ranked from だいきち (大吉, great blessing) to だいきょう (大凶, great curse).

responses.japanese: こちらのはこからひいてください
responses.romaji: Kochira no hako kara hiite kudasai
responses.english: Please draw from this box
responses.listen_for: はこ (箱, hako) = box.
responses.kanji: こちらの箱から引いてください

responses.japanese: わるいけっかはむすんでかえるといいですよ
responses.romaji: Warui kekka wa musunde kaeru to ii desu yo
responses.english: If it's a bad result, it's good to tie it up before leaving
responses.listen_for: むすんで (結んで, musunde) = tying.
responses.kanji: 悪い結果は結んで帰るといいですよ

phrases.kanji: おみくじを引きたいです

phrases.japanese: このおまもりはなにのためですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono omamori wa nani no tame desu ka?
phrases.notes: おまもり (お守り, omamori) = protective amulet, often sold for specific purposes like こうつうあんぜん (交通安全, traffic safety) or えんむすび (縁結び, good relationships).

responses.japanese: こうつうあんぜんのおまもりです
responses.english: It's a traffic-safety charm
responses.listen_for: こうつうあんぜん (交通安全, koutsuu anzen) = traffic safety.
responses.kanji: 交通安全のお守りです

responses.japanese: えんむすびのごりやくがあります
responses.english: It brings the blessing of good relationships
responses.listen_for: ごりやく (ご利益, goriyaku) = divine blessing/benefit.
responses.kanji: 縁結びのご利益があります

phrases.kanji: このお守りは何のためですか？

phrases.japanese: このじんじゃはいつごろたてられたのですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono jinja wa itsu goro tateraretano desu ka?
phrases.english: About when was this shrine built?
phrases.notes: じんじゃ (神社, jinja) = Shinto shrine. Great question to ask a priest, shop attendant, or tour guide.

responses.japanese: えどじだいにたてられました
responses.english: It was built during the Edo period
responses.listen_for: えどじだい (江戸時代, Edo jidai) = the Edo period.
responses.kanji: 江戸時代に建てられました

responses.japanese: せんねんいじょうのれきしがあります
responses.romaji: Sennen ijou no rekishi ga arimasu
responses.english: It has over a thousand years of history
responses.listen_for: れきし (歴史, rekishi) = history.
responses.kanji: 千年以上の歴史があります

phrases.kanji: この神社はいつ頃建てられたのですか？

phrases.japanese: しゃしんをとってもだいじょうぶなばしょはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Shashin wo totte mo daijoubu na basho wa doko desu ka?
phrases.english: Where is it okay to take photos?
phrases.notes: Some inner sanctuaries (ほんでん, 本殿, honden) prohibit photography — always check signage.

responses.japanese: けいだいはほとんどさつえいかのうです
responses.romaji: Keidai wa hotondo satsuei kanou desu
responses.english: Most of the grounds allow photography
responses.listen_for: けいだい (境内, keidai) = shrine/temple grounds.
responses.kanji: 境内はほとんど撮影可能です

responses.japanese: ほんでんのなかはさつえいきんしです
responses.romaji: Honden no naka wa satsuei kinshi desu
responses.english: Photography is prohibited inside the main hall
responses.listen_for: ほんでん (本殿, honden) = main shrine hall.
responses.kanji: 本殿の中は撮影禁止です

phrases.kanji: 写真を撮っても大丈夫な場所はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: えまはどこにかけますか？
phrases.romaji: Ema wa doko ni kakemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where do I hang the ema wooden wish plaque?
phrases.notes: えま (絵馬, ema) = small wooden plaque for writing wishes/prayers, hung on a dedicated rack.

responses.japanese: あちらのえまかけにかけてください
responses.romaji: Achira no ema-kake ni kakete kudasai
responses.english: Please hang it on the ema rack over there
responses.listen_for: えまかけ (絵馬掛け, ema-kake) = ema hanging rack.
responses.kanji: あちらの絵馬掛けに掛けてください

responses.japanese: ねがいごとをかいてからかけてくださいね
responses.romaji: Negaigoto wo kaite kara kakete kudasai ne
responses.english: Please write your wish before hanging it
responses.listen_for: ねがいごと (願い事, negaigoto) = wish.
responses.kanji: 願い事を書いてから掛けてくださいね

phrases.kanji: 絵馬はどこに掛けますか？

phrases.japanese: おさいせんはいくらがいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Osaisen wa ikura ga ii desu ka?
phrases.english: How much is good for the offering?
phrases.notes: おさいせん (お賽銭, osaisen) = monetary offering tossed into the box before praying. ごえん (五円, goen) / 5-yen coin is a popular choice since it's a pun on ごえん (ご縁, goen) = good connection/fate.

responses.japanese: ごえんだまがえんぎがいいとされています
responses.romaji: Goen-dama ga engi ga ii to sarete imasu
responses.english: A 5-yen coin is considered good luck
responses.listen_for: えんぎ (縁起, engi) = luck/omen.
responses.kanji: 五円玉が縁起が良いとされています

responses.japanese: きんがくはじゆうですよ
responses.english: The amount is entirely up to you
responses.listen_for: きんがく (金額, kingaku) = amount of money.

phrases.kanji: お賽銭はいくらがいいですか？

phrases.japanese: おぼうさんにおはなしをうかがってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Obousan ni ohanashi wo ukagatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I ask the priest/monk some questions?
phrases.notes: おぼうさん (お坊さん, obousan) = Buddhist monk at a temple. For a Shinto shrine priest, use かんぬしさん (神主さん, kannushi-san) instead.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞおきかせください
responses.english: Yes, please go ahead and ask
responses.listen_for: おきかせください (お聞かせください, okikase kudasai) = please tell/ask me.
responses.kanji: はい、どうぞお聞かせください

responses.japanese: いまはごきとうちゅうですので、しょうしょうおまちください
responses.romaji: Ima wa gokitou-chuu desu node, shoushou omachi kudasai
responses.english: We're in the middle of a prayer ritual right now, please wait a moment
responses.listen_for: ごきとう (ご祈祷, gokitou) = prayer ritual.
responses.kanji: 今はご祈祷中ですので、少々お待ちください

phrases.kanji: お坊さんにお話を伺ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: このじはんきはなにがかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono jihanki wa nani ga kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: What can I buy from this vending machine?
phrases.notes: じはんき (自販機, jihanki) = vending machine. Japan has some of the most varied vending machines in the world — drinks, snacks, even hot food.

responses.japanese: あたたかいのみものとつめたいのみものがあります
responses.romaji: Atatakai nomimono to tsumetai nomimono ga arimasu
responses.english: There are hot drinks and cold drinks
responses.listen_for: あたたかい (温かい, atatakai) = warm/hot. つめたい (冷たい, tsumetai) = cold.
responses.kanji: 温かい飲み物と冷たい飲み物があります

responses.japanese: これはおかしのじはんきです
responses.romaji: Kore wa okashi no jihanki desu
responses.english: This is a snack vending machine
responses.listen_for: おかし (お菓子, okashi) = snacks/sweets.
responses.kanji: これはお菓子の自販機です

phrases.kanji: この自販機は何が買えますか？

phrases.japanese: あかいひょうじはなにをあらわしていますか？
phrases.romaji: Akai hyouji wa nani wo arawashite imasu ka?
phrases.english: What does the red label mean?
phrases.notes: On Japanese drink machines, あか (赤, aka) / red usually marks あたたかい (温かい, atatakai) / hot drinks, and あお (青, ao) / blue marks つめたい (冷たい, tsumetai) / cold ones.

responses.japanese: あかはあたたかいのみものです
responses.english: Red is for hot drinks
responses.listen_for: あか (赤, aka) = red.
responses.kanji: 赤は温かい飲み物です

responses.japanese: あおはつめたいのみものです
responses.english: Blue is for cold drinks
responses.listen_for: あお (青, ao) = blue.
responses.kanji: 青は冷たい飲み物です

phrases.kanji: 赤い表示は何を表していますか？

phrases.japanese: このボタンはうりきれです
phrases.notes: うりきれ (売り切れ, urikire) = sold out, shown by a lit-up label over the item.

responses.japanese: べつのものをえらんでください
responses.romaji: Betsu no mono wo erande kudasai
responses.english: Please choose something else
responses.listen_for: べつの (別の, betsu no) = a different.
responses.kanji: 別のものを選んでください

responses.japanese: となりのじはんきをためしてみてください
responses.romaji: Tonari no jihanki wo tameshite mite kudasai
responses.english: Please try the vending machine next to it
responses.listen_for: となり (隣, tonari) = next to/neighboring.
responses.kanji: 隣の自販機を試してみてください

phrases.kanji: このボタンは売り切れです

phrases.japanese: おつりがでてきません
phrases.notes: おつり (お釣り, otsuri) = change. Look for a へんきゃくボタン (返却ボタン, henkyaku botan) / return button if the machine seems stuck.

responses.japanese: へんきゃくボタンをおしてみてください
responses.romaji: Henkyaku botan wo oshite mite kudasai
responses.english: Please try pressing the return button
responses.listen_for: へんきゃく (返却, henkyaku) = return.
responses.kanji: 返却ボタンを押してみてください

responses.japanese: きんがくをかくにんしてもういちどいれてください
responses.romaji: Kingaku wo kakunin shite mou ichido irete kudasai
responses.english: Please check the amount and insert it again
responses.listen_for: きんがく (金額, kingaku) = amount of money.
responses.kanji: 金額を確認してもう一度入れてください

phrases.kanji: お釣りが出てきません

phrases.japanese: このじはんきはICカードがつかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono jihanki wa IC kaado ga tsukaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I use an IC card at this vending machine?
phrases.notes: Most newer jihanki accept Suica/Pasmo-type IC cards — look for the IC card logo on the machine.

responses.japanese: はい、タッチするだけでかえます
responses.romaji: Hai, tacchi suru dake de kaemasu
responses.english: Yes, you can buy just by tapping
responses.listen_for: タッチする (tacchi suru) = to tap/touch.
responses.kanji: はい、タッチするだけで買えます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、げんきんのみです
responses.english: I'm sorry, cash only
responses.listen_for: げんきんのみ (現金のみ, genkin nomi) = cash only.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、現金のみです

phrases.kanji: この自販機はICカードが使えますか？

phrases.japanese: めずらしいじはんきをみつけました
phrases.english: I found an unusual vending machine
phrases.notes: A fun conversation starter — Japan is famous for oddball vending machines selling everything from bananas to umbrellas.

responses.japanese: なにをうっているじはんきですか？
responses.romaji: Nani wo utte iru jihanki desu ka?
responses.english: What does the vending machine sell?
responses.listen_for: うっている (売っている, utte iru) = selling.
responses.kanji: 何を売っている自販機ですか？

responses.japanese: しゃしんをとっておくといいですよ
responses.romaji: Shashin wo totte oku to ii desu yo
responses.english: It's good to take a photo of it
responses.listen_for: とっておく (撮っておく, totte oku) = take a photo for later.
responses.kanji: 写真を撮っておくといいですよ

phrases.kanji: 珍しい自販機を見つけました

phrases.japanese: じはんきのよこにごみばこはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Jihanki no yoko ni gomibako wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a trash bin next to the vending machine?
phrases.notes: Drink vending machines usually have a dedicated recycling bin for empty bottles and cans right beside them.

responses.japanese: はい、ペットボトルようのごみばこがあります
responses.romaji: Hai, pettobotoru you no gomibako ga arimasu
responses.english: Yes, there's a bin for plastic bottles
responses.listen_for: ペットボトル (pettobotoru) = PET plastic bottle.
responses.kanji: はい、ペットボトル用のゴミ箱があります

responses.japanese: かんとびんはべつにわけてください
responses.romaji: Kan to bin wa betsu ni wakete kudasai
responses.english: Please separate cans and glass bottles
responses.listen_for: わけて (分けて, wakete) = separate.
responses.kanji: 缶と瓶は別に分けてください

phrases.kanji: 自販機の横にゴミ箱はありますか？

phrases.japanese: このじはんきでチケットがかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono jihanki de chiketto ga kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I buy a ticket from this vending machine?
phrases.notes: Some restaurants (especially ramen shops) use しょっけんき (食券機, shokkenki) ticket vending machines where you buy a meal ticket before sitting down.

responses.japanese: はい、しょっけんをさきにかってください
responses.romaji: Hai, shokken wo saki ni katte kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please buy a meal ticket first
responses.listen_for: しょっけん (食券, shokken) = meal ticket.
responses.kanji: はい、食券を先に買ってください

responses.japanese: ボタンのしゃしんをみてえらんでください
responses.romaji: Botan no shashin wo mite erande kudasai
responses.english: Please choose by looking at the pictures on the buttons
responses.listen_for: えらんで (選んで, erande) = choose.
responses.kanji: ボタンの写真を見て選んでください

phrases.kanji: この自販機でチケットが買えますか？

phrases.japanese: このじはんきはなんえんからつかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono jihanki wa nan'en kara tsukaemasu ka?
phrases.english: From how much yen can I use this vending machine?
phrases.notes: Useful before putting in a large bill — some older machines only accept coins and small notes.

responses.japanese: せんえんさつからつかえます
responses.english: You can use it starting from 1000 yen bills
responses.listen_for: さつ (札, satsu) = bill/note.
responses.kanji: 千円札から使えます

responses.japanese: こうかのみたいおうです
responses.english: It only accepts coins
responses.listen_for: こうか (硬貨, kouka) = coin.
responses.kanji: 硬貨のみ対応です

phrases.kanji: この自販機は何円から使えますか？

phrases.japanese: これはジュースですか、おちゃですか？
phrases.romaji: Kore wa juusu desu ka, ocha desu ka?
phrases.notes: Good for decoding unfamiliar drink labels quickly when you can't read the kanji.

responses.japanese: それはむとうのおちゃです
responses.romaji: Sore wa mutou no ocha desu
responses.english: That's unsweetened tea
responses.listen_for: むとう (無糖, mutou) = unsweetened/sugar-free.
responses.kanji: それは無糖のお茶です

responses.japanese: それはかじゅうひゃくパーセントのジュースです
responses.romaji: Sore wa kajuu hyaku paasento no juusu desu
responses.english: That's 100% fruit juice
responses.listen_for: かじゅう (果汁, kajuu) = fruit juice content.
responses.kanji: それは果汁100パーセントのジュースです

phrases.kanji: これはジュースですか、お茶ですか？

phrases.japanese: ボタンをおしたのに、でてきません
phrases.english: I pressed the button but nothing came out
phrases.notes: Situation: the machine took your money but no drink dropped. Don't keep pressing. 出てくる (dete kuru) = to come out.

responses.japanese: きかいにかいてあるばんごうにれんらくしてください
responses.romaji: Kikai ni kaite aru bangou ni renraku shite kudasai
responses.english: Please contact the number written on the machine
responses.listen_for: 連絡 (renraku) = contact. 書いてある (kaite aru) = written on. Vending machines post a phone number for problems.
responses.kanji: 機械に書いてある番号に連絡してください

responses.japanese: 返金ボタンをおすと、おかねがもどります
responses.romaji: Henkin botan wo osu to, okane ga modorimasu
responses.english: Press the refund button and your money comes back
responses.listen_for: 返金 (henkin) = refund. もどる (戻る) = to return.
responses.kanji: 返金ボタンを押すと、お金が戻ります

phrases.kanji: ボタンを押したのに、出てきません

phrases.japanese: おつりが、でてきません
phrases.notes: Situation: you inserted more money than the price and no change dropped. Check the change slot first. おつり (お釣り, otsuri) = change.

responses.japanese: おつりのとりだしぐちを、かくにんしてください
responses.romaji: Otsuri no toridashiguchi wo, kakunin shite kudasai
responses.english: Please check the change slot
responses.listen_for: 取り出し口 (toridashiguchi) = pickup slot. Change or drinks come out here.
responses.kanji: お釣りの取り出し口を、確認してください

responses.japanese: でんわばんごうに、おといあわせください
responses.english: Please inquire at the phone number
responses.listen_for: お問い合わせ (otoiawase) = inquiry / contact support.
responses.kanji: 電話番号に、お問い合わせください

phrases.kanji: お釣りが、出てきません

phrases.japanese: カットをおねがいします
phrases.notes: カット (katto) = cut. Ask for シャンプーつき (シャンプー付き, shanpuu-tsuki) if you want a wash included.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、どのようなスタイルにしますか？
responses.romaji: Kashikomarimashita, dono you na sutairu ni shimasu ka?
responses.english: Certainly, what kind of style would you like?
responses.listen_for: スタイル (sutairu) = style.

responses.japanese: シャンプーもごいっしょにいかがですか？
responses.romaji: Shanpuu mo go-issho ni ikaga desu ka?
responses.english: Would you like a shampoo together with that?
responses.listen_for: ごいっしょに (ご一緒に, go-issho ni) = together with.
responses.kanji: シャンプーもご一緒にいかがですか？

phrases.kanji: カットをお願いします

phrases.japanese: すこしだけみじかくしてください
phrases.english: Please cut it just a little shorter
phrases.notes: みじかく (短く, mijikaku) = shorter. Pair with ながく (長く, nagaku) = longer if you need the opposite.

responses.japanese: どれくらいきりましょうか？
responses.english: About how much should I cut?
responses.listen_for: きりましょうか (切りましょうか, kirimashou ka) = shall I cut?
responses.kanji: どれくらい切りましょうか？

responses.japanese: このくらいでいかがですか？
responses.romaji: Kono kurai de ikaga desu ka?
responses.english: How about this much?
responses.listen_for: このくらい (kono kurai) = about this much.

phrases.kanji: 少しだけ短くしてください

phrases.japanese: みじかくしすぎないでください
phrases.english: Please don't cut it too short
phrases.notes: すぎる (過ぎる, sugiru) = to overdo/too much. A crucial phrase to avoid a haircut disaster.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、きをつけますね
responses.english: Certainly, I'll be careful
responses.listen_for: きをつけます (気をつけます, ki wo tsukemasu) = will be careful.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、気をつけますね

responses.japanese: とちゅうでかくにんしながらすすめますね
responses.romaji: Tochuu de kakunin shinagara susumemasu ne
responses.english: I'll check in with you partway through as I go
responses.listen_for: とちゅうで (途中で, tochuu de) = partway/midway.
responses.kanji: 途中で確認しながら進めますね

phrases.kanji: 短くしすぎないでください

phrases.japanese: このしゃしんのようなかみがたにしてください
phrases.romaji: Kono shashin no you na kamigata ni shite kudasai
phrases.english: Please make my hair like this photo
phrases.notes: かみがた (髪型, kamigata) = hairstyle. Showing a reference photo is completely normal and very effective.

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、にせてみますね
responses.english: Certainly, I'll try to match it
responses.listen_for: にせて (似せて, nisete) = make similar/match.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、似せてみますね

responses.japanese: おきゃくさまのかみしつだとすこしちがうかもしれません
responses.romaji: Okyakusama no kamishitsu da to sukoshi chigau kamoshiremasen
responses.english: With your hair texture, it might turn out a bit different
responses.listen_for: かみしつ (髪質, kamishitsu) = hair texture/type.
responses.kanji: お客様の髪質だと少し違うかもしれません

phrases.kanji: この写真のような髪型にしてください

phrases.japanese: まえがみはみじかくしないでください
phrases.english: Please don't cut the bangs short
phrases.notes: まえがみ (前髪, maegami) = bangs/fringe.

responses.japanese: まゆげのうえくらいでよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Mayuge no ue kurai de yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: Is just above the eyebrows okay?
responses.listen_for: まゆげ (眉毛, mayuge) = eyebrows.
responses.kanji: 眉毛の上くらいでよろしいですか？

responses.japanese: かしこまりました、ながめにのこしますね
responses.english: Certainly, I'll leave them on the longer side
responses.listen_for: ながめに (長めに, nagame ni) = on the longer side.
responses.kanji: かしこまりました、長めに残しますね

phrases.kanji: 前髪は短くしないでください

phrases.japanese: カラーもできますか？
phrases.english: Can you also do hair coloring?
phrases.notes: カラー (karaa) = hair color/dye.

responses.japanese: はい、どのいろがごきぼうですか？
responses.romaji: Hai, dono iro ga gokibou desu ka?
responses.english: Yes, which color would you like?
responses.listen_for: ごきぼう (ご希望, gokibou) = your desired/requested.
responses.kanji: はい、どの色がご希望ですか？

responses.japanese: カラーはべつりょうきんになります
responses.romaji: Karaa wa betsu ryoukin ni narimasu
responses.english: Coloring is an additional charge
responses.listen_for: べつりょうきん (別料金, betsu ryoukin) = additional fee.
responses.kanji: カラーは別料金になります

phrases.kanji: カラーもできますか？

phrases.japanese: パーマはどれくらいじかんがかかりますか？
phrases.romaji: Paama wa dorekurai jikan ga kakarimasu ka?
phrases.english: How long does a perm take?
phrases.notes: パーマ (paama) = perm.

responses.japanese: だいたいにじかんほどかかります
responses.english: It takes about two hours
responses.listen_for: だいたい (大体, daitai) = approximately.
responses.kanji: 大体2時間ほどかかります

responses.japanese: かみのながさによってかわります
responses.romaji: Kami no nagasa ni yotte kawarimasu
responses.english: It varies depending on your hair length
responses.listen_for: ながさ (長さ, nagasa) = length.
responses.kanji: 髪の長さによって変わります

phrases.kanji: パーマはどれくらい時間がかかりますか？

phrases.japanese: ひげをそってもらえますか？
phrases.notes: ひげ (髭, hige) = beard/facial hair. Common at traditional とこや (床屋, tokoya) barbershops.

responses.japanese: はい、かみそりでそりますね
responses.english: Yes, I'll shave with a razor
responses.listen_for: かみそり (kamisori) = razor.
responses.kanji: はい、カミソリで剃りますね

responses.japanese: どのながさにととのえますか？
responses.english: What length should I trim it to?
responses.listen_for: ととのえます (整えます, totonoemasu) = trim/shape.
responses.kanji: どの長さに整えますか？

phrases.kanji: 髭を剃ってもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: じかんはどれくらいかかりますか？
phrases.notes: General question for any salon service — useful for planning your day.

responses.japanese: いちじかんほどいただきます
responses.english: It will take about an hour
responses.listen_for: いちじかん (1時間, ichijikan) = one hour.
responses.kanji: 1時間ほどいただきます

responses.japanese: ごよやくのないかたはおまちいただくことがあります
responses.romaji: Goyoyaku no nai kata wa omachi itadaku koto ga arimasu
responses.english: Walk-in guests may need to wait
responses.listen_for: ごよやくのないかた (ご予約のない方, goyoyaku no nai kata) = guests without a reservation.
responses.kanji: ご予約のない方はお待ちいただくことがあります

phrases.kanji: 時間はどれくらいかかりますか？

phrases.japanese: よやくなしでもだいじょうぶですか？
phrases.romaji: Yoyaku nashi demo daijoubu desu ka?
phrases.english: Is it okay without a reservation?
phrases.notes: よやくなし (予約なし, yoyaku nashi) = without a reservation/walk-in.

responses.japanese: はい、ただいまごあんないできます
responses.english: Yes, we can accommodate you right now
responses.listen_for: ごあんない (ご案内, go-annai) = guide/accommodate.
responses.kanji: はい、ただいまご案内できます

responses.japanese: ただいまこんでおりますので、おまちいただきます
responses.romaji: Tadaima konde orimasu node, omachi itadakimasu
responses.english: We're currently busy, so you'll need to wait
responses.listen_for: こんでおります (混んでおります, konde orimasu) = is crowded/busy.
responses.kanji: ただいま混んでおりますので、お待ちいただきます

phrases.kanji: 予約なしでも大丈夫ですか？

phrases.japanese: ビジターでりようできますか？
phrases.english: Can I use this as a day visitor?
phrases.notes: ビジター (bijitaa) = visitor, the common term for a single-day gym pass without membership.

responses.japanese: はい、いちにちビジターりょうきんは〜えんです
responses.romaji: Hai, ichinichi bijitaa ryoukin wa [X] en desu
responses.english: Yes, the one-day visitor fee is [X] yen
responses.listen_for: いちにち (1日, ichinichi) = one day.
responses.kanji: はい、1日ビジター料金は〜円です

responses.japanese: みぶんしょうめいしょがひつようです
responses.english: An ID is required
responses.listen_for: みぶんしょうめいしょ (身分証明書, mibun shoumeisho) = identification document.
responses.kanji: 身分証明書が必要です

phrases.kanji: ビジターで利用できますか？

phrases.japanese: ロッカーはどこですか？
phrases.notes: ロッカー (rokkaa) = locker. Some gyms require a 100-yen coin deposit (returned afterward).

responses.japanese: こういしつのおくにございます
responses.english: They're at the back of the changing room
responses.listen_for: こういしつ (更衣室, kouishitsu) = changing room.
responses.kanji: 更衣室の奥にございます

responses.japanese: ひゃくえんがへんきゃくされるタイプです
responses.romaji: Hyaku en ga henkyaku sareru taipu desu
responses.english: It's the type where the 100 yen is returned
responses.listen_for: へんきゃく (返却, henkyaku) = returned.
responses.kanji: 100円が返却されるタイプです

phrases.kanji: ロッカーはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: タオルはかしだししていますか？
phrases.romaji: Taoru wa kashidashi shite imasu ka?
phrases.notes: かしだし (貸し出し, kashidashi) = rental/lending.

responses.japanese: はい、むりょうでかしだししています
responses.romaji: Hai, muryou de kashidashi shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we lend them for free
responses.listen_for: むりょう (無料, muryou) = free of charge.
responses.kanji: はい、無料で貸し出ししています

responses.japanese: ゆうりょうでレンタルできます
responses.english: You can rent one for a fee
responses.listen_for: ゆうりょう (有料, yuuryou) = paid/fee-based.
responses.kanji: 有料でレンタルできます

phrases.kanji: タオルは貸し出ししていますか？

phrases.japanese: このマシンのつかいかたをおしえてください
phrases.romaji: Kono mashin no tsukaikata wo oshiete kudasai
phrases.english: Please show me how to use this machine
phrases.notes: マシン (mashin) = gym machine/equipment.

responses.japanese: まずシートのたかさをあわせてください
responses.romaji: Mazu shiito no takasa wo awasete kudasai
responses.english: First, adjust the seat height
responses.listen_for: たかさ (高さ, takasa) = height.
responses.kanji: まずシートの高さを合わせてください

responses.japanese: このピンでふかをちょうせいします
responses.romaji: Kono pin de fuka wo chousei shimasu
responses.english: Adjust the weight load with this pin
responses.listen_for: ふか (負荷, fuka) = load/resistance.
responses.kanji: このピンで負荷を調整します

phrases.kanji: このマシンの使い方を教えてください

phrases.japanese: シャワーはついていますか？
phrases.notes: シャワー (shawaa) = shower.

responses.japanese: はい、ろっかーしつのなかにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, rokkaa-shitsu no naka ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, they're inside the locker room
responses.listen_for: ろっかーしつ (ロッカー室, rokkaa-shitsu) = locker room.

responses.japanese: シャンプーとボディソープはごじさんください
responses.romaji: Shanpuu to bodii soopu wa gojisan kudasai
responses.english: Please bring your own shampoo and body soap
responses.listen_for: ごじさん (ご持参, gojisan) = please bring with you.
responses.kanji: シャンプーとボディソープはご持参ください

phrases.kanji: シャワーは付いていますか？

phrases.japanese: グループレッスンにさんかできますか？
phrases.romaji: Guruupu ressun ni sanka dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I join a group lesson/class?
phrases.notes: グループレッスン (guruupu ressun) = group fitness class, e.g. yoga or dance.

responses.japanese: はい、じかんまでにうけつけしてください
responses.romaji: Hai, jikan made ni uketsuke shite kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please check in at the front desk before the time
responses.listen_for: うけつけ (受付, uketsuke) = reception/check-in.
responses.kanji: はい、時間までに受付してください

responses.japanese: よやくがひつようなレッスンもあります
responses.romaji: Yoyaku ga hitsuyou na ressun mo arimasu
responses.english: Some classes require a reservation
responses.listen_for: よやくがひつよう (予約が必要, yoyaku ga hitsuyou) = reservation required.
responses.kanji: 予約が必要なレッスンもあります

phrases.kanji: グループレッスンに参加できますか？

phrases.japanese: たいけんにゅうかいはできますか？
phrases.english: Can I do a trial membership?
phrases.notes: たいけんにゅうかい (体験入会, taiken nyuukai) = trial membership, often free or discounted for the first visit.

responses.japanese: はい、むりょうたいけんができます
responses.english: Yes, you can do a free trial
responses.listen_for: むりょうたいけん (無料体験, muryou taiken) = free trial.
responses.kanji: はい、無料体験ができます

responses.japanese: みぶんしょうめいしょをおもちください
responses.english: Please bring an ID
responses.listen_for: みぶんしょうめいしょ (身分証明書, mibun shoumeisho) = identification document.
responses.kanji: 身分証明書をお持ちください

phrases.kanji: 体験入会はできますか？

phrases.japanese: うんどうぐつをわすれました
phrases.notes: うんどうぐつ (運動靴, undougutsu) = athletic/training shoes.

responses.japanese: レンタルシューズもございます
responses.english: We also have rental shoes
responses.listen_for: レンタルシューズ (rentaru shuuzu) = rental shoes.

responses.japanese: うわばきがあればりようできます
responses.english: If you have indoor shoes, you can use the facility
responses.listen_for: うわばき (上履き, uwabaki) = indoor shoes.
responses.kanji: 上履きがあれば利用できます

phrases.kanji: 運動靴を忘れました

phrases.japanese: このきかいはいまつかってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kikai wa ima tsukatte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I use this equipment now?
phrases.notes: Polite gym-floor etiquette — always confirm before jumping in, especially with shared equipment during busy hours.

responses.japanese: はい、どうぞつかってください
responses.english: Yes, please go ahead and use it
responses.listen_for: どうぞ (douzo) = please go ahead.

responses.japanese: すみません、いまつかっています
responses.english: Sorry, I'm using it right now
responses.listen_for: つかっています (使っています, tsukatte imasu) = currently using.

phrases.kanji: この機械は今使ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: マシンをふくためのタオルはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Mashin wo fuku tame no taoru wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a towel for wiping down the machine?
phrases.notes: Wiping down equipment after use is standard gym etiquette in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、あちらにアルコールスプレーもございます
responses.romaji: Hai, achira ni arukooru supuree mo gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, there's also alcohol spray over there
responses.listen_for: アルコールスプレー (arukooru supuree) = alcohol spray.

responses.japanese: つかったあとはかならずふいてくださいね
responses.romaji: Tsukatta ato wa kanarazu fuite kudasai ne
responses.english: Please always wipe it down after use
responses.listen_for: かならず (必ず, kanarazu) = always/without fail.
responses.kanji: 使った後は必ず拭いてくださいね

phrases.kanji: マシンを拭くためのタオルはありますか？

phrases.japanese: ロッカーが、あきません
phrases.notes: Situation: your locker won't open with your key or code. ロッカー (rokkaa) = locker. あかない (開かない) = won't open.

responses.japanese: こちらで、あけますね
responses.english: I'll open it for you
responses.listen_for: あける (開ける, akeru) = to open. こちらで = here, on our side.
responses.kanji: こちらで、開けますね

responses.japanese: すぐに係の者がまいります
responses.romaji: Sugu ni kakari no mono ga mairimasu
responses.english: A staff member will come right away
responses.listen_for: 係の者 (kakari no mono) = staff member. まいります (参ります) = will come (humble).
responses.kanji: すぐに係の者が参ります

phrases.kanji: ロッカーが、開きません

phrases.japanese: いちにちいくらですか？
phrases.english: How much is a day pass?
phrases.notes: 一日 (ichinichi) = one day. ビジター (bijitaa) = visitor / day pass. 料金 (ryoukin) = fee.

responses.japanese: ビジターはせんごひゃくえんです
responses.english: A day pass is 1,500 yen
responses.listen_for: 円 (en) = yen.

responses.japanese: とうじつのおしはらいになります
responses.english: You pay on the day of your visit
responses.listen_for: 当日 (toujitsu) = the same day.

phrases.japanese: げつかいはいくらですか？
phrases.english: How much is a monthly membership?
phrases.notes: 月会費 (gekkaihi) = monthly fee. 入会金 (nyuukaikin) = sign-up fee.

responses.japanese: げつかいひははっせんえんです
responses.english: The monthly fee is 8,000 yen
responses.listen_for: 月会費 (gekkaihi) = monthly fee.

responses.japanese: にゅうかいきんはべつにかかります
responses.english: There's a separate sign-up fee
responses.listen_for: 別に (betsu ni) = separately.

phrases.japanese: がくせいわりびきはありますか？
phrases.notes: 割引 (waribiki) = discount. 学生 (gakusei) = student.

responses.japanese: はい、がくせいしょうをみせてください
responses.english: Yes, please show your student ID
responses.listen_for: 学生証 (gakuseishou) = student ID card.

responses.japanese: はい、じゅっぱーせんとおやすくなります
responses.english: Yes, it's 10% cheaper
responses.listen_for: パーセント (percent) = %. お安く = cheaper.

phrases.japanese: なにをもっていけばいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Nani wo motte ikeba ii desu ka?
phrases.english: What do I need to bring?
phrases.notes: 持って行く (motte iku) = to bring along.

responses.japanese: みぶんしょうとおかねをもってきてください
responses.romaji: Mibunshou to okane wo motte kite kudasai
responses.english: Please bring ID and money
responses.listen_for: 身分証 (mibunshou) = ID.

responses.japanese: パスポートがあれば、だいじょうぶです
responses.english: If you have your passport, that's fine
responses.listen_for: あれば = if you have.

phrases.japanese: かいいんにならなくても、つかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kaiin ni naranakute mo, tsukaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I use it without becoming a member?
phrases.notes: 会員 (kaiin) = member. 利用 (riyou) = use.

responses.japanese: はい、ビジターでりようできます
responses.english: Yes, you can use it as a visitor
responses.listen_for: 利用 (riyou) = use.

responses.japanese: かいいんのかたのみです
responses.english: It's for members only
responses.listen_for: のみ = only.

phrases.japanese: つかうじかんのきまりはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Tsukau jikan no kimari wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Are there time limits for using the gym?
phrases.notes: 決まり (kimari) = rule. 時間 (jikan) = time.

responses.japanese: はい、いっかいきゅうじゅっぷんまでです
responses.english: Yes, up to 90 minutes per visit
responses.listen_for: 一回 (ikkai) = one time.

responses.japanese: きかいはさんじゅっぷんでかわってください
responses.romaji: Kikai wa sanjuppun de kawatte kudasai
responses.english: Please switch machines after 30 minutes
responses.listen_for: 代わる (kawaru) = to take turns / switch.

phrases.japanese: ロッカーのかぎはどうすればいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Rokkaa no kagi wa dou sureba ii desu ka?
phrases.english: What should I do with the locker key?
phrases.notes: 鍵 (kagi) = key. 返す (kaesu) = to return.

responses.japanese: つかったあと、かえしてください
responses.english: Please return it after you use it
responses.listen_for: 〜あと = after.

responses.japanese: デポジットはさんびゃくえんです
responses.english: The deposit is 300 yen
responses.listen_for: デポジット (deposit) = refundable deposit.

phrases.japanese: くつはぬぐひつようがありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kutsu wa nugu hitsuyou ga arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do I need to take my shoes off?
phrases.notes: 脱ぐ (nugu) = to take off. 必要 (hitsuyou) = necessary.

responses.japanese: トレーニングエリアはぬがなくてもいいです
responses.romaji: Toreeningu eria wa nuganakute mo ii desu
responses.english: In the training area, you don't need to take them off
responses.listen_for: 脱がなくてもいい = don't have to take off.

responses.japanese: はい、ぬいでロッカーにいれてください
responses.romaji: Hai, nuide rokkaa ni irete kudasai
responses.english: Yes, take them off and put them in the locker
responses.listen_for: 入れる (ireru) = to put in.

phrases.japanese: パーソナルトレーニングのよやくはできますか？
phrases.romaji: Paasonaru toreeningu no yoyaku wa dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I book a personal trainer session?
phrases.notes: 予約 (yoyaku) = reservation. パーソナルトレーニング = personal training.

responses.japanese: はい、うけつけでよやくできます
responses.english: Yes, you can book at the front desk
responses.listen_for: 受付 (uketsuke) = front desk.

responses.japanese: いっかいごせんえんからです
responses.english: It starts at 5,000 yen per session
responses.listen_for: 〜から = starting from.

phrases.japanese: レッスンのじかんわりをみせてください
phrases.romaji: Ressun no jikanwari wo misete kudasai
phrases.english: Please show me the class timetable
phrases.notes: 時間割 (jikanwari) = timetable. チラシ (chirashi) = flyer.

responses.japanese: こちらのチラシをどうぞ
responses.english: Here's the flyer
responses.listen_for: チラシ (chirashi) = flyer.

responses.japanese: ウェブサイトでもかくにんできます
responses.english: You can also check it on the website
responses.listen_for: ウェブサイト (website).

phrases.japanese: タトゥーがあっても、はいれますか？
phrases.romaji: Tatuu ga atte mo, hairemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I enter with a tattoo?
phrases.notes: Some gyms and pools in Japan restrict visible tattoos. Ask before you join.

responses.japanese: はい、かくさなくてもだいじょうぶです
responses.english: Yes, you don't need to cover it
responses.listen_for: 隠す (kakusu) = to cover.

responses.japanese: おおきいタトゥーはかくしてください
responses.english: Please cover large tattoos
responses.listen_for: 大きい (ookii) = large.

phrases.japanese: かいいんをやめたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to cancel my membership
phrases.notes: やめる (yameru) = to quit / cancel. 退会 (taikai) = leaving the club.

responses.japanese: たいかいのてつづきはうけつけでできます
responses.romaji: Taikai no tetsuzuki wa uketsuke de dekimasu
responses.english: You can cancel at the front desk
responses.listen_for: 手続き (tetsuzuki) = procedure.

responses.japanese: いっかげつまえにおしらせください
responses.english: Please let us know one month in advance
responses.listen_for: 知らせる (shiraseru) = to inform.

phrases.japanese: しゃしんやどうがをとってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Shashin ya douga wo totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: May I take photos or videos?
phrases.notes: 写真 (shashin) = photo. 動画 (douga) = video.

responses.japanese: ほかのかたがうつらないようにしてください
responses.romaji: Hoka no kata ga utsuranai you ni shite kudasai
responses.english: Please make sure other people aren't in the shot
responses.listen_for: 写る (utsuru) = to be captured in a photo.

responses.japanese: トレーニングエリアはさつえいきんしです
responses.romaji: Toreeningu eria wa satsuei kinshi desu
responses.english: Filming is prohibited in the training area
responses.listen_for: 禁止 (kinshi) = prohibited.

phrases.japanese: ドリンクはもちこみできますか？
phrases.english: Can I bring my own drinks?
phrases.notes: 持ち込み (mochikomi) = bringing in your own items.

responses.japanese: はい、ふたつきのボトルならOKです
responses.romaji: Hai, futatsuki no botoru nara OK desu
responses.english: Yes, bottles with lids are OK
responses.listen_for: ふた付き (futatsuki) = with a lid.

responses.japanese: ほかのかたのめいわくにならないようにしてください
responses.romaji: Hoka no kata no meiwaku ni naranai you ni shite kudasai
responses.english: Please don't bother other people
responses.listen_for: 迷惑 (meiwaku) = trouble / inconvenience.

phrases.japanese: このまんがのさいしんかんはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono manga no saishinkan wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have the latest volume of this manga?
phrases.notes: さいしんかん (最新刊, saishinkan) = the latest volume/issue.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらにございます
responses.english: Yes, it's here
responses.listen_for: こちら (kochira) = here/this way.

responses.japanese: じかいはらいげつはつばいです
responses.english: The next one goes on sale next month
responses.listen_for: はつばい (発売, hatsubai) = release/on sale.
responses.kanji: 次回は来月発売です

phrases.kanji: この漫画の最新刊はありますか？

phrases.japanese: よやくしたフィギュアをうけとりたいです
phrases.romaji: Yoyaku shita figyua wo uketoritai desu
phrases.english: I'd like to pick up the figure I pre-ordered
phrases.notes: フィギュア (figyua) = collectible figure. よやく (予約, yoyaku) = reservation/pre-order.

responses.japanese: よやくばんごうをおしえてください
responses.english: Please tell me your reservation number
responses.listen_for: よやくばんごう (予約番号, yoyaku bangou) = reservation number.
responses.kanji: 予約番号を教えてください

responses.japanese: おなまえをうかがってもよろしいですか？
responses.romaji: Onamae wo ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
responses.english: May I ask your name?
responses.listen_for: おなまえ (お名前, onamae) = name.
responses.kanji: お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか？

phrases.kanji: 予約したフィギュアを受け取りたいです

phrases.japanese: このキャラクターのグッズはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kyarakutaa no guzzu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you have merchandise of this character?
phrases.notes: キャラクター (kyarakutaa) = character. グッズ (guzzu) = merchandise/goods.

responses.japanese: はい、にかいのコーナーにございます
responses.romaji: Hai, nikai no koonaa ni gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, it's in the corner on the second floor
responses.listen_for: にかい (2階, nikai) = second floor.
responses.kanji: はい、2階のコーナーにございます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、げんざいざいこぎれです
responses.english: Sorry, it's currently out of stock
responses.listen_for: ざいこぎれ (在庫切れ, zaiko-gire) = out of stock.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、現在在庫切れです

phrases.kanji: このキャラクターのグッズはありますか？

phrases.japanese: トレーディングカードはどこでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Toreedingu kaado wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I buy trading cards?
phrases.notes: トレーディングカード (toreedingu kaado) = trading cards, e.g. Pokémon or Yu-Gi-Oh!.

responses.japanese: さんがいのカードコーナーでかえます
responses.romaji: San-kai no kaado koonaa de kaemasu
responses.english: You can buy them at the card corner on the 3rd floor
responses.listen_for: さんがい (3階, san-kai) = third floor.
responses.kanji: 3階のカードコーナーで買えます

responses.japanese: ブースターパックとデッキがございます
responses.romaji: Buusutaa pakku to dekki ga gozaimasu
responses.english: We have booster packs and decks
responses.listen_for: ブースターパック (buusutaa pakku) = booster pack.

phrases.kanji: トレーディングカードはどこで買えますか？

phrases.japanese: このカードのそうばはいくらですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono kaado no souba wa ikura desu ka?
phrases.english: What's the market price of this card?
phrases.notes: そうば (相場, souba) = market rate/going price, used for rare collectibles.

responses.japanese: じょうたいによってねだんがかわります
responses.romaji: Joutai ni yotte nedan ga kawarimasu
responses.english: The price changes depending on condition
responses.listen_for: じょうたい (状態, joutai) = condition.
responses.kanji: 状態によって値段が変わります

responses.japanese: かいとりかかくは〜えんです
responses.english: The buyback price is [X] yen
responses.listen_for: かいとりかかく (買取価格, kaitori kakaku) = buyback/purchase price.
responses.kanji: 買取価格は〜円です

phrases.kanji: このカードの相場はいくらですか？

phrases.japanese: このまんがはなんかんまでありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono manga wa nan-kan made arimasu ka?
phrases.english: How many volumes does this manga have so far?
phrases.notes: かん (巻, kan) = volume counter for books/manga.

responses.japanese: げんざいにじゅっかんまではっこうされています
responses.romaji: Genzai nijukkan made hakkou sarete imasu
responses.english: Currently 20 volumes have been published
responses.listen_for: はっこう (発行, hakkou) = publication.
responses.kanji: 現在20巻まで発行されています

responses.japanese: かんぜんにかんけつしています
responses.english: It has completely finished (completed series)
responses.listen_for: かんけつ (完結, kanketsu) = series completion.
responses.kanji: 完全に完結しています

phrases.kanji: この漫画は何巻までありますか？

phrases.japanese: コスプレいしょうをさがしています
phrases.english: I'm looking for a cosplay costume
phrases.notes: コスプレ (kosupure) = cosplay. いしょう (衣装, ishou) = costume.

responses.japanese: どのキャラクターのいしょうをおさがしですか？
responses.romaji: Dono kyarakutaa no ishou wo osagashi desu ka?
responses.english: Which character's costume are you looking for?
responses.listen_for: おさがし (お探し, osagashi) = looking for.
responses.kanji: どのキャラクターの衣装をお探しですか？

responses.japanese: オーダーメイドでもせいさくできます
responses.english: We can also make one custom-order
responses.listen_for: オーダーメイド (oodaa meido) = custom-made/order-made.
responses.kanji: オーダーメイドでも製作できます

phrases.kanji: コスプレ衣装を探しています

phrases.japanese: このさくひんのげんさくはしっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono sakuhin no gensaku wa shitte imasu ka?
phrases.english: Do you know the original work this is based on?
phrases.notes: げんさく (原作, gensaku) = original source material (often a manga or light novel an anime is adapted from).

responses.japanese: げんさくはライトノベルですよ
responses.romaji: Gensaku wa raito noberu desu yo
responses.english: The original is a light novel
responses.listen_for: ライトノベル (raito noberu) = light novel.
responses.kanji: 原作はライトノベルですよ

responses.japanese: アニメがさきで、げんさくはあとからでました
responses.romaji: Anime ga saki de, gensaku wa ato kara demashita
responses.english: The anime came first, the original came out later
responses.listen_for: さきで (先で, saki de) = first/earlier.
responses.kanji: アニメが先で、原作は後から出ました

phrases.kanji: この作品の原作は知っていますか？

phrases.japanese: サインかいのせいりけんはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Sainkai no seiriken wa arimasu ka?
phrases.english: Is there a numbered ticket for the autograph session?
phrases.notes: サイン会 (sainkai) = autograph/fan signing event. せいりけん (整理券, seiriken) = numbered queue ticket, often distributed with a purchase.

responses.japanese: たいしょうしょうひんをこうにゅうするとせいりけんがつきます
responses.romaji: Taishou shouhin wo kounyuu suru to seiriken ga tsukimasu
responses.english: A numbered ticket comes with the purchase of a qualifying item
responses.listen_for: たいしょうしょうひん (対象商品, taishou shouhin) = qualifying/eligible item.
responses.kanji: 対象商品を購入すると整理券が付きます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、せいりけんはくばりおわりました
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen, seiriken wa kubari owarimashita
responses.english: Sorry, the numbered tickets are all handed out
responses.listen_for: くばりおわりました (配り終わりました, kubari owarimashita) = finished handing out.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、整理券は配り終わりました

phrases.kanji: サイン会の整理券はありますか？

phrases.japanese: げんていばんはまだありますか？
phrases.english: Is the limited edition still available?
phrases.notes: げんていばん (限定版, genteiban) = limited edition version.

responses.japanese: はい、のこりわずかございます
responses.english: Yes, there are only a few left
responses.listen_for: のこりわずか (残りわずか, nokori wazuka) = very few remaining.
responses.kanji: はい、残りわずかございます

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、かんばいいたしました
responses.english: I'm sorry, it's sold out
responses.listen_for: かんばい (完売, kanbai) = sold out.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、完売いたしました

phrases.kanji: 限定版はまだありますか？

phrases.japanese: このおにぎりのぐはなんですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono onigiri no gu wa nan desu ka?
phrases.english: What's the filling of this onigiri?
phrases.notes: ぐ (具, gu) = filling/ingredients. Common fillings: うめ (梅, ume) / pickled plum, しゃけ (鮭, shake) / salmon, ツナマヨ (tsuna mayo) / tuna mayo, こんぶ (昆布, konbu) / kelp.

responses.japanese: これはしゃけのおにぎりです
responses.romaji: Kore wa shake no onigiri desu
responses.english: This is a salmon onigiri
responses.listen_for: しゃけ (鮭, shake) = salmon.
responses.kanji: これは鮭のおにぎりです

responses.japanese: からいのがにがてならうめはさけてください
responses.romaji: Karai no ga nigate nara ume wa sakete kudasai
responses.english: If you don't like spicy/sour things, avoid the pickled plum
responses.listen_for: にがて (苦手, nigate) = not good with/dislike.
responses.kanji: 辛いのが苦手なら梅は避けてください

phrases.kanji: このおにぎりの具は何ですか？

phrases.japanese: このおべんとうはれいとうですか、れいぞうですか？
phrases.romaji: Kono obentou wa reitou desu ka, reizou desu ka?
phrases.english: Is this bento frozen or refrigerated?
phrases.notes: れいとう (冷凍, reitou) = frozen. れいぞう (冷蔵, reizou) = refrigerated/chilled.

responses.japanese: れいぞうですので、すぐにたべられます
responses.romaji: Reizou desu node, sugu ni taberaremasu
responses.english: It's chilled, so you can eat it right away
responses.listen_for: れいぞう (冷蔵, reizou) = refrigerated.
responses.kanji: 冷蔵ですので、すぐに食べられます

responses.japanese: れいとうなので、かいとうがひつようです
responses.romaji: Reitou nanode, kaitou ga hitsuyou desu
responses.english: It's frozen, so it needs to be thawed
responses.listen_for: かいとう (解凍, kaitou) = thawing.
responses.kanji: 冷凍なので、解凍が必要です

phrases.kanji: このお弁当は冷凍ですか、冷蔵ですか？

phrases.japanese: からあげのあじはなんしゅるいありますか？
phrases.romaji: Karaage no aji wa nan-shurui arimasu ka?
phrases.english: How many flavors of fried chicken are there?
phrases.notes: からあげ (唐揚げ, karaage) = Japanese fried chicken, a konbini hot-food staple with seasonal flavor variations.

responses.japanese: ふつうあじとからいあじのにしゅるいです
responses.romaji: Futsuu aji to karai aji no nishurui desu
responses.english: There are two flavors: regular and spicy
responses.listen_for: にしゅるい (2種類, nishurui) = two kinds/types.
responses.kanji: 普通味と辛い味の2種類です

responses.japanese: きせつげんていのあじもあります
responses.romaji: Kisetsu gentei no aji mo arimasu
responses.english: There's also a seasonal limited flavor
responses.listen_for: きせつげんてい (季節限定, kisetsu gentei) = seasonal limited.
responses.kanji: 季節限定の味もあります

phrases.kanji: 唐揚げの味は何種類ありますか？

phrases.japanese: このにくまんはいつできましたか？
phrases.romaji: Kono nikuman wa itsu dekimashita ka?
phrases.english: When was this meat bun made?
phrases.notes: にくまん (肉まん, nikuman) = steamed meat bun, a winter konbini classic kept warm in a heated case (ホットショーケース).

responses.japanese: すうじかんまえにつくりました
responses.english: It was made a few hours ago
responses.listen_for: すうじかんまえ (数時間前, suujikan mae) = a few hours ago.
responses.kanji: 数時間前に作りました

responses.japanese: じょうじほかんですので、いつでもあたたかいです
responses.romaji: Jouji hokan desu node, itsudemo atatakai desu
responses.english: It's kept warm at all times, so it's always hot
responses.listen_for: じょうじ (常時, jouji) = at all times.
responses.kanji: 常時保管ですので、いつでも温かいです

phrases.kanji: この肉まんはいつできましたか？

phrases.japanese: スイーツのコーナーはどこですか？
phrases.romaji: Suiitsu no koonaa wa doko desu ka?
phrases.notes: スイーツ (suiitsu) = sweets/desserts. Konbini sweets (プリン/purin pudding, シュークリーム/shuu kuriimu cream puffs) have a cult following.

responses.japanese: れいぞうこのみぎがわにございます
responses.english: It's on the right side of the refrigerator
responses.listen_for: れいぞうこ (冷蔵庫, reizouko) = refrigerator.
responses.kanji: 冷蔵庫の右側にございます

responses.japanese: しんさくのスイーツがにんきです
responses.romaji: Shinsaku no suiitsu ga ninki desu
responses.english: The new sweets release is popular
responses.listen_for: しんさく (新作, shinsaku) = new release.
responses.kanji: 新作のスイーツが人気です

phrases.kanji: スイーツのコーナーはどこですか？

phrases.japanese: このおでんのぐをえらべますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono oden no gu wo erabemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I choose the oden ingredients?
phrases.notes: おでん (oden) = winter hot-pot dish simmered in dashi broth, often self-serve or staff-served from a heated case at konbini.

responses.japanese: はい、おすきなものをおえらびください
responses.romaji: Hai, osuki na mono wo oerabi kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please choose whatever you like
responses.listen_for: おすきなもの (お好きなもの, osuki na mono) = whatever you like.
responses.kanji: はい、お好きなものをお選びください

responses.japanese: ふくろにいれてごじさんできます
responses.english: I can put it in a bag for you to take with you
responses.listen_for: ごじさん (ご持参, gojisan) = taking it with you.
responses.kanji: 袋に入れてご持参できます

phrases.kanji: このおでんの具を選べますか？

phrases.japanese: このサンドイッチはなにがはいっていますか？
phrases.romaji: Kono sandoitchi wa nani ga haitte imasu ka?
phrases.notes: サンドイッチ (sandoitchi) = sandwich. たまごサンド (tamago sando) / egg sandwich is a konbini classic.

responses.japanese: たまごとレタスがはいっています
responses.romaji: Tamago to retasu ga haitte imasu
responses.english: It has egg and lettuce
responses.listen_for: レタス (retasu) = lettuce.
responses.kanji: 卵とレタスが入っています

responses.japanese: ハムとチーズのサンドイッチです
responses.romaji: Hamu to chiizu no sandoitchi desu
responses.english: It's a ham and cheese sandwich
responses.listen_for: ハム (hamu) = ham.

phrases.kanji: このサンドイッチは何が入っていますか？

phrases.japanese: このドリンクはあたためられますか？
phrases.english: Can this drink be heated up?
phrases.notes: Many canned coffees and teas can be warmed at the register, same as hot food.

responses.japanese: はい、あたためますね
responses.english: Yes, I'll warm it up for you
responses.listen_for: あたためます (温めます, atatamemasu) = will warm up.
responses.kanji: はい、温めますね

responses.japanese: もうしわけありません、これはあたためられません
responses.english: Sorry, this one can't be heated
responses.listen_for: あたためられません (温められません, atatameraremasen) = cannot be heated.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありません、これは温められません

phrases.kanji: このドリンクは温められますか？

phrases.japanese: きせつげんていのしょうひんはありますか？
phrases.romaji: Kisetsu gentei no shouhin wa arimasu ka?
phrases.notes: きせつげんてい (季節限定, kisetsu gentei) = seasonal limited — konbini chains rotate flavors constantly (sakura in spring, momo in summer, etc.).

responses.japanese: はい、いまはさくらあじがございます
responses.romaji: Hai, ima wa sakura aji ga gozaimasu
responses.english: Yes, right now we have a sakura flavor
responses.listen_for: さくらあじ (桜味, sakura aji) = sakura/cherry blossom flavor.
responses.kanji: はい、今は桜味がございます

responses.japanese: らいげつあたらしいしょうひんがでます
responses.english: New products come out next month
responses.listen_for: らいげつ (来月, raigetsu) = next month.
responses.kanji: 来月新しい商品が出ます

phrases.kanji: 季節限定の商品はありますか？

phrases.japanese: カップめんにおゆはどこでもらえますか？
phrases.romaji: Kappumen ni oyu wa doko de moraemasu ka?
phrases.english: Where can I get hot water for instant noodles?
phrases.notes: カップめん (カップ麺, kappumen) = cup noodles. Many konbini have a free hot water dispenser (きゅうとうき, 給湯器) near the register.

responses.japanese: レジのよこのきゅうとうきをおつかいください
responses.romaji: Reji no yoko no kyuutouki wo otsukai kudasai
responses.english: Please use the hot water dispenser next to the register
responses.listen_for: きゅうとうき (給湯器, kyuutouki) = hot water dispenser.
responses.kanji: レジの横の給湯器をお使いください

responses.japanese: さんぷんかんおまちくださいね
responses.english: Please wait 3 minutes
responses.listen_for: さんぷんかん (3分間, sanpun-kan) = for 3 minutes.
responses.kanji: 3分間お待ちくださいね

phrases.kanji: カップ麺にお湯はどこでもらえますか？

phrases.japanese: ATMはどこですか？
phrases.notes: Many konbini ATMs (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) accept foreign-issued cards — look for the 英語 (eigo) / English button on the screen.

responses.japanese: レジのよこにございます
responses.english: It's next to the register
responses.listen_for: よこ (横, yoko) = next to/beside.
responses.kanji: レジの横にございます

responses.japanese: てんないのおくにございます
responses.english: It's at the back of the store
responses.listen_for: おく (奥, oku) = inner part/back.
responses.kanji: 店内の奥にございます

phrases.japanese: げんきんをひきだしたいです
phrases.notes: げんきん (現金, genkin) = cash. ひきだす (引き出す, hikidasu) = to withdraw.

responses.japanese: カードをそうにゅうしてください
responses.english: Please insert your card
responses.listen_for: そうにゅう (挿入, sounyuu) = insert.
responses.kanji: カードを挿入してください

responses.japanese: えいごのがめんにきりかえられます
responses.english: You can switch to the English screen
responses.listen_for: きりかえ (切り替え, kirikae) = switch over.
responses.kanji: 英語の画面に切り替えられます

phrases.kanji: 現金を引き出したいです

phrases.japanese: こうきょうりょうきんをはらいたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to pay a utility bill
phrases.notes: こうきょうりょうきん (公共料金, koukyou ryoukin) = utility bills (electricity, gas, water) — commonly paid at konbini registers with a printed barcode slip.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらのバーコードをスキャンします
responses.romaji: Hai, kochira no baakoodo wo sukyan shimasu
responses.english: Yes, I'll scan this barcode
responses.listen_for: バーコード (baakoodo) = barcode.

responses.japanese: げんきんのみのおしはらいとなります
responses.romaji: Genkin nomi no oshiharai to narimasu
responses.english: Payment is cash only
responses.listen_for: げんきんのみ (現金のみ, genkin nomi) = cash only.
responses.kanji: 現金のみのお支払いとなります

phrases.kanji: 公共料金を払いたいです

phrases.japanese: コピーきはどこですか？
phrases.notes: コピーき (コピー機, kopiiki) = photocopier, usually a multifunction machine that also prints and scans.

responses.japanese: まどのちかくにございます
responses.english: It's near the window
responses.listen_for: まど (窓, mado) = window.
responses.kanji: 窓の近くにございます

responses.japanese: はくろコピーですか、カラーコピーですか？
responses.romaji: Hakuro kopii desu ka, karaa kopii desu ka?
responses.english: Black and white or color copy?
responses.listen_for: はくろ (白黒, hakuro) = black and white.
responses.kanji: 白黒コピーですか、カラーコピーですか？

phrases.kanji: コピー機はどこですか？

phrases.japanese: スマホのデータをいんさつできますか？
phrases.romaji: Sumaho no deeta wo insatsu dekimasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I print data from my phone?
phrases.notes: Konbini multifunction printers support printing via a dedicated app or by uploading a file and entering a code.

responses.japanese: はい、せんようアプリからそうしんできます
responses.romaji: Hai, senyou apuri kara soushin dekimasu
responses.english: Yes, you can send it via the dedicated app
responses.listen_for: せんようアプリ (専用アプリ, senyou apuri) = dedicated app.
responses.kanji: はい、専用アプリから送信できます

responses.japanese: QRコードをよみとってください
responses.english: Please scan the QR code
responses.listen_for: よみとって (読み取って, yomitotte) = scan/read.
responses.kanji: QRコードを読み取ってください

phrases.kanji: スマホのデータを印刷できますか？

phrases.japanese: にもつをはっそうしたいです
phrases.english: I'd like to ship a package
phrases.notes: Many konbini accept たっきゅうびん (宅急便, takkyuubin) parcel drop-offs for courier services like ヤマト運輸.

responses.japanese: でんぴょうにごじゅうしょをごきにゅうください
responses.romaji: Denpyou ni gojuusho wo gokinyuu kudasai
responses.english: Please fill in the address on this slip
responses.listen_for: でんぴょう (伝票, denpyou) = shipping slip/invoice.
responses.kanji: 伝票にご住所をご記入ください

responses.japanese: サイズとじゅうりょうをはかります
responses.english: I'll measure the size and weight
responses.listen_for: じゅうりょう (重量, juuryou) = weight.
responses.kanji: サイズと重量を測ります

phrases.kanji: 荷物を発送したいです

phrases.japanese: きってはうっていますか？
phrases.notes: きって (切手, kitte) = postage stamp — most konbini sell common denominations.

responses.japanese: はい、レジではんばいしています
responses.romaji: Hai, reji de hanbai shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, we sell them at the register
responses.listen_for: はんばい (販売, hanbai) = sell/sale.
responses.kanji: はい、レジで販売しています

responses.japanese: なんまいひつようですか？
responses.english: How many do you need?
responses.listen_for: まい (枚, mai) counts flat thin objects like stamps.
responses.kanji: 何枚必要ですか？

phrases.kanji: 切手は売っていますか？

phrases.japanese: がいこくのカードもつかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Gaikoku no kaado mo tsukaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I use a foreign card too?
phrases.notes: Most 7-Eleven ATMs reliably accept foreign Visa/Mastercard/UnionPay debit and credit cards — a lifesaver when other ATMs don't.

responses.japanese: はい、かいがいはっこうのカードもたいおうしています
responses.romaji: Hai, kaigai hakkou no kaado mo taiou shite imasu
responses.english: Yes, cards issued overseas are also supported
responses.listen_for: はっこう (発行, hakkou) = issued.
responses.kanji: はい、海外発行のカードも対応しています

responses.japanese: てすうりょうがかかるばあいがあります
responses.romaji: Tesuuryou ga kakaru baai ga arimasu
responses.english: There may be a handling fee
responses.listen_for: てすうりょう (手数料, tesuuryou) = handling fee.
responses.kanji: 手数料がかかる場合があります

phrases.kanji: 外国のカードも使えますか？

phrases.japanese: チケットをこのきかいでかえますか？
phrases.romaji: Chiketto wo kono kikai de kaemasu ka?
phrases.english: Can I buy tickets at this machine?
phrases.notes: Konbini ticket terminals (Loppi/FamiPort) sell concert, event, and even some transport tickets — look for the touchscreen kiosk near the entrance.

responses.japanese: はい、がめんのしじにしたがってそうさしてください
responses.romaji: Hai, gamen no shiji ni shitagatte sousa shite kudasai
responses.english: Yes, please follow the on-screen instructions
responses.listen_for: しじ (指示, shiji) = instructions.
responses.kanji: はい、画面の指示に従って操作してください

responses.japanese: はっけんされたばんごうをレジへおもちください
responses.romaji: Hakken sareta bangou wo reji e omochi kudasai
responses.english: Please bring the printed number to the register
responses.listen_for: はっけん (発券, hakken) = ticket issuance.
responses.kanji: 発券された番号をレジへお持ちください

phrases.kanji: チケットはこの機械で買えますか？

phrases.japanese: ごみをすてたいのですが
phrases.romaji: Gomi wo sutetai no desu ga
phrases.english: I'd like to throw away some trash
phrases.notes: Most konbini only accept trash from items purchased there — ask first, since public trash cans are rare in Japan.

responses.japanese: はい、こちらのごみばこへどうぞ
responses.romaji: Hai, kochira no gomibako e douzo
responses.english: Yes, please use this trash bin
responses.listen_for: ごみばこ (ゴミ箱, gomibako) = trash bin.

responses.japanese: もうしわけありませんが、てんないのごみのみです
responses.romaji: Moushiwake arimasen ga, tennai no gomi nomi desu
responses.english: Sorry, only trash from items bought here
responses.listen_for: のみ (nomi) = only.
responses.kanji: 申し訳ありませんが、店内のごみのみです

phrases.kanji: ごみを捨てたいのですが

phrases.japanese: ラインこうかんしてもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Rain koukan shite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.notes: LINE is Japan's dominant messaging app — exchanging it is the standard way to stay in touch, more common than exchanging phone numbers.

responses.japanese: はい、もちろんです
responses.english: Yes, of course
responses.listen_for: もちろん (mochiron) = of course.

responses.japanese: QRコードをみせますね
responses.english: I'll show you my QR code
responses.listen_for: QRコード (QR koodo) = QR code.

phrases.kanji: LINE交換してもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: いっしょにしゃしんをとってもいいですか？
phrases.romaji: Issho ni shashin wo totte mo ii desu ka?
phrases.english: Can we take a photo together?
phrases.notes: Different from asking someone else to take your photo — this is asking to be in a photo together.

responses.japanese: はい、もちろんいいですよ
responses.english: Yes, of course that's fine
responses.listen_for: もちろん (mochiron) = of course.

responses.japanese: ちょっとはずかしいですが、いいですよ
responses.romaji: Chotto hazukashii desu ga, ii desu yo
responses.english: It's a bit embarrassing, but okay
responses.listen_for: はずかしい (恥ずかしい, hazukashii) = embarrassing/shy.
responses.kanji: ちょっと恥ずかしいですが、いいですよ

phrases.kanji: 一緒に写真を撮ってもいいですか？

phrases.japanese: またこんどいっしょにあそびましょう
phrases.english: Let's hang out together again sometime
phrases.notes: あそぶ (遊ぶ, asobu) = to hang out/play — used broadly for socializing, not just children's play.

responses.japanese: ぜひ、たのしみにしています
responses.english: Definitely, I'm looking forward to it
responses.listen_for: たのしみにしています (楽しみにしています, tanoshimi ni shite imasu) = looking forward to it.
responses.kanji: ぜひ、楽しみにしています

responses.japanese: れんらくまちしていますね
responses.english: I'll be waiting to hear from you
responses.listen_for: れんらく (連絡, renraku) = contact/message.
responses.kanji: 連絡待ちしていますね

phrases.kanji: また今度一緒に遊びましょう
